When merging projects you can reuse resources and nodes you created in another project. Merging projects allows you to import a complete project or only selected resources and nodes. During merging Kanzi provides conflict resolution.
Kanzi provides these options for bringing content from other projects:
  * You can bring an entire project to the current project. See [Importing projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/importing-projects.html).
  * You can merge 3D assets from a 3D asset file. See [Merging 3D assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/3d-assets/merging-3d-assets.html).
  * You can bring to the current project only a part of another project. See [Merging content from referenced Kanzi Studio projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/using-assets-from-another-project.html#merging-content-from-referenced-kanzi-studio-projects).
  * You can share individual project items. See [Sharing project items](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/sharing-project-items.html).
  * If you want to import collections of ready-made content, use Kanzi Studio asset packages.
See [Asset packages](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-packages/asset-packages.html).
  * If you want to import the assets that you created with third-party tools, use Kanzi Studio importing tools. See [Importing](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing.html).


## Merging Kanzi Studio projects[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html#merging-ks-projects "Link to this heading")
To merge projects:
  1. Select File > Import > Merge Project, select the project you want to merge (source project) to the currently open project (target project), and click Open.
The Project Merge dialog opens.
![../../_images/merge-project-menu-option.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/merge-project-menu-option.png)
  2. In the Project Merge dialog set:
     * Select referenced items. Select the checkbox when you want Kanzi Studio to automatically select all items to which the selected item refers.
For example, when you check the Select referenced items checkbox and select a mesh that has a material, Kanzi Studio studio automatically selects the material, material type, and shaders used by the mesh you selected.
     * **Transformations**. If Kanzi Studio encounters a conflict in object transformations when an object in the target is replaced with an object from the source, set Keep transformations from to:
       * Target Project: <ProjectName> to keep the object transformations you use in the target. Kanzi Studio remembers all transformation changes you made to the objects in Kanzi Studio.
       * Source Project: <ProjectName> to import the object transformations you use in the source.
![../../_images/merging-keep-transformations-from.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/merging-keep-transformations-from.png)
     * **Materials**. If Kanzi Studio encounters a conflict in object materials when an object in the target is replaced with an object from the source, set Keep materials from to:
       * Target Project: <ProjectName> to keep the materials you use for the objects in the target. Kanzi Studio remembers all material changes you made to the objects in Kanzi Studio.
       * Source Project: <ProjectName> to import the materials you use for the objects in the source.
![../../_images/merging-keep-materials-from.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/merging-keep-materials-from.png)
  3. Select the checkboxes next to the items you want to merge from the source to target. Depending on the existence of the selected item in the target project, the name of the item is written using:
     * **White** font. Items exist in the source, but not in the target. When you select such items, Kanzi Studio creates them in the target.
     * **Red** font. Items exist in both the source and target, but differ between the two.
Before you can continue with the merging, you have to resolve conflicts by choosing to use either the item in the target or the source.
     * **Purple** font. Items exist in the target, but not in the source. When you select such items, Kanzi Studio removes them from the target.
  4. If you are merging projects with data sources that use locally stored data, see [Merging projects with data sources that use locally stored data](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html#merging2).
  5. If you are merging projects that contain Kanzi Engine Plugins, see [Merging projects with Kanzi Engine plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html#merging).
  6. Resolve conflicts. When your target and source both contain the same item and properties of this item differ, you have to decide which properties you want to keep:
     * Click Resolve to source to use the values in the source to resolve all conflicts.
     * Click Resolve to target to use the values in the target to resolve all conflicts.
     * Click Use base project to select a base project for resolving conflicts between the target and the source. For example, Use base project is useful when you are merging two projects or assets that are modifications of an initial project.
When using three-way merge, this is how conflict resolution works in Kanzi Studio:
       * If the difference is only between the base project and the target, Kanzi Studio uses the change in the target.
       * If the difference is only between the base project and the source, Kanzi Studio uses the change in the source.
       * If the change is between both the base project and the target, and the source and the target, you have to resolve the conflict.
     * To resolve conflicts manually, select the item in the source tree and in the conflicts pane select for each property whether you want to keep the value used in the target or the source.
       * You can select several properties and click Resolve to Target to keep the values used in the target or Resolve to Source to keep the values used in the source.
![../../_images/merging-manually-resolve-to-target.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/merging-manually-resolve-to-target.png)
       * You can select a single value you want to keep from the Target or Source column.
![../../_images/merging-manually-resolve-to-source.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/merging-manually-resolve-to-source.png)
Once you have resolved all the conflicts, the font color of the item name in the source tree changes to green.
  7. Click Merge. Kanzi Studio merges the source with the target by placing the content of source into the corresponding places of the target.


## Merging projects with Kanzi Engine plugins[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html#merging-projects-with-kr-plugins "Link to this heading")
When you merge projects with Kanzi Engine plugins that have the same name, but different component types, data sources, messages, or property types, you cannot resolve the conflict in the Project Merge tool.
![../../_images/kanzi-engine-plugin-merge-conflict.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/kanzi-engine-plugin-merge-conflict.png)
To merge projects with conflicting Kanzi Engine plugins:
  1. In Kanzi Studio open the project which does not use the correct version of the Kanzi Engine plugin.
  2. In the Library > Kanzi Engine Plugins right-click the plugin and select Update Kanzi Engine Plugin.
![../../_images/update-plugin-metadata.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/update-plugin-metadata.png)
  3. Merge the Kanzi Studio projects. See [Merging Kanzi Studio projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html#merging-kanzi-studio-projects).


## Merging projects with data sources that use locally stored data[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html#merging-projects-with-data-sources-that-use-locally-stored-data "Link to this heading")
Typically the data in a data source you merge to a Kanzi Studio project is provided by a server to which your application connects. If, however, the source files of the data source you want to merge are stored locally in the source project, you must manually copy them from `<SourceProjectName>/Application/bin` to `<TargetProjectName>/Application/bin`. If you do not copy the data files to the target project, the Preview fails to start.
## Responding to kzm file changes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html#responding-to-kzm-file-changes "Link to this heading")
When Kanzi Studio detects that kzm files in the project directory changed outside of Kanzi Studio, for example, after a `git pull` or a file copy from another project, it shows a **Project modified** notification dialogue with these options:
  * Reload — reloads the project from disk. If you have unsaved local changes, reloading discards them.
  * Merge — opens the Project Merge dialog so you can selectively merge the on-disk changes into your local version. This option is only available when you have unsaved local changes.
  * Ignore — keeps your current project state and discards the on-disk changes.


Kanzi Studio monitors all files with `.kzm` extensions in the project directory and its subdirectories.
## Merging projects using version control tools[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html#merging-projects-using-version-control-tools "Link to this heading")
After configuring your version control tool you can use the Kanzi merge tool for Kanzi project updating and merging. For the integration Kanzi requires a version control tool that provides the necessary parameters to the Kanzi merge tool.  
| Example of parameter types  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| MINE  | The parameter for the source project.  |  
| THEIRS  | The parameter for the target project.  |  
| BASE  | The parameter for the base project.  |  
| MERGED  | The parameter for the merged project.  |  
## Integrating the Kanzi merge tool with a version control tool[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html#integrating-the-k-merge-tool-with-a-version-control-tool "Link to this heading")
To integrate the Kanzi merge tool with a version control tool:
  1. Configure your version control tool to use the Kanzi merge tool (`<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/KanziMergeTool.bat`) for .kzproj files.
  2. Pass to your version control tool the absolute path to the `KanziStudio.exe`. For example, `C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi\Studio\Bin\KanziStudio.exe`.
  3. Set the version control tool parameters for the Kanzi merge tool. For example, these parameters can be called MINE, THEIRS, BASE, MERGED.


## Integrating the Kanzi merge tool with SVN version control software[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html#integrating-the-k-merge-tool-with-svn-version-control-software "Link to this heading")
To integrate the Kanzi merge tool with SVN version control software, add Kanzi merge tool as an external program for merging files with the .kzproj extension.
For example, if you are using Tortoise SVN, in TortoiseSVN select SVN > Settings > External Programs > Merge Tool > Advanced and set:
  * Filename, extension or mime-type to .kzproj
  * External program to

```
<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/KanziMergeTool.bat "<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/KanziStudio.exe"  %mine %theirs %base %merged

```
Copy to clipboard
For example, if your installation of Kanzi is in `C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi`, use

```
C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi\Studio\Bin\KanziMergeTool.bat "C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi\Studio\Bin\KanziStudio.exe" %mine %theirs %base %merged

```
Copy to clipboard


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Importing projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/importing-projects.html)
[Merging 3D assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/3d-assets/merging-3d-assets.html)
[Asset packages](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-packages/asset-packages.html)
[Projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/projects.html)
[Using version control systems with Kanzi](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html)

# Asset Toolkit[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#asset-toolkit "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
The Asset Toolkit contains easy, ready-made components and materials with a similar structure and set of properties, that you can use to create Kanzi applications faster.
Here you can find all the Asset Toolkit content:
  * A high quality placeholder car model that you can use in your prototype application. See [Car](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#car).
  * Materials that you can apply to 3D content in your project. See [Materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#materials).
  * Environment Textures that you can use to give perspective to your scene. See [Environments](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#environments).
  * Flipbook and Transition Material types that you can use to present content in your application. See [Material types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#material-types).
  * Interactive User Interface Components that you can use to receive user input. See [Interactivity Control components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#interactivity-control-components).
  * Radial UI Components that you can show progress in a circular arc. See [Radial UI Components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#radial-ui-components).
  * Simple shapes to use in your application. See [Simple Shape UI Components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#simple-shape-ui-components).
  * Scrollable lists that can present collections of items. See [Scroll list UI Components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#scroll-list-ui-components).
  * Example components that shows ways to combine these assets into more complex, reusable components. See [Examples](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#examples).


To use the Asset Toolkit assets in your Kanzi Studio project, from the Asset Packages drag an asset to a node in the Node Tree, to the Prefabs, or to the Preview. See [Using the Asset Toolkit assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html).
![../../_images/asset-packages-asset-toolkit-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-asset-toolkit-selected.png)
## Car[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#car "Link to this heading")
Use the Car to add a car model into your scene.
![../../_images/car-asset1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-asset1.png)
To position the car, in the Preview use either the Node tool or the Camera tool. See [Editing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html) and [Using the Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html).
To set the material for the different parts of the car, you can drag materials from the Assets window to the Car in the Preview window, or on the part of the car in the Node Tree. See [Using the Asset Toolkit assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html).
## Materials[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#materials "Link to this heading")
The Asset Toolkit includes Physically Based Rendering (PBR) materials that you can apply to 3D content in your project.
![../../_images/carpaint-blue.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/carpaint-blue.png)
PBR Carpaint-blue
![../../_images/carpaint-orange.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/carpaint-orange.png)
PBR Carpaint-orange
![../../_images/chrome.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/chrome.png)
PBR Chrome
![../../_images/glass.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/glass.png)
PBR Glass
![../../_images/plastic.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/plastic.png)
PBR Plastic
To learn about using materials from the Asset Toolkit in your Kanzi application, see [Using Asset Toolkit materials in your project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html#using-at-materials).
## Environments[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#environments "Link to this heading")
The Asset Toolkit includes two environment textures which are also included in the car and PBR materials, but provided independently for use with your own materials or models.
  * Use Environment Studio Irradiance to provide diffused ambient lighting to materials in your scene, as is done with glass and plastics in the assets.


![../../_images/environment-irradiance.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/environment-irradiance.png)
Environment Studio Irradiance
  * Use Environment Studio Specular to provide a sharp, smooth reflective surface to materials in your scene, as is done with metals and paint in the assets.


![../../_images/environment-specular.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/environment-specular.png)
Environment Studio Specular
To use an environment texture in your project, from the Assets window right-click and import, and apply to your materials by setting it as the Ambient and/or Reflection texture in the material properties. Control its strength by adjusting the Factor slider.
![../../_images/set-environment-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-environment-texture.png)
To learn more about environment textures, see [Using environment textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html).
## Material types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#material-types "Link to this heading")
The Asset Toolkit includes two Material Types that can be used to animate display of content in your application:
  * The Flipbook Material Type allows you to use a texture atlas that contains multiple images arranged in a grid layout. Use it to selectively display images from that texture atlas, or to play out an animated sequence. This is useful for example, to set the state of navigation arrow in a cluster, or to animate a simple pedestrian figure walking.
![../../_images/flipbook.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flipbook.png)
Flipbook Material Type
To use the Flipbook Material Type in your project:
    * Right-click to import or drag it into your preview or node tree.
    * Apply it as a brush to 2D or 3D nodes in your scene.
    * In the Flipbook Material Type properties window, set the grid to correspond to the layout of the images in the texture atlas.
![../../_images/flipbook-configuration.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flipbook-configuration.png)
    * Set the static image to display by setting the Static Image Index property.
![../../_images/static-image-index.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/static-image-index.png)
    * Play out an animated flipbook sequence by advancing the Time property value.
![../../_images/time-sequence.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/time-sequence.png)
To learn about using tile atlases, see [Using a tile atlas](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-tile-atlases.html).
  * The Transition Material Type allows you to transition between nodes in either a Fade, Sweep or Noise motion.
![../../_images/transition.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/transition.png)
Transition Material Type
To use the Transition Material Type in your project:
    * Right-click to import or drag it into your preview or node tree.
    * Apply it as a brush to 2D or 3D nodes in your scene.
    * In the Transition Material Type properties window,
      * Set the Transition Type to apply to the transition.
      * Select textures between which to transition as the Transition Texture Start and Transition Texture End properties.
![../../_images/transition-textures.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/transition-textures.png)
    * To apply a Fade transition, set the Transition type property to Fade.
      * Control the progression of the fade by advancing the Transition Progress property value.
![../../_images/fade-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fade-properties.png)
    * To apply a Sweep transition, set the Transition type property to Sweep.
      * Control the smoothing intensity by setting the Transition Smoothing property
      * Set orientation of the sweep motion using the Transition Rotation property.
![../../_images/sweep-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/sweep-properties.png)
    * To apply a Noise transition, set the Transition type property to Noise.
      * Additionally, control the granularity of the noise by setting the Transition Noise Scale property.
![../../_images/noise-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/noise-properties.png)


## Interactivity Control components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#interactivity-control-components "Link to this heading")
Use the UI Components provided in the Asset Toolkit to receive user input, and provide an interactive user experience in your application.
![../../_images/interactivity-ui-components.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/interactivity-ui-components.png)
The interactive UI components included in the Asset Toolkit all share a set of similar properties and behaviors, exposed and named the same way. This makes it easier to apply consistent styling, and to combine them in your project.
When you import a UI component, Kanzi Studio adds to your project Library and Prefabs, the required shaders and materials to render that component.
It uses the FillStrokeBrush material, applied as BackgroundBrush to all the UI components, to expose properties that control their appearance and behavior.
![../../_images/fillstrokebrush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fillstrokebrush.png) ![../../_images/fillstrokebrush-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fillstrokebrush-properties.png)
For example, to adjust the appearance and behavior of the Button, after you add the Button to your project, in the Properties set:
  * UI - Appearance to set the Corner Radius value that adjust the roundness of the button corners.
  * UI - Fill to set the Fill Color of the button background.
  * UI - Fill Gradient to set the Fill Gradient Color of the button background and its Rotation.
  * UI - Fill Texture to apply a texture to the button background and set how it should be applied.
  * UI - Progress to apply a progress bar state across the background of the button.
  * UI - Segments to divide the button background into segments, and set its number and weight.
  * UI - Stroke to apply an outline to the button, and set its color and weight.


Use any combination of these properties to adjust the appearance of the UI components. Each are enabled individually by marking the property Active.
![../../_images/fill-gradient-active.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fill-gradient-active.png)
You can use bindings to control the UI - Progress property. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
To learn more about the interactivity controls, see [Interactivity controls](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/controls/controls.html).
## Radial UI Components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#radial-ui-components "Link to this heading")
Use the Radial UI Components provided in the Asset Toolkit display values to progress in a round control.
![../../_images/radial-components.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/radial-components.png)
The Radial UI components included in the Asset Toolkit all share a set of similar properties and behaviors, exposed and named the same way.
When you import a UI component, Kanzi Studio adds to your project Library and Prefabs, the required shaders and materials to render that component.
It uses the FillStrokeRadialBrush material, applied as BackgroundBrush to all the UI components, to expose properties that control their appearance and behavior.
![../../_images/fillstrokeradialbrush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fillstrokeradialbrush.png) ![../../_images/fillstrokeradialbrush-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fillstrokeradialbrush-properties.png)
For example, to adjust the appearance and behavior of the Gauge Progress control, after you add it to your project, in the Properties set:
  * UI - Appearance to set the angle at which to apply progress, its radial weight and cap shape.
  * UI - Fill to set the Fill Color of the UI background.
  * UI - Progress to apply progression state across the background of the dial, and its color.
  * UI - Segments to divide the gauge into segments, and set its number and weight.
  * UI - Stroke to apply an outline to the gauge, and set its color and weight.


Use any combination of these properties to adjust the appearance of the Radial UI components. Each are enabled individually by marking the property Active.
![../../_images/segments-active.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/segments-active.png)
You can use bindings to control the UI - Progress property. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
## Simple Shape UI Components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#simple-shape-ui-components "Link to this heading")
Use the simple shape UI components provided in the Asset Toolkit to add basic shapes to your application without the need of a plugin.
![../../_images/simple-shapes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/simple-shapes.png)
  * On the Box with Rounded Corners, set the Corner Radius property to square or round out the shape.
  * On the Circle, set the UI - Fill property values to apply color.


## Scroll list UI Components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#scroll-list-ui-components "Link to this heading")
Use the scroll list UI components provided in the Asset Toolkit to add scrollable lists to your application in one of a four layout patterns.
![../../_images/scroll-list-ui-components.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/scroll-list-ui-components.png)
  * Use the Scroll List Vertical to present items two dimensionally in a vertical scrollable list.
  * Use the Horizontal List Vertical to present items two dimensionally in a horizontally scrollable list.
  * Use the Scroll Trajectory 3D Horizontal to present the items three dimensionally in on horizontal plane.
  * Use the Scroll Trajectory 3D Arc to present the items three dimensionally in an arc.


To learn more about list, see [List Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html).
To use a data source to display your own data in a list component, see [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html), and [Tutorial: Get application data from a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-sources/data-sources.html).
## Examples[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#examples "Link to this heading")
Expand the Asset Toolkit to find a folder with example components that show possible ways to combine these assets into more complex, reusable components.
![../../_images/examples.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/examples.png)
Explore these example components for practical ideas on assembling your own custom controls by combining them.

# Using the Asset Toolkit assets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html#using-the-asset-toolkit-assets "Link to this heading")

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
You can add assets from the Asset Toolkit asset source to your Kanzi application in Kanzi Studio. For a list of the Asset Toolkit assets, see [Asset Toolkit](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html).
## Using Asset Toolkit in your project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html#using-asset-toolkit-in-your-project "Link to this heading")
To use Asset Toolkit in your project:
  1. In the Asset Packages window select the Asset Toolkit asset source.
The Asset Toolkit contains easy, ready-made components and materials with a similar structure and set of properties, that you can use to create Kanzi applications faster.
![../../_images/asset-packages-asset-toolkit-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-asset-toolkit-selected.png)
  2. From the Asset Packages, drag the item that you want to use in your project to a node in the Node Tree, to the Prefabs, or to the Preview. The cursor will indicate whether you can drop the item in that location or not.
For example, drag the Car to the Preview. When you drag an item from the Asset Packages to the Preview or a node in the Node Tree or Pages, Kanzi Studio instantiates that item as a prefab, and adds it to the Prefabs.
![../../_images/select-car-asset1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-car-asset1.png) ![../../_images/car-asset1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-asset1.png) ![../../_images/car-prefab-in-project1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-prefab-in-project1.png)


## Using Asset Toolkit materials in your project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html#using-asset-toolkit-materials-in-your-project "Link to this heading")
To use Asset Toolkit materials in your project:
  1. In the Asset Packages window select the Asset Toolkit asset source.
The Asset Toolkit contains easy, ready-made components and materials with a similar structure and set of properties, that you can use to create Kanzi applications faster.
![../../_images/asset-packages-asset-toolkit-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-asset-toolkit-selected.png)
  2. From the Asset Toolkit drag the material that you want to use in your project to a node in the Preview, or a node in the Node Tree.
For example, to use a paint material to turn the sunroof on the car to a metal, drag that material to either:
     * Preview and drop it on the car body part.
     * Node Tree and drop it on the Model node that shows the mesh for the car body part.
![../../_images/drag-paint-sunroof.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/drag-paint-sunroof.png) ![../../_images/painted-roof-car.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/painted-roof-car.png)
When you use a Asset Toolkit material in your project, Kanzi Studio adds that material to the Library > Materials and Textures > Materials, and the shaders used by the material to the Library > Resource Files > Shaders.


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html#sa "Link to this heading")

Create and position 2D nodes, create and edit Text Block nodes, add triggers, create and position Camera nodes, and zoom and pan around the Preview.
To edit your application in the Preview use the Preview tools.
![../../_images/edit-mode.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/edit-mode.png)
## The Preview tools[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html#the-preview-tools "Link to this heading")
You can use these tools to edit the content in your project:  
| Tool  | Control  | Description  | Shortcut key  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  ![../../_images/node-tool.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png)  |   | Use the Node tool to select any node.  |   |  
|   |  ![../../_images/move.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/move.png)  | Move the selected node.  | 1  |  
|   |  ![../../_images/rotate.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rotate.png)  | Rotate the selected node.  | 2  |  
|   |  ![../../_images/scale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/scale.png)  | Scale the selected node.  | 3  |  
|   |  ![../../_images/align.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/align.png)  | Click the square to align the selected 2D node to that side. For example, the setting in this image sets the Vertical Alignment property to Top and Horizontal Alignment property to Left.  |   |  
|   |  ![../../_images/horizontal-stretch.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/horizontal-stretch.png)  | Stretch the selected 2D node horizontally. Sets the Horizontal Alignment property to Stretch.  |   |  
|   |  ![../../_images/vertical-stretch.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/vertical-stretch.png)  | Stretch the selected 2D node vertically. Sets the Vertical Alignment property to Stretch.  |   |  
|   | ![image7](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/horizontal-and-vertical-stretch.png)  | Stretch the selected 2D node horizontally and vertically. Sets the Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment properties to Stretch.  |   |  
|   | ![image8](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-transformation-layout-transformation.png)  | Use the Layout Transformation property fields to place the selected node. For 2D nodes enter the values for the X and Y property fields. See [Optimizing the rendering of layouts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/optimizing-rendering-of-layouts.html).  |   |  
|   | ![image9](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-transformation-render-transformation.png)  | Use the Render Transformation property fields to place the selected node. For 2D nodes enter the values for the X and Y property fields. See [Optimizing the rendering of layouts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/optimizing-rendering-of-layouts.html).  |   |  
|   | ![image10](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/scale-layout-height-and-width.png)  | Use the Layout Height and Layout Width properties to set the size of the selected 2D node.  |   |  
|   | ![image11](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-snap.png)  | Snap the size or position of the selected 2D node to the nearest coordinates of a surrounding node.  |   |  
|   | ![image12](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/scale-attribute.png)  | Use the Scale of the Layout Transformation or Render Transformation properties to set the size of the selected node.  |   |  
|   | ![image13](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/world-space.png)  | Use the world coordinates to position the selected 3D node.  |   |  
|   | ![image14](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/local-space.png)  | Use the local coordinates to position the selected 3D node.  |   |  
| ![image15](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout-2d-tool.png)  |   | Grid Layout 2D tool. Click and drag in the Preview to create a Grid Layout 2D. The size of the area you create defines the size of the layout (Layout Width and Layout Height). See [Using the Grid Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html).  |   |  
| ![image16](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-tool.png)  |   | Text Block 2D tool. Click and drag in the Preview to create a Text Block 2D. The size of the area you create defines the size of the layout (Layout Width and Layout Height). See [Using the Text Block nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html).  |   |  
|   | ![image17](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-tool-text.png)  | Enter the text that a Text Block 2D shows.  |   |  
|   | ![image18](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/align.png)  | Click the square to align the text to that side. For example, the setting in this image sets the Text Vertical Alignment property to Top and Text Horizontal Alignment property to Left.  |   |  
|   | ![image19](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-tool-size.png)  | Select the font size in device independent pixels you want to use for the Text Block 2D node.  |   |  
|   | ![image20](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-tool-font.png)  | Select the font you want to use for the Text Block 2D node. Note that the dropdown menu lists only the fonts in your current project. See [Importing fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html).  |   |  
| ![image21](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-2d-tool.png)  |   | Stack Layout 2D tool. Click and drag in the Preview to create a Stack Layout 2D. The size of the area you create defines the size of the layout (Layout Width and Layout Height). To set the Stack Layout 2D to arrange its items along either x or y axis, create an area that is longer on the axis along which you want the Stack Layout 2D to arrange its items. See [Using the Stack Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-stack-layouts.html).  |   |  
| ![image22](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-2d-tool.png)  |   | Flow Layout 2D tool. Click and drag in the Preview to create a Flow Layout 2D. The size of the area you create defines the size of the layout (Layout Width and Layout Height). See [Using the Flow Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-flow-layouts.html).  |   |  
| ![image23](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera-tool.png)  |   |  Use the Camera tool to move around the scene using the preview camera and to create and position cameras in your project. See [Using the Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html). Tip You can control the position of a Camera node when you use the Node tool in the Preview window. To move with the Orbit Camera, hold down `Alt` and use these controls:
  * Click and drag the left mouse button to rotate.
  * Click and drag the middle mouse button to pan.
  * Scroll the mouse wheel to zoom.

To move with the Free Camera, hold down the right mouse button and use these controls:
  * Move the mouse to tilt and rotate the camera angle in any direction.
  * Use `W`, `S`, `A`, and `D` to move the camera position forward, backward, left, and right.
  * Use `E` and `Q` to move the camera position up and down.
  * Scroll the mouse wheel to set the camera speed.
  * Hold down `Shift` to double the speed when moving.
  * Use `F` to bring the camera to the 3D object selected in the Preview

Tip To place:
  * A node to the position of the current view of the Camera in the Preview, in the Node Tree, right-click that node and select Align With View.
  * The Preview view to the location of any node, in the Node Tree, right-click that node and select Align View To Selected.

For example, to place a Camera node to the position of any node in a Scene node:
  1. Right-click the node to whose position you want to place a Camera node and select Align View To Selected.
  2. To store that position to the Camera, right-click the Camera and select Align With View.

![../../_images/node-tree-align-view-align-to-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-align-view-align-to-selected.png)  |   |  
|   | ![image24](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera-tool-set-position-of-the-preview-camera.png)  | Store the current position of the camera to the preview Camera node.  |   |  
|   | ![image25](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera-tool-reset-to-preview-camera.png)  | Reset the camera to the current position of the preview Camera node.  |   |  
|   | ![image26](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera-tool-create-new-camera.png)  | Create a new Camera node from the current position of the camera.  | J  |  
|   | ![image27](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera-tool-orbit-camera.png)  |  Orbit Camera lets you move around:
  * The nodes that you select in the Node Tree.
  * The node that you set with the Constraints > Look At property of the camera.

 |   |  
|   | ![image28](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera-tool-free-camera.png)  | Free Camera lets you move around without attachment to any point.  |   |  
|   | ![image29](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera-tool-bring-the-camera.png)  | Bring the camera to the 3D object selected in the Node Tree or the Preview.  |   |  
|   | ![image30](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera-node-selector.png)  | Select the Camera node through which you want to view the current scene.  |   |  
|   | ![image31](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera-tool-fov.png)  | Set the field of view for the camera in degrees when working with 3D nodes.  |   |  
## Panning and zooming in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html#panning-and-zooming-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
To pan and zoom in the Preview:  
| Action  | Shortcut  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Pan  | Click and drag the middle mouse button.  |  
| Zoom  | 
  * Use the control in the upper right corner of the Preview: ![../../_images/adjust-the-preview-zoom-level.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/adjust-the-preview-zoom-level.png)
  * Scroll the mouse wheel.
  * Press the `Shift` and `Alt` keys, and click and drag the left mouse button.

 |  
## Resetting the view in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html#resetting-the-view-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
When you want to return the Preview zoom level to 100% and position your application screen in the center of the Preview, click ![image32](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/zoom.png) or press `Ctrl` `1` to reset the view in the Preview.
![../../_images/view-in-the-preview-needs-resetting.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/view-in-the-preview-needs-resetting.png) ![../../_images/view-in-the-preview-position-and-zoom-reset.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/view-in-the-preview-position-and-zoom-reset.png)
## Taking a screenshot of the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html#taking-a-screenshot-of-the-preview "Link to this heading")
Use the the Screenshot button ![image33](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/screenshot-tool.png) to capture the current view of your application as it appears in the Preview. This is useful for product verification, documentation or to use as project thumbnail for example.
In the User Preferences > Advanced tab, set:
  * The Default Screenshot location where screenshots are saved.
  * The Screenshot background options which controls how the background of the image is filled.
    * Without Background takes the screenshot with a transparent background.
    * With Screen Clear Color takes the screenshot with the Screen Clear Color as background.
![../../_images/preview-screenshot-user-preferences.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-screenshot-user-preferences.png)
Note
The Screenshot background options only take effect if the Background Brush and Foreground Brush properties are set to NullBrush and No Brush. If not, the screenshot background will be filled using the Background Brush defined in the Brush property of the node.
  * To take a screenshot of the current view in the Preview window, click the Screenshot ![image33](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/screenshot-tool.png) button.
![../../_images/preview-screenshot-button.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-screenshot-button.png)
A message in the Status Bar indicates that the screenshot was taken successfully. The image is saved in the location you set in the User Preferences, as a `png` file with the project name and date-time stamp as the name.


## Setting anti-aliasing in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html#setting-anti-aliasing-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
By default, the Kanzi Studio Preview and the Kanzi Application Player on Windows apply anti-aliasing using 4 samples. For both, you can configure the amount of anti-aliasing that you want to use.
If you have a Kanzi application with a C++ application, to see your content in the Kanzi Studio Preview and Kanzi Application Player the same way as when running your Kanzi application on a target device, you can set anti-aliasing in an `application.cfg` file. See [Applying anti-aliasing to an entire application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/anti-aliasing.html#applying-anti-aliasing-to-an-entire-application).
To set anti-aliasing in the Kanzi Studio Preview for a Kanzi application without a C++ application:
  1. In the Kanzi Studio main menu, select Project > Properties. In the Properties in the Preview section, set the value of the Preview Working Directory property to the directory where you want to store the `application.cfg` to configure the Preview.
For example, set the Preview Working Directory property to `Application Player`. This way, you can apply the same anti-aliasing setting to the Preview and the Kanzi Application Player on Windows. If the `<ProjectName>/Application Player` directory does not yet exist, select File > Export > Export as KZB Player for Windows. See [Building and deploying Kanzi applications to Windows from Kanzi Studio](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/deploying-applications/deploying-kanzi-applications-for-windows.html#building-and-deploying-kanzi-applications-to-windows-from-kanzi-studio).
![../../_images/project-properties-myproject.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties-myproject.png) ![../../_images/preview-working-dir-application-player.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-working-dir-application-player.png)
  2. In the directory that you set in the previous step, create or open the `application.cfg` file. Add and set the `SurfaceSamplesAntialiasing` parameter to the number of anti-aliasing samples that you want the Preview to use.
For example, to disable anti-aliasing in the Preview, in the `application.cfg`, add:

```
SurfaceSamplesAntialiasing = 0

```
Copy to clipboard
  3. In Kanzi Studio, restart the Preview.
![../../_images/preview-restart-button-gray.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-restart-button-gray.png)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use an environment texture to represent the environment, such as an outdoor scene or an indoor space. You can create an environment texture from an HDR or EXR image:
  * An environment cubemap texture combines six square-shaped images into a texture that represents the environment. See [Using an environment cubemap texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html#using-an-environment-cubemap-texture).
  * An environment lat-long (equirectangular) texture is a single image that represents the environment. See [Using a lat-long environment texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html#using-a-lat-long-environment-texture).


## Using an environment cubemap texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html#using-an-environment-cubemap-texture "Link to this heading")
To use an environment cubemap texture:
  1. Create an environment cubemap texture:
    1. In the Assets click Import Assets and select an HDR or EXR image from which you want to create an environment cubemap texture.
![../../_images/assets-import-assets.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assets-import-assets.png)
Tip
To create an environment cubemap texture for an HDR or EXR image that you have already imported to your Kanzi Studio project, in the Library > Resource Files > Images press `Alt` and right-click that image and select Environment Cubemap Texture.
![../../_images/create-environment-cubemap-texture-context-menu.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-environment-cubemap-texture-context-menu.png)
    2. In the Create Textures for HDR Images dialog:
      1. Select Environment Cubemap Texture.
![../../_images/create-environment-cubemap-texture-dialog.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-environment-cubemap-texture-dialog.png)
Tip
To create for the image also irradiance and specular cubemap textures that represent the lighting coming from the environment, select Image-Based Lighting Cubemap Textures. See [Using image-based lighting cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html).
      2. (Optional) To manually set the size of the cubemap faces, disable the Automatic setting and set the Cubemap Face Resolution.
For example, to create an environment cubemap texture where the size of each cubemap face is 512 by 512 pixels, set Cubemap Face Resolution to 512.
Kanzi Studio by default creates a cubemap texture where the width and height of each cubemap face is one quarter of the width of the image that you import.
![../../_images/environment-cubemap-face-resolution.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/environment-cubemap-face-resolution.png)
      3. Click Create.
Kanzi Studio imports the image and creates in the Library > Materials and Textures > Textures an environment Cubemap Texture for that image.
Kanzi Studio creates and sets the cubemap face images:
       * NegZ Image to the front face image
       * PosZ Image to the back face image
       * NegX Image to the left face image
       * PosX Image to the right face image
       * NegY Image to the bottom face image
       * PosY Image to the top face image
![../../_images/my-hdr-image-environment.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-hdr-image-environment.png) ![../../_images/my-hdr-image-environment-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-hdr-image-environment-properties.png) ![../../_images/environment-cubemap-faces.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/environment-cubemap-faces.png)
Tip
You can restrict the brightness of strongly lit areas in the textures that you create from an HDR image.
To set the maximum brightness level in the cubemap textures that you create from an HDR image:
      1. In the Library > Resource Files > Images, select the image. In the Properties, add the Clamp Pixels property and set it to the value to which you want to restrict the color values in the cubemap face images that you create from that image.
      2. In the Library > Resource Files > Images, press `Alt` and right-click the image and select the cubemap texture that you want to create.
![../../_images/clamp-pixels.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clamp-pixels.png) ![../../_images/recreate-env-cubemap-textures.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/recreate-env-cubemap-textures.png)
  2. In the Library > Materials and Textures, press `Alt` and right-click Material Types, and select CubemapSkybox.
Kanzi Studio creates in the Library > Materials and Textures the CubemapSkybox material type and CubemapSkyboxMaterial, which supports showing a cubemap texture as a skybox.
![../../_images/library-create-cubemap-skybox-material-type.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-create-cubemap-skybox-material-type.png)
  3. In the Library, select the CubemapSkyboxMaterial material. In the Properties, set the TextureCube property to the cubemap texture that you want to use to render a skybox.
![../../_images/library-cubemap-skybox-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-cubemap-skybox-material.png) ![../../_images/properties-cubemap-skybox-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-cubemap-skybox-material.png)
  4. Create a Box or Sphere node that you use to render the skybox. In the Properties, set:
     * Mesh Material to CubemapSkyboxMaterial
     * The size of the node so that it is large enough to fit the content that you want to show inside it:
       * For a Box, set the Width, Height, and Depth properties.
       * For a Sphere, set the Radius property.
     * Generate Mesh Inside Out to enabled
When this property is enabled, Kanzi renders the cubemap texture inside the mesh.
![../../_images/node-tree-box.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-box.png) ![../../_images/properties-box-skybox.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-box-skybox.png)
  5. Position a Camera node inside the node that you created.


When you rotate the camera, in the Preview you can see the environment texture rendered as a skybox.
![../../_images/environment-map-rotation.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/environment-map-rotation.gif)
## Using a lat-long environment texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html#using-a-lat-long-environment-texture "Link to this heading")
To use a lat-long (equirectangular) environment texture:
  1. Create a lat-long environment texture:
    1. In the Assets click Import Assets and select an HDR or EXR image that you want to use for the lat-long environment texture.
![../../_images/assets-import-assets.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assets-import-assets.png)
Note
If you use an LDR image, import the image, select the texture in the Library > Materials and Textures > Textures, and in the Properties set the Wrap Mode property to Repeat.
    2. In the Create Textures for HDR Images dialog, select Single Texture, and click Create.
![../../_images/create-single-texture-dialog.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-single-texture-dialog.png)
Kanzi Studio imports the image and creates a Single Texture in the Library > Materials and Textures > Textures.
  2. In the Library > Materials and Textures, press `Alt` and right-click Material Types, and select LatLongSkybox.
Kanzi Studio creates in the Library > Materials and Textures the LatLongSkybox material type and LatLongSkyboxMaterial, which supports showing a lat-long environment texture as a skybox.
![../../_images/library-create-latlong-skybox-material-type.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-create-latlong-skybox-material-type.png)
  3. In the Library, select the LatLongSkyboxMaterial material. In the Properties, set the Texture property to the lat-long (equirectangular) texture that you want to use to render a skybox.
![../../_images/library-latlong-skybox-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-latlong-skybox-material.png) ![../../_images/properties-latlong-skybox-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-latlong-skybox-material.png)
  4. Create a Box or Sphere node that you use to render the skybox. In the Properties, set:
     * Mesh Material to LatLongSkyboxMaterial
     * The size of the node so that it is large enough to fit the content that you want to show inside it:
     * For a Box, set the Width, Height, and Depth properties.
     * For a Sphere, set the Radius property.
     * Generate Mesh Inside Out to enabled
When this property is enabled, Kanzi renders the environment texture inside the mesh.
![../../_images/node-tree-box.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-box.png) ![../../_images/properties-box-latlong-skybox.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-box-latlong-skybox.png)
  5. Position a Camera node inside the node that you created.


When you rotate the camera, in the Preview you can see the environment texture rendered as a skybox.
![../../_images/environment-map-rotation.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/environment-map-rotation.gif)
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html#sa "Link to this heading")

[Using image-based lighting cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html)
[Creating textured materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/creating-textured-materials.html)
[Images](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/images.html)

# Automating Kanzi Studio tasks[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#automating-ks-tasks "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
