Use render passes to define the rendering of 3D content in your Kanzi application.
For example, in render passes you can define:
  * Which Camera that render pass and its descendants use for rendering. See [Setting the camera for render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html#setting-the-camera-for-render-passes).
  * What nodes the render pass renders. See [Collecting nodes for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/filtering-node-lists.html).
  * What lights to use to light the content. See [Using lights in rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/lights-rendering.html).
  * What material to use to render the content. [Setting materials for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-materials.html).
  * The format of the composition target. See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html).
  * Post-processing effects. [Creating a post-processing effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/post-processing-grayscale.html).


To achieve a specific rendering result, create a hierarchy of render passes which together form a render pass prefab. In a Viewport 2D node the Render Pass Prefab property sets which render passes Kanzi uses to render the 3D content of that node. See [Creating and using render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html#creating-and-using-render-passes).
You can reuse render passes in your Kanzi Studio project in these ways:
  * Customize render passes in each Viewport 2D node where you use them. See [Customizing instances of render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html#customizing-instances-of-render-passes).
  * Reuse render passes in another render pass tree. See [Reusing render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html#reusing-render-passes).
  * Import render passes that you created in another Kanzi Studio project. See [Reusing render passes by merging](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html#reusing-render-passes-by-merging).


Learn how to use render passes by completing these tutorials:
  * Apply a stencil to 3D content and render only the area defined by the stencil. See [Tutorial: Apply a stencil to 3D content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/stencil/stencil.html).
  * Create reflections of 3D content. See [Tutorial: Create reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/reflections/reflections.html).
  * Distribute the rendering workload across several frames. See [Tutorial: Progressive rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/progressive-rendering/progressive-rendering.html).
  * Apply a bloom effect on 3D content. See [Tutorial: Create a bloom effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/bloom/bloom.html).
![../../_images/bloom-completed.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/bloom-completed.gif)


## Creating and using render passes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html#creating-and-using-render-passes "Link to this heading")
To create and use render passes:
  1. In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs press `Alt` and right-click and select the render pass that you want to use as the root render pass of your render pass tree. See [Render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#render-passes).
In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs each top-level render pass is the root of a render pass prefab.
In a render pass prefab, you can create a hierarchy of render passes to achieve a specific rendering result.
For example, create a Group render pass.
Group render pass allows you to collect render passes so that you can refer to a single render pass prefab in your Viewport 2D node.
![../../_images/create-group-render-pass.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-group-render-pass.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select the Viewport 2D node that contains the 3D content that you want to render and in the Properties set the Render Pass Prefab property to the render pass that you created.
When you set a Viewport 2D node to use a specific render pass, Kanzi instantiates in the Viewport 2D node the render pass tree defined by that render pass. Kanzi now renders the content of the Viewport 2D node using the render pass that you created.
![../../_images/viewport-2d-in-the-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/viewport-2d-in-the-project.png) ![../../_images/render-pass-prefab-set-to-group-render-pass.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-pass-prefab-set-to-group-render-pass.png)
  3. In the render pass that you created, create the hierarchy of render passes that you need to render your 3D content.
For example:
     * For the most common rendering results, use the Kanzi Studio render pass presets. See [Using Kanzi Studio render pass presets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html).
     * Create a night vision mode or an infinity mirror. See [Setting materials for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-materials.html).
     * Apply post-processing to your 3D content. See [Creating a post-processing effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/post-processing-grayscale.html).
     * Apply a stencil to 3D content so that Kanzi renders only a selected area of the content. See [Applying a stencil to 3D content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/stencil-buffer.html).
     * Reduce aliasing in your content. See [Using multisampling](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/anti-aliasing.html#using-multisampling).


## Customizing instances of render passes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html#customizing-instances-of-render-passes "Link to this heading")
A render pass can contain a hierarchy of render passes, each with their own properties. When you edit the render passes, you change how those render passes render content in all Viewport 2D nodes that use them. You can customize individual instances of a render passes to have individual values by overriding the values in the default render pass. For example, when you create a hierarchy of render passes that blits a composition target to the screen, you can blit the content using a different material in different instances of the render passes.
To customize instances of render passes:
  1. In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs select the render pass that you want to customize.
For example, to customize the material that you use to blit a composition target to the screen, in a Compose and Blit Pass render pass prefab, which renders content to a composition target and blits the result to the screen, select the Blit render pass. See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html).
![../../_images/blit-render-pass-in-render-target-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blit-render-pass-in-render-target-tree.png)
  2. In the Properties, next to the property that you want to customize, click ![enable-editing](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enable-editing-of-this-property.png).
Kanzi Studio creates from that property a custom property, adds it to the root of the render pass prefab, and creates a `##Template` binding to the property in the render pass prefab root. See [Prefab root bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#prefab-root-bindings).
For example, to customize the material which you use to blit the composition target to the screen, click ![enable-editing](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enable-editing-of-this-property.png) next to the Material property. Kanzi Studio adds the Material property to the Compose and Blit Pass render pass prefab and creates in the Blit render pass a `##Template` binding to the Material property in that Compose and Blit Pass.
![../../_images/publish-material-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/publish-material-property.png) ![../../_images/template-binding-to-blit-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/template-binding-to-blit-material.png)
  3. In the Node Tree or Prefabs select a Viewport 2D node and in the Properties set the Render Pass Prefab property to the render pass prefab that you customized.
When you set a Viewport 2D node or prefab to use a render pass prefab, Kanzi Studio shows in that Viewport 2D node the properties of that render pass prefab as frequently used properties.
![../../_images/viewport-2d-in-the-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/viewport-2d-in-the-project.png) ![../../_images/render-pass-prefab-set-to-compose-and-blit-pass.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-pass-prefab-set-to-compose-and-blit-pass.png)
  4. In the Properties click ![add-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-property.png) next to the property that you customized and set the value of the property.
Kanzi Studio adds to the Viewport 2D node a to-source binding which pushes the value of that property to the render pass prefab instance made available through the `Viewport2D::RenderPassProperty[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13906.html#a4028fe02fff026d7ae712099f685652d)` property of the Viewport 2D node.
You can set multiple Viewport 2D nodes to use the same render pass prefab and in each Viewport 2D node you can add and set the render pass prefab property to have different values.
![../../_images/group-render-pass-material-frequently-used.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/group-render-pass-material-frequently-used.png) ![../../_images/tosource-binding-to-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/tosource-binding-to-material.png)
Tip
When you want to remove from a node a property and its To Source binding, right-click that property and select Remove Property And Binding.


## Reusing render passes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html#reusing-render-passes "Link to this heading")
You can reuse render passes in another render pass tree. In each instance of a render pass prefab you can set the property values of render passes in that render pass prefab. For example, reuse multiple instances of a render pass prefab to create render pass chains to achieve post-processing effects. See [Tutorial: Create a bloom effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/bloom/bloom.html).
To reuse render passes:
  1. In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs press `Alt` and right-click the render pass where you want to instantiate a render pass prefab and select Render Pass View.
![../../_images/create-render-pass-view.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-render-pass-view.png)
  2. In the Properties add the Render Pass Prefab property and set it to the render pass prefab that you want to instantiate.
Kanzi Studio shows in the Render Pass View all properties of the render pass prefab that the Render Pass View instantiates. See [Customizing instances of render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html#customizing-instances-of-render-passes).
![../../_images/render-pass-view-add-render-pass-prefab-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-pass-view-add-render-pass-prefab-property.png) ![../../_images/render-pass-view-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-pass-view-properties.png)


Tip
You can instantiate a render pass prefab by dragging it to a render pass or another render pass prefab.
## Reusing render passes by merging[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html#reusing-render-passes-by-merging "Link to this heading")
You can reuse render passes from another Kanzi Studio project by merging the render passes to the project in which you want to use them.
To reuse render passes by merging:
  1. In the project where you want to use render passes from another project, select File > Import > Merge Project, select the Kanzi Studio project which contains the render passes that you want to merge, and click Open.
![../../_images/merge-project-menu-option.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/merge-project-menu-option.png)
  2. In the Project Merge dialog:
    1. At the bottom left of the dialog enable Select referenced items.
You set Kanzi Studio to automatically select all items to which the render pass prefab, which you want to merge, refers.
    2. In Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs select the render pass prefab which contains the hierarchy of render passes that you want to use.
Click Merge.
![../../_images/merge-gaussian-blur.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/merge-gaussian-blur.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the Viewport 2D node, which contains the 3D content you want to render using the render passes that you merged, and in the Properties set the Render Pass Prefab property to the render pass prefab that you merged to your project.
![../../_images/viewport-2d-to-use-gaussian-blur.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/viewport-2d-to-use-gaussian-blur.png)


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html)

# Binding Render Pass node properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-prism-property-bindings.html#binding-render-pass-node-properties "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
These steps show how to bind properties on Render Pass nodes so the value of one property drives another.
For an introduction to Prism graphs, see [Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html).
## Resource property bindings[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-prism-property-bindings.html#resource-property-bindings "Link to this heading")
A resource property binding is a line drawn directly between two resource properties of the same type. To create the binding, drag from the source property on one node onto the target property on another.
### Example: connect Build Acceleration Structure to Draw Objects for raytraced shadows[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-prism-property-bindings.html#example-connect-build-acceleration-structure-to-draw-objects-for-raytraced-shadows "Link to this heading")
This example rebuilds an existing raytraced-shadow scene as a Prism graph. The original scene uses a manual render-pass setup to produce a top-level acceleration structure and pass it to the draw pass that consumes it. The Prism graph expresses the same dependency as a binding line between two resource properties.
To connect Build Acceleration Structure to Draw Objects for raytraced shadows:
  1. In the Kanzi Studio Quick Start window, click Projects and select the Examples tab. If the Raytracing example is not yet downloaded, click ![download](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/download.svg) next to it.
Kanzi Studio downloads the example to the `<KanziWorkspace>/Examples/Raytracing` directory.
  2. Copy the `<KanziWorkspace>/Examples/Raytracing` folder to a new location to keep the original project unchanged.
  3. Open `Raytracing.proj.kzm` from your copy of the project and confirm raytraced shadows are visible in the **Preview**.
![Preview of the Raytracing example before any Prism graph changes, showing raytraced shadows on the scene.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/raytracing-baseline-shadows.png)
  4. In the **Library** , go to **Rendering** > **Prism Graphs**. Right-click **Prism Graphs** and select **Create** > **Empty Prism Graph**. Name it `Raytracing Prism Graph`.
![Right-click context menu in the Library Prism Graphs folder, with Create > Empty Prism Graph highlighted.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png)
  5. Select the **Viewport 2D** that renders the scene. In the **Properties** panel, set Render Pass Prefab to the new Prism graph. The viewport stops rendering until the graph is complete.
![Viewport 2D Properties panel with the Render Pass Prefab dropdown open and Raytracing Prism Graph selected.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-raytracing-prism-graph.png)
  6. Open the Prism graph by double-clicking it in the **Library**. The Prism editor opens for the graph, showing the initial empty state with only the Output node.
![Library showing Raytracing Prism Graph under Rendering > Prism Graphs, being double-clicked.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-raytracing-prism-graph.png) ![Prism editor open for Raytracing Prism Graph, showing the initial empty state with only the Output node.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/raytracing-prism-graph-empty-editor.png)
  7. Add the main rendering nodes. Right-click in the graph and add:
     * **Gather Lights** render pass node.
     * **Draw Objects** render pass node.
Connect **Gather Lights** to **Draw Objects** , and **Draw Objects** to the **Output** node.
The **Preview** now renders the scene objects under the scene lighting, but raytraced shadows are not yet visible. The next steps add and bind the acceleration structure that **Draw Objects** needs to render those shadows.
![Preview showing the scene rendered with objects and lighting but without raytraced shadows, alongside the Prism graph containing the Gather Lights, Draw Objects, and Output nodes.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/raytracing-prism-main-chain.png)
  8. On the **Draw Objects** node, click ![add-properties-window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png) to open the Add Properties window. In the search box, type `topLevelAS` to locate the property under Material Properties.
![Add Properties window for the Draw Objects node with "topLevelAS" typed in the search box and the topLevelAS property highlighted under Material Properties in the Available Properties pane.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-toplevelas-search.png)
Double-click **topLevelAS** to add it. The property moves from Available Properties to Existing Properties.
![Add Properties window after adding topLevelAS, showing the property in the Existing Properties pane on the right.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-toplevelas-added.png)
Close the Add Properties window.
  9. Right-click in the graph and add a **Build Acceleration Structure** render pass node. This node has no framebuffer socket because it produces an acceleration structure rather than a rendered image. Leave it unconnected to the other nodes. It reaches its consumer through the binding line added in the next step.
  10. Drag a binding line from the **OutputAccelerationStructure** property on the **Build Acceleration Structure** node onto the **topLevelAS** property on the **Draw Objects** node.
This creates a resource property binding between the two properties. The binding copies the value from **OutputAccelerationStructure** into **topLevelAS** so the draw pass uses the acceleration structure that the build pass produced.
![Animation of dragging a binding line from the OutputAccelerationStructure property of the Build Acceleration Structure node onto the topLevelAS property of the Draw Objects node.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/bind-toplevelas.gif)
  11. Confirm the **Preview** again renders the raytraced shadows. The binding gives **Draw Objects** the acceleration structure that **Build Acceleration Structure** produced.
![Preview showing raytraced shadows in the Prism-driven rebuild, alongside the completed Prism graph with the binding line from Build Acceleration Structure into Draw Objects.topLevelAS.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/raytracing-prism-result.png)


### Example: use Decode to bind an offscreen framebuffer to a Blit Render Pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-prism-property-bindings.html#example-use-decode-to-bind-an-offscreen-framebuffer-to-a-blit-render-pass "Link to this heading")
This example uses the **Decode** adapter node to create a resource property binding.
Some Prism nodes expose bindable resource properties through the **Decode** adapter node. You need **Decode** to bind from a non-Render-Pass node’s offscreen framebuffer output to another resource property. **Decode** presents the framebuffer’s attachments as named texture properties (`ResultTexture0`, `ResultDepthTexture`) that a Render Pass node’s property can bind to.
To use Decode to bind an offscreen framebuffer to a Blit Render Pass:
  1. In your project, add a Box to the scene by right-clicking **Scene** > **Create** > **Box** so the graph has something to render.
  2. In the **Library** , go to **Rendering** > **Prism Graphs**. Right-click **Prism Graphs** and select **Create** > **Empty Prism Graph**. Name it `Decode Bridge Prism Graph`.
  3. Select the **Viewport 2D** that renders the scene. In the **Properties** panel, set Render Pass Prefab to the new Prism graph.
  4. Open the Prism graph by double-clicking it in the **Library**.
  5. Add the framebuffer-rendering nodes. Right-click in the graph and add:
     * **Offscreen Framebuffer** node.
     * **Clear** node.
     * **Draw** node.
Connect **Offscreen Framebuffer** to **Clear** , and **Clear** to **Draw**.
  6. Continue with Render Pass nodes. Add:
     * **Decode** adapter node, which exposes the upstream framebuffer’s contents as a named texture property.
     * **Blit** Render Pass node.
Connect **Draw** to **Decode**. Then connect **Blit** to the **Output** node. **Decode** has no output socket, so it cannot connect to **Blit** via a node socket. The connection from **Decode** to **Blit** is made through a binding line in the next step.
![Prism graph with Offscreen Framebuffer, Clear, Draw, Decode on the left and the Blit Render Pass and Output nodes on the right, before any binding is added.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/decode-bridge-mixed-chain.png)
  7. On the **Blit** node, click ![add-properties-window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png) to open the Add Properties window. In the search box, type `Texture 0` and double-click the property to add it. Close the Add Properties window.
  8. Drag a binding line from the **ResultTexture0** property on the **Decode** node onto the **Texture 0** property on the **Blit** node.
This creates a resource property binding: the value of **ResultTexture0** is copied into **Texture 0** so the **Blit** Render Pass consumes the texture rendered into the offscreen framebuffer by the upstream nodes.
![Animation of dragging a binding line from the ResultTexture0 property of the Decode node onto the Texture 0 property of the Blit node.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/bind-decode-texture0.gif)
  9. Confirm the **Preview** renders the box composited through the **Blit** Render Pass. The upstream nodes render the box into the offscreen framebuffer; **Decode** exposes that framebuffer as **ResultTexture0** ; the binding hands the texture to **Blit** , which composites it to the **Output**.
![Preview showing the box rendered through the Decode bridge to the Blit Render Pass.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/decode-bridge-result.png)


Tip
In this example, dragging directly from the **Draw** node’s output connector onto the **Texture 0** property on **Blit** inserts the **Decode** node and creates the binding in one step.
## Text property bindings[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-prism-property-bindings.html#text-property-bindings "Link to this heading")
A text property binding drives a non-resource property from a binding expression. Non-resource properties are values such as numbers, booleans, colors, or vectors. Use a text binding when you want the property value to come from a Kanzi binding expression instead of a direct value set in the editor. Unlike a direct value set, a binding expression can include arithmetic, function calls, and references to other properties. See [Bindings expressions reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html) for the expression syntax.
### Example: set the background color of a Prism graph from a binding expression[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-prism-property-bindings.html#example-set-the-background-color-of-a-prism-graph-from-a-binding-expression "Link to this heading")
This example reuses the **Raytracing** example project from the previous examples. It builds a small Prism graph that clears the screen to a color computed from a binding expression, then draws the scene on top. Use the same pattern to drive any non-resource property on a Render Pass node from a binding expression.
To set the background color of a Prism graph from a binding expression:
  1. If you have not already, open `Raytracing.proj.kzm` from your copy of the **Raytracing** example. See steps 1 to 3 of _Example: connect Build Acceleration Structure to Draw Objects for raytraced shadows_.
  2. In the **Library** , go to **Rendering** > **Prism Graphs**. Right-click **Prism Graphs** and select **Create** > **Empty Prism Graph**. Name it `Background Color Prism Graph`.
  3. Select the **Viewport 2D** that renders the scene. In the **Properties** panel, set Render Pass Prefab to the new graph. The viewport stops rendering until the graph is complete.
  4. Open the Prism graph by double-clicking it in the **Library**.
  5. Right-click in the graph and add a **Clear** basic node and a **Draw Objects** Render Pass node. Connect **Clear** to **Draw Objects** , and **Draw Objects** to the **Output** node.
  6. On the **Clear** node, click ![add-properties-window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png) to open the Add Properties window. In the search box, type `Clear Color 0`. Under Available Properties, double-click **Clear Color 0** to add it. Close the Add Properties window.
The **Preview** now renders the scene on the default black clear color.
  7. In the Prism property pane on the **Clear** node, right-click the **Clear Color 0** row and select Edit binding….
Kanzi Studio opens the binding editor in a floating window with **Clear Color 0** as the binding target.
![Right-click context menu on the Clear Color 0 row in the Prism property pane, with the Edit binding entry highlighted.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clear-color-edit-binding-menu.png)
  8. In the binding editor expression field, enter:

```
Color4(0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0)

```
Copy to clipboard
Click Save. The editor closes. The **Preview** shows the scene against a deep blue background. The **Clear Color 0** row shows a binding indicator on the label and a read-only preview of the expression in place of the value editor.
![Animation of the Clear Color 0 row in the Prism property pane after binding, showing the binding indicator on the label and the expression preview Color4\(0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0\) in place of the value editor.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clear-color-bound-row.gif)
  9. Open the binding editor again and replace the expression with one that scales the current expression:

```
Color4(0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0) * 2

```
Copy to clipboard
Save. The background becomes brighter. The row preview updates to show the new expression.
![Preview window showing the brighter blue background, alongside the Clear Color 0 row with the expression preview Color4\(0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0\) * 2.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clear-color-bound-row-brighter.png)


To remove the binding and restore a direct editable value, right-click the row and select Clear binding.
If the expression cannot be parsed, the inline preview turns red. Reopen Edit binding… to correct the expression.
Tip
You can also start a text binding by dragging from the display name of one Prism property row onto another non-resource property row. The binding editor opens prefilled with an expression that references the source row’s property.
![Animation of dragging from the Blend Mode row of one Blit Render Pass node onto the Blend Mode row of another Blit Render Pass node, with the binding editor opening prefilled with an expression that references the source row's property.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prism-text-binding-drag.gif)
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-prism-property-bindings.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html)
[Creating Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html)
[Adding shadows to Prism render graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html)
[Creating Bloom Effect with Prism Graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html)

# Using bookmarks[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#using-bookmarks "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use bookmarks to provide a quick way to access objects and resources in your Kanzi Studio project. To access resources and objects in your Kanzi application in code, use the kzb file URL.
Kanzi Studio stores bookmarks in the Library > Bookmarks.
To access nodes in your Kanzi Studio project or using the Kanzi API you can also use aliases. See [Using aliases](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/aliases/using-aliases.html).
## Creating a bookmark from any item[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#creating-a-bookmark-from-any-item "Link to this heading")
To create a bookmark from any item in Kanzi Studio, in the Node Tree, Nodes, or Library press `Alt` and right-click and select Bookmark.
Kanzi Studio creates a bookmark and sets its Target property to the item from which you created the bookmark.
## Accessing a bookmarked item[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#accessing-a-bookmarked-item "Link to this heading")
To access a bookmarked item, in the Library > Bookmarks double-click the bookmark of the item you want to access.
Kanzi Studio takes you to the bookmarked item.
## Changing the target of a bookmark[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#changing-the-target-of-a-bookmark "Link to this heading")
To change the item to which a bookmark points, in the Library select the bookmark, and in the Properties set the Target property to the item you want the bookmark to point to.
##  Bookmark property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#bookmark-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for bookmarks, see [Bookmark](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/bookmark-reference.html).
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Using aliases](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/aliases/using-aliases.html)

# Using brushes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#using-brushes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Brushes are graphics objects that describe how 2D content is drawn.
Use Brushes to set the appearance of the foreground and background of 2D nodes. For example, with brushes you can define the color of text in a Text Block 2D node, fill a background of a 2D node with an image pattern, or apply a material effect on 2D content.
Most 2D nodes have a foreground and a background. With brushes you can change the appearance of both.
These brushes are available in Kanzi:
  * Color Brush to fill a 2D node with a solid color.
See [Filling 2D nodes with a solid color](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-solid-color).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png)
  * Texture Brush to fill a 2D node with a texture.
See [Filling 2D nodes with a texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-texture).
![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png)
  * Material Brush to fill a 2D node with a material.
See [Filling 2D nodes with a material](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-material).
![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)


Kanzi Studio stores brushes in the Library > Materials and Textures > Brushes.
![../../_images/brushes-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/brushes-in-library.png)
For example, with the brushes you can:
  * Set the color of 2D text. See [Setting the color of text in 2D text nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#setting-the-color-of-text-in-2d-text-nodes).
![../../_images/text.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text.png)
  * Define the appearance of brushes in different application states. See [Controlling the appearance of brushes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#controlling-the-appearance-of-brushes).
![../../_images/brush-appearance.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/brush-appearance.png)
  * Create post-processing effects for 2D nodes. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#applying-custom-rendering-to-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)


## Filling 2D nodes with a solid color[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-solid-color "Link to this heading")
Use a Color Brush to fill a 2D node with a solid color.
To fill a 2D node with a solid color:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures, select Color Brush, and name the brush.
![../../_images/library-create-color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-create-color-brush.png) ![../../_images/dark-gray-color-brush-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dark-gray-color-brush-in-library.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select the 2D node that you want to fill with the brush you created, in the Properties add the Background Brush or the Foreground Brush property, and select the brush you created in the first step.
For example, create a Button 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and set it to the brush you created in the first step.
![../../_images/button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d.png) ![../../_images/button-2d-background-brush-set-to-dark-gray.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-background-brush-set-to-dark-gray.png)
  3. In the Properties click ![quick-edit-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) next to the property you added in the previous step and set the color of the color brush you created in the previous step.
In the Preview you can see that the Color Brush you created fills the node for which you set the property.
![../../_images/appearance-quick-set-color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/appearance-quick-set-color-brush.png)
Tip
To quickly edit a brush, in the Properties next to the Background Brush or Foreground Brush property click ![quick-edit-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) and edit the brush.
![../../_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png)


## Filling 2D nodes with a texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-texture "Link to this heading")
Use a Texture Brush to fill a 2D node with a texture.
To fill a 2D node with a texture:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures, select Texture Brush, and name the brush.
![../../_images/create-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-texture-brush.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select the 2D node that you want to fill with the brush you created, in the Properties add the Background Brush or the Foreground Brush property, and select the brush you created in the first step.
For example, create a Grid Layout 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and set it to the brush you created in the first step.
![../../_images/grid-layout-2d-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout-2d-in-project.png) ![../../_images/grid-layout-2d-background-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout-2d-background-texture-brush.png)
  3. In the Properties click ![go-to-item](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/go-to-selected-item.png) next to the property that you added in the previous step to go to the brush used by that property, set the texture you want this texture brush to use, and adjust how the Texture Brush uses that texture:
     * Brush Modulate Color sets the modulation color for the brush.
     * Brush Horizontal Tiling affects the scale of the texture coordinates to set the horizontal tiling of the texture.
     * Brush Vertical Tiling affects the scale of the texture coordinates to set the vertical tiling of the texture.
     * Brush Texture sets the texture for the brush.
![../../_images/go-to-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/go-to-texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush-properties.png)


## Filling 2D nodes with a material[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-material "Link to this heading")
Use a Material Brush to fill a 2D node with a material.
To fill a 2D node with a material:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures, select Material Brush, and name the brush.
![../../_images/create-material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-material-brush.png)
  2. In the Properties set the Material property to the material you want to use to fill a 2D node.
If you do not have any materials in your project, create a material. See [Creating a material](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-materials.html#creating-a-material).
![../../_images/material-brush-set-material-to-colortexturematerial.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush-set-material-to-colortexturematerial.png) ![../../_images/colortexturematerial-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/colortexturematerial-properties.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the 2D node that you want to fill with the brush you created, in the Properties add the Background Brush or the Foreground Brush property, and select the brush you created in the first step.
For example, create a Button 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and set it to the brush you created in the first step.
![../../_images/button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d.png) ![../../_images/button-2d-properties-and-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-properties-and-preview.png)
  4. To adjust the appearance of the material, set the Material properties either in:
     * The Material Brush.
For example, to change the ambient color, texture, and blending of the material for the Material Brush, add and set the Ambient Color, Texture, and Blend Mode properties.
![../../_images/set-material-properties-in-material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-material-properties-in-material-brush.png)
     * The node which uses the Material Brush.
For example, to change the ambient color, texture, and blending of the material for a node, add and set the Ambient Color, Texture, and Blend Mode properties in that node.
![../../_images/set-material-properties-in-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-material-properties-in-node.png)


## Setting the color of text in 2D text nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#setting-the-color-of-text-in-2d-text-nodes "Link to this heading")
To set the color of text in a Text Block 2D or Text Box 2D node:
  1. In the Node Tree create or select a Text Block 2D or Text Box 2D node.
![../../_images/select-text-block-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-text-block-2d.png)
  2. In the Properties add the Foreground Brush property.
![../../_images/add-foreground-brush-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-foreground-brush-property.png)
  3. Set the Foreground Brush property to an existing Color Brush or select + Color Brush, name the brush, click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) next to the property, and set the color of the Color Brush you created.
![../../_images/select-and-set-color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-and-set-color-brush.png)
Tip
To quickly edit a brush, in the Properties next to the Background Brush or Foreground Brush property click ![quick-edit-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) and edit the brush.
![../../_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png)


## Controlling the appearance of brushes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#controlling-the-appearance-of-brushes "Link to this heading")
You can define the appearance of brushes in different application states. For example, when you use a brush to fill a Button 2D node, you can change the appearance of the brush when the user presses the button.
To control the appearance of a brush, create a state manager which sets the properties of the brush in the node which uses the brush.
To control the appearance of a brush:
  1. Create a brush and use it to fill a 2D node.
For example, create a texture brush and set the Background Brush property of a Button 2D node to the texture brush that you created. See [Filling 2D nodes with a texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-texture).
![../../_images/my-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/button-2d-with-background-my-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-with-background-my-texture-brush.png)
  2. Create a state manager which you use to control the appearance of the brush that you created in the first step.
For example:
    1. Create for the Button 2D node a state manager that has two states named Released and Pressed and set the state manager to use the Button > Is Down controller property. See [Using a state manager to set button states](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#using-a-state-manager-to-set-button-states).
![../../_images/button-2d-state-manager-for-setting-texture-brush-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-state-manager-for-setting-texture-brush-properties.png)
    2. Set the appearance of the brush in the Released and Pressed states.
For example, in the Properties next to the Background Brush property click ![quick-edit-properties](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png), set the Brush Modulate Color property, and in the State Tools click ![store-current-values](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/store-current-values.png) in the Pressed state to save the property value to the Pressed state.
![../../_images/my-texture-brush-set-properties-for-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-texture-brush-set-properties-for-state.png) ![../../_images/set-brush-properties-to-pressed-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-brush-properties-to-pressed-state.png)


Now when you interact with the node in the Preview, Kanzi changes the appearance of the brush that you created.
## Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#applying-custom-rendering-to-2d-nodes "Link to this heading")
Apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects.
For example, you can convert color images in a 2D node to grayscale.
To apply custom rendering to a 2D node, use the Composition Brush property to compose the node on the screen with a Material Brush, and enable the Force Composition property.
To apply custom rendering to a 2D node:
  1. Create a material with which you want to apply custom rendering.
For example, to create a material that converts color to grayscale:
    1. In the Library, press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures and select Material Type. Kanzi Studio creates a material type and a material that uses the material type.
![../../_images/create-material-type.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-material-type.png) ![../../_images/material-type-and-its-material-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-type-and-its-material-in-library.png)
    2. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Material Types, expand the material type that you created. Double-click the Vertex Shader to open it in the Shader Source Editor, replace the existing shader code with this code, and save the shader.

```
#version 310 es

in vec3 kzPosition;
in vec2 kzTextureCoordinate0;
uniform highp mat4 kzProjectionCameraWorldMatrix;

out mediump vec2 vTexCoord;

void main()
{
    precision mediump float;
    vTexCoord = kzTextureCoordinate0;
    gl_Position = kzProjectionCameraWorldMatrix * vec4(kzPosition.xyz, 1.0);
}

```
Copy to clipboard
    3. Open the Fragment Shader, replace the existing shader code with the code in this step, and save the shader.
In the shader, use these Kanzi default uniforms:
       * `ContentTexture` to define the texture that the rendered node provides when rendering
       * `RenderOpacity` to define the opacity of the rendered node
See [Shader uniforms](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/editing-shaders.html#shader-uniforms).

```
#version 310 es

uniform sampler2D ContentTexture;
in mediump vec2 vTexCoord;
uniform lowp float RenderOpacity;
layout(location = 0) out vec4 fragColor;

void main()
{
    precision mediump float;
    // Use this algorithm to convert the colors in the texture used by
    // the 2D node to grayscale.
    // To integrate to the Kanzi rendering pipeline, the shader must output
    // premultiplied alpha.
    vec4 color = texture(ContentTexture, vTexCoord);
    float grayscale = dot(color.rgb, vec3(0.21, 0.72, 0.07));
    float alpha = color.a * RenderOpacity;
    vec3 premultipliedColor = vec3(grayscale) * alpha;
    fragColor = vec4(premultipliedColor, alpha);
}

```
Copy to clipboard
  2. In the Library, press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures and select Material Brush. In the Properties, set the Material property to the material that you created in the previous step.
![../../_images/create-material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-material-brush.png) ![../../_images/set-material-to-material-type-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-material-to-material-type-material.png)
  3. In the Node Tree, create or select a 2D node to which you want to apply the material that you created. For example, create a Stack Layout 2D node. In the Stack Layout 2D node, create an Image node.
![../../_images/stack-layout-with-image-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-with-image-node.png)
  4. In the Properties, add and set:
     * Brush Composition Brush to the material brush that uses the material you want to apply to that node
     * Node 2D > Force Composition to enabled
     * (Optional) Render Target > Multisample Level to the number of anti-aliasing samples that you want to apply to the content
     * (Optional) Node > Opacity to control the translucency of the node
![../../_images/stack-layout-with-applied-composition-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-with-applied-composition-brush.png)


## Using brushes in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#using-brushes-in-the-api "Link to this heading")

Use the Camera node to show the content of a Scene in Kanzi Studio Preview and in your Kanzi application.
To change the view of a Scene, you can use several Camera nodes and set them in different ways, but you can use only one Camera node at a time to view a scene. In each Scene, use the Camera property to set the camera that you want to use for the final view of your Kanzi application.
In the Preview, a grey movie camera pictograph represents the camera node. The lens of the camera is the point of view from which the content of a Scene is shown.
Tip
To see Camera nodes in the Preview, click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to enter the Analyze mode, right-click ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png), and select Debug objects.
![../../_images/camera1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera1.png)
When you create a Kanzi Studio project, the Viewport 2D > Scene node contains a Camera node that shows that Scene in the Preview. See [Using the Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html).

You can set 3D nodes to automatically turn towards a Camera node.
For example, the Plane nodes in the top image automatically turn towards the default camera of the Scene node, while the bottom image shows the same scene, but the nodes do not turn towards a Camera node.
![../../_images/face-to-camera-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/face-to-camera-enabled.png) ![../../_images/face-to-camera-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/face-to-camera-disabled.png)
To make nodes turn to a Camera node:
  1. In the Node Tree select the nodes that you want to automatically turn to a Camera node and in the Properties add and set the Constraints > Face to Camera Mode property.
When you set the Face to Camera Mode property, Kanzi by default sets the default camera of the Scene node as the target camera towards which the nodes turn.
![../../_images/plane-grid-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/plane-grid-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/face-to-camera-mode.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/face-to-camera-mode.png)  
| Look at sets the nodes to rotate along all axes to turn to the target camera.  |  ![../../_images/face-to-camera-look-at.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/face-to-camera-look-at.png)  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Billboarding sets the nodes to rotate with the rotation of the target camera, keeping the nodes rotated perpendicular to the field of view of the target camera.  |  ![../../_images/face-to-camera-billboarding-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/face-to-camera-billboarding-enabled.png)  |  
| Cylindrical sets the nodes to turn to the target camera so that they turn around an imaginary cylinder on the y axis, but do not rotate along the x axis.  |  ![../../_images/face-to-camera-cylindrical.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/face-to-camera-cylindrical.png)  |  
  2. (Optional) To make any camera in the Scene node the target camera, in the Properties add the Constraints > Face to Camera Target Camera property, and set it to the Camera node towards which you want the nodes to turn.
![../../_images/face-to-camera-target-camera.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/face-to-camera-target-camera.png)

# Color workflow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#color-workflow "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
## Linear and nonlinear gamma color spaces[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#linear-and-nonlinear-gamma-color-spaces "Link to this heading")
The purpose of the sRGB color space is to represent colors for display on computer monitors. Currently sRGB is the standard for the nonlinear gamma color space. It is needed because human perception of light is nonlinear, and computer monitors have a nonlinear response to light intensity.
The human eye distinguishes between darker shades better than lighter shades. For this reason it makes sense to preserve more accuracy for dark intensities when storing and displaying images on screens. The nonlinear gamma color space achieves this with gamma correction, which puts the intensity of each pixel in an image through a power function:
Iγ
Images are usually stored with an encoding gamma applied to them, and screens apply a decoding gamma. This image shows the graphs of the gamma transfer functions that Kanzi uses to convert between the linear and gamma color spaces.
![../../_images/gamma.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/gamma.svg)
This image shows a gradient where the intensity of the light emitted by your screen increases linearly.
![../../_images/linear_emitted_intensity.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linear_emitted_intensity.png)
Applying a decoding gamma to the above gradient results in this gradient where the perceptual light intensity increases linearly.
![../../_images/linear_perceptual_intensity.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linear_perceptual_intensity.png)
The problem with the nonlinear gamma color space is its unsuitability for graphics operations. Performing color calculations in nonlinear space leads to inaccurate results in color and alpha blending. Linear color space is needed for mathematically correct lighting and color blending calculations.
In linear color space numerical intensity values correspond to their actual intensity, which makes it possible to add and multiply color values correctly. Linear color space rendering provides more accurate results and more realistic surface shading, particularly with physically based rendering techniques.
These images show an example of blending in nonlinear gamma (left) and linear (right) color space. Blending in nonlinear gamma color space results in overly bright blends and saturated bands.
[![../../_images/legacy-blending.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/legacy-blending.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/legacy-blending.png) [![../../_images/linear-blending.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linear-blending.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linear-blending.png)
Kanzi by default uses the the nonlinear gamma, or standard, color workflow, where Kanzi operates on color values in the gamma color space. See [Using the standard color workflow](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#using-the-standard-color-workflow).
Kanzi also supports the linear color workflow, where Kanzi operates on color values in linear color space. See [Using the linear color workflow](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#using-the-linear-color-workflow) and [Converting applications from standard to linear color workflow](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#converting-applications-from-standard-to-linear-color-workflow).
## Using the linear color workflow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#using-the-linear-color-workflow "Link to this heading")
In the linear color workflow Kanzi enables realistic lighting computations and correct color blending. To achieve accurate rendering of color and light, Kanzi converts all color values to linear color space before performing operations on them. Kanzi then converts the color values back to the gamma color space for storage or display.
### Images[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#images "Link to this heading")
To configure the images in your Kanzi Studio project for linear color workflow:
  * In the Library > Resource Files > Images for each image resource that uses the ASTC, ETC2, JPEG, or PNG format set the value of the sRGB Content property:
    * If the image contains sRGB color information, set the sRGB Content property to enabled. This is the default setting.
If you disable the sRGB Content property for an image that contains sRGB color information, Kanzi can render the textures that use the image brighter than expected.
    * If the image contains non-color information, such as a normal, roughness, or occlusion map, set the sRGB Content property to disabled.
Textures that contain non-color information are stored in linear format. By disabling the sRGB Content property you set Kanzi to pass the image data to a shader directly, without performing a color space conversion.
![../../_images/srgb-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/srgb-content.png)
  * Kanzi by default premultiplies the alpha channel of images in linear color space. To premultiply the alpha channel in the color space of the image, in the Library > Resource Files > Images select an image and in the Properties disable the Linear Premultiply property. See [Preparing images in third-party tools](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/preparing-images-in-3rd-party-tools.html).
![../../_images/linear-premultiply.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linear-premultiply.png)


### Color property bindings[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#color-property-bindings "Link to this heading")
To set color values in binding expressions in the linear color workflow:
  * Specify `Color4` values in sRGB color space. See [color4](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#id1).
For example:

```
Color4(0, 0.75, 0.25, 1)

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/r0g192b64.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/r0g192b64.png)
  * Specify the values of individual RGB color channels in linear color space.
Use the [sRGBToLinear](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#srgbtolinear) binding function to convert a color channel value to linear color space.
For example:
    * This binding expression is equal to `Color4(0, 0.75, 0.25, 1)`:

```
color = Color4(0, 0, 0, 1)
color.g = sRGBToLinear(0.75)
color.b = sRGBToLinear(0.25)
color

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/r0g192b64.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/r0g192b64.png)
    * This binding expression is equal to `Color4(0, 0.879, 0.535, 1)`:

```
color = Color4(0, 0, 0, 1)
color.g = 0.75
color.b = 0.25
color

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/r0g225b137.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/r0g225b137.png)


### Shaders[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#shaders "Link to this heading")
In the linear color workflow shaders expect color input to be in linear color space and they output color in linear color space. To preserve accuracy when storing color values in 8-bit per channel texture formats, Kanzi converts the color values back to the sRGB color space before storing.
### Graphics API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#graphics-api "Link to this heading")
The linear color workflow needs either:
  * EGL version 1.5 or later, or EGL version 1.4 with the `EGL_KHR_gl_colorspace` extension.
  * Vulkan 1.1 or later.


## Using the standard color workflow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#using-the-standard-color-workflow "Link to this heading")
By default Kanzi uses the standard color workflow. This performs operations on color values in the nonlinear gamma color space. This provides less precise rendering results than the linear color workflow.
Use the standard color workflow when you:
  * Deploy your application to a device that does not support linear color space.
To support linear color space, your target platform must implement EGL version 1.5 or later, or EGL version 1.4 with the `EGL_KHR_gl_colorspace` extension, or Vulkan 1.1 or later.
When your Kanzi application requests linear color space but the target device does not support it, the resulting behavior varies between target platforms.
For example, your application can:
    * Print to the log a warning about lack of support for EGL_GL_COLORSPACE, and fall back to the legacy color space.
    * Terminate with this error:

```
eglCreateWindowSurface() failed: EGL_BAD_ATTRIBUTE

```
Copy to clipboard
  * Migrate a project from earlier versions of Kanzi.


In the standard color workflow Kanzi does not convert color input. If you use the Kanzi Engine API to create a `ColorRGBA[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a14966.html)` object, provide the color values in the sRGB color space.
To use the standard color workflow:
  1. Configure your application to use an unspecified color space by setting either:
     * In `application.cfg`:

```
SurfaceColorSpace = "standard"

```
Copy to clipboard
     * In the C++ application in the `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` function:

```
configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.colorSpace = "standard";

```
Copy to clipboard
See [SurfaceColorSpace](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#surfacecolorspace).
  2. In Kanzi Studio in the Project > Properties set the Color Workflow property to Standard.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/color-workflow-legacy.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-workflow-legacy.png)
  3. Write your shaders to output colors in the gamma space of your target display, which is likely sRGB. See [Shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/shaders.html).


## Converting applications from standard to linear color workflow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#converting-applications-from-standard-to-linear-color-workflow "Link to this heading")
To convert your application from the standard color workflow to the linear color workflow:
  1. Configure your application to use the sRGB color space by configuring the linear color workflow:
     * In `application.cfg`:

```
SurfaceColorSpace = "srgb"

```
Copy to clipboard
     * In the C++ application in the `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` function:

```
configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.colorSpace = "srgb";

```
Copy to clipboard
See [SurfaceColorSpace](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#surfacecolorspace).
  2. In Kanzi Studio in the Project > Properties set Color Workflow to Linear.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/color-workflow-linear.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-workflow-linear.png)
  3. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Material Types for each material type make sure that:
     * Bindings do not contain needless manually added sRGB conversions.
For example, you do not need to use the [linearTosRGB](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#lineartosrgb) binding function to convert color values from linear color space to sRGB color space. In the linear color workflow shaders expect color input to be in linear color space.
     * Shaders do not apply gamma correction at input or output.
In the linear color workflow shaders expect color input to be in linear color space and they output color in linear color space.
  4. In the Library > Resource Files > Images for each image resource that uses the ASTC, ETC2, JPEG, or PNG format check that the sRGB Content property is set correctly:
     * If the image contains sRGB color information, set the sRGB Content property to enabled. This is the default setting.
If you disable the sRGB Content property for an image that contains sRGB color information, Kanzi can render the textures that use the image brighter than expected.
     * If the image contains non-color information, such as a normal, roughness, or occlusion map, set the sRGB Content property to disabled.
Textures that contain non-color information are stored in linear format. By disabling the sRGB Content property you set Kanzi to pass the image data to a shader directly, without performing a color space conversion.
![../../_images/srgb-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/srgb-content.png)
  5. To get the desired color blending result, adjust the partially transparent colors in your project where needed.
For example, nodes filled with these color brushes look different in the standard and linear color workflow modes:
![../../_images/red-green-blue-brushes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/red-green-blue-brushes.png)  
| Standard color workflow  | Linear color workflow  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ![../../_images/color-brush-blending-legacy.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush-blending-legacy.png)  |  ![../../_images/color-brush-blending-linear.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush-blending-linear.png)  |

# Using the Content Layout nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#using-the-content-layout-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
