# Using the Click Manipulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#using-the-click-manipulator "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Click Manipulator to enable users to click nodes in your Kanzi application.
See [Enabling the click gesture for a node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#enabling-the-click-gesture-for-a-node) and [Enabling the click gesture for a node using the Kanzi Studio Preview tools](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#enabling-click-gesture).
You can react to the click gesture using:
  * Click Manipulator triggers in Kanzi Studio. See [Using the Click Manipulator triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#using-click-manipulator-triggers).
  * Kanzi Engine API. See [Reacting to the click gesture using the Kanzi Engine API](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#reacting-to-click-gesture-using-api).

![../../_images/click-manipulator.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-manipulator.gif)
The Click Manipulator is one of the input manipulators you can use to add gesture recognition to nodes in your Kanzi application. See [Using input manipulators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#using-input-manipulators).
To enable the double-click gesture for nodes, use the Multi-Click Manipulator. See [Using the Multi-Click Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/multi-click-manipulator.html).
## Enabling the click gesture for a node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#enabling-the-click-gesture-for-a-node "Link to this heading")
To enable the click gesture for a node:
  1. In the Node Tree create a node for which you want to enable the click gesture.
For example, create an Empty Node 2D node, name it ClickNode, and add content to the node.
![../../_images/clicknode-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clicknode-in-project.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select the node that you created in the previous step, in the Properties add the Input > Hit Testable property, and set it to enabled.
When you enable this property you enable the user to pick a node.
![../../_images/clicknode-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clicknode-properties.png)
  3. In the Node Components press `Alt` and right-click Input Manipulators, and select Click Manipulator.
This way you enable the ClickNode node to react to the click gesture. By adding a Click Manipulator component to a node you install a `ClickManipulator[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13162.html)` to that node.
![../../_images/add-click-manipulator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-click-manipulator.png) ![../../_images/click-manipulator-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-manipulator-properties.png)
  4. Use the Click Manipulator triggers to react to the click gesture. For example, you can change the appearance of a node when the user clicks that node.
See [Using the Click Manipulator triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#using-click-manipulator-triggers).


## Enabling the click gesture for a node using the Kanzi Studio Preview tools[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#enabling-the-click-gesture-for-a-node-using-the-ks-preview-tools "Link to this heading")
To enable the click gesture for a node using the Kanzi Studio Preview tools:
  1. Select or create a node which you want to react to clicks.
For example, create an Image node.
![../../_images/clickablenode-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clickablenode-in-project.png)
  2. In the Preview select the Node tool ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png), right-click the node which you want to react to clicks, and in the Create click trigger with action menu select an action.
For example, select the Log > Write Log action.
![../../_images/create-click-trigger-with-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-click-trigger-with-action.png)
When you create a click trigger with an action, Kanzi Studio adds to that node:
     * Input > Hit Testable property and sets it to enabled
When you enable this property you enable the user to pick a node.
See [Defining which node receives input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#defining-which-node-receives-input).
     * Click Manipulator node component
By adding a Click Manipulator component to a node you install a `ClickManipulator[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13162.html)` to that node. This way you enable the click gesture for a node.
     * Click trigger with the action that you selected
Click trigger is set off when the user presses and releases a node while the pointer is still within the node area and Kanzi does not recognize another gesture.
![../../_images/hit-testable-and-click-enabled-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/hit-testable-and-click-enabled-properties.png) ![../../_images/click-manipulator-with-trigger.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-manipulator-with-trigger.png) ![../../_images/click-trigger-with-write-log-null.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-trigger-with-write-log-null.png)
  3. In the Node Components > Triggers configure the action that the Click trigger executes when the user sets off the trigger.
For example, in the Write Log action set Log Text to the message that you want to write to the Log window when the user clicks that node.
To learn more about the Write Log action, see [Using Write Log action](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html).
![../../_images/writelog-for-clickablenode.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/writelog-for-clickablenode.png)
  4. In the Preview click ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/interact.png) to switch to the Interact mode.
In the Preview when you click the node which you set to react to clicks, the trigger executes the action that you selected in the Create click trigger with action in the Preview.


## Using the Click Manipulator triggers[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#using-the-click-manipulator-triggers "Link to this heading")
Use the Click Manipulator triggers to react to the click gesture. For example, you can change the appearance of a node when the user clicks that node.
The Click Manipulator has these triggers:
  * Click trigger is set off when the user presses and releases a node while the pointer is still within the node area and Kanzi does not recognize another gesture.
  * Begin trigger is set off when the user presses a node.
  * Cancel trigger is set off:
    * When the user first presses a node, then moves the pointer outside of the node area, and lifts the pointer.
    * When the focus moves away from the node during the click gesture.
    * When Kanzi sets off a Long Press trigger.
  * Enter trigger is set off:
    * When the user presses a node.
    * When the user presses a node, moves the pointer outside of the node area, and then moves the pointer back to the node area while still holding down the pointer.
  * Leave trigger is set off:
    * When the user presses a node and releases the press.
    * When the user sets off a Long Press trigger.
    * When the user presses a node and then moves the pointer outside of the node area.


To use the Click Manipulator triggers:
  1. Enable the click gesture for a node. See [Enabling the click gesture for a node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#enabling-the-click-gesture-for-a-node).
  2. Define the behavior that you want to set with the Click Manipulator triggers.
For example, create a state manager where you define the states which set the appearance of a node when different Click Manipulator triggers are set off. See [Creating a state manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#creating-a-state-manager).
  3. Add and configure a Click Manipulator trigger:
    1. In the Node Tree select the node to which you want to add the trigger, and in the Node Components > Triggers add one of the Click Manipulator triggers.
For example, in the Node Tree select the node for which you enabled the click gesture, in the Node Components press `Alt` and right-click Triggers, and select Message Trigger > Click > Click.
![../../_images/clicknode-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clicknode-in-project.png) ![../../_images/add-general-click-trigger.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-general-click-trigger.png)
    2. In the trigger that you created in the previous step disable the Set Message Handled property.
When you disable the Set Message Handled property, this trigger intercepts the message, but does not stop it. This way you let the input manipulator handle the message.
![../../_images/click-trigger-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-trigger-settings.png)
    3. In the Node Components press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you created, select an action, and configure it.
For example, select Dispatch Message Action > State Manager > Go to State, and in the action set:
       * Target Item to the node for which you enabled the click gesture
       * State to the state which sets the appearance of the node when the Click trigger is set off
![../../_images/click-click-click-click-go-to-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-click-click-click-go-to-state.png) ![../../_images/go-to-state-action-for-click.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/go-to-state-action-for-click.png)


## Reacting to the click gesture using the Kanzi Engine API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#reacting-to-the-click-gesture-using-the-kr-api "Link to this heading")
To react to the click gesture using the Kanzi Engine API:
  1. In Kanzi Studio create a project using the Application template.
![../../_images/create-project-with-application.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-project-with-application.png)
  2. Enable the click gesture for a node. See [Enabling the click gesture for a node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#enabling-the-click-gesture-for-a-node).
When you enable the click gesture for a node in Kanzi Studio, you create in that node a `ClickManipulatorComponent[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a19022.html)`, which installs to the node a `ClickManipulator[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13162.html)`.
  3. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node that you created and select Alias.
Kanzi Studio creates an alias pointing to the node from which you created the alias and adds it to the resource dictionary of its nearest ancestor node that contains a resource dictionary.
Access alias target nodes using the `#` sign followed by the name of the alias.
![../../_images/clicknode-create-alias.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clicknode-create-alias.png) ![../../_images/clicknode-in-dictionaries.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clicknode-in-dictionaries.png)
  4. Select File > Export > Export KZB.
Kanzi Studio creates the kzb file and configuration files from your Kanzi Studio project. Kanzi Studio stores the exported files in the `<ProjectName>/Application/bin` directory or the location that you set in Project > Properties in the Binary Export Directory property. The kzb file contains all nodes and resources from your Kanzi Studio project, except the resources that you mark in a localization table as locale packs.
When you run your Kanzi application from Visual Studio, your application loads the kzb file and configuration files.
![../../_images/export-kzb-binary.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-kzb-binary.png)
  5. In Kanzi Studio, select File > Open Kanzi Command Prompt.
The Kanzi Command Prompt opens the Windows Command Prompt with the Kanzi environment variables set for the version of Kanzi for which you open a Kanzi Command Prompt.
Use the Kanzi Command Prompt to access Kanzi utilities and build tools, such as Gradle and CMake, without using absolute paths or setting environment variables.
![../../_images/open-kanzi-command-prompt.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-kanzi-command-prompt.png)
Tip
You can find the Kanzi Command Prompt in the Windows Start Menu in the Rightware directory.
When you have more than one version of Kanzi installed, make sure that you launch a Kanzi Command Prompt for the version of Kanzi with which you want to work in that command prompt.
  6. In the Kanzi Command Prompt in the `<ProjectName>/Application` directory, run the script that generates a Visual Studio solution for the application.

```
generate_cmake_vs2022_solution.bat

```
Copy to clipboard
This script generates a Visual Studio solution for the application in the directory `<ProjectName>/Application/build_vs2022`.
  7. In Visual Studio open the `<ProjectName>/Application/build_vs<Version>/<ProjectName>.sln` Visual Studio solution and in the file that implements the logic of your application configure the `ClickManipulator[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13162.html)`:
    1. Define the handlers for different click messages. In each handler add the code that defines the behavior for a specific click event.
You can define the behavior also in Kanzi Studio using the Click Manipulator triggers. See [Using the Click Manipulator triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#using-click-manipulator-triggers).
For example, to define handlers for the `ClickManipulator::ClickMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13162.html#a5ec459cf339d2a9fa47a77a1e245cb8c)` and `ClickManipulator::ClickCancelMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13162.html#a7b9cd5c8924d8715ce9fbd5dc53f3461)` messages, after the public section of the class which implements the logic of your application add:

```
private:
    // Define the handler for the ClickManipulator::ClickMessage message from the nodes
    // that have an input manipulator which generates the ClickMessage message.
    void onNodeClicked(ClickManipulator::ClickMessageArguments&)
    {
        // Add the code that handles the click event.
    }

    // Define the handler for the ClickManipulator::ClickCancelMessage message from the nodes
    // that have an input manipulator which generates the ClickCancelMessage message.
    void onNodeClickCanceled(ClickManipulator::ClickCancelMessageArguments&)
    {
        // Add the code that handles the click cancel event.
    }

```
Copy to clipboard
    2. In the `Application::onProjectLoaded[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a4bfecf9d67bcbf85c1eecfafa8129d22)` function subscribe to the `ClickManipulator[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13162.html)` messages.
For example, add:

```
void onProjectLoaded() override
{
    ScreenSharedPtr screen = getScreen();

    // Get the ClickNode node using its alias.
    NodeSharedPtr clickNode = screen->lookupNode<Node>("#ClickNode");

    // Subscribe to the ClickManipulator::ClickMessage message at the ClickNode node.
    // The ClickManipulator manipulator generates this message when the user clicks the node.
    clickNode->addMessageHandler(ClickManipulator::ClickMessage, bind(&MyProject::onNodeClicked, this, placeholders::_1));

    // Subscribe to the ClickManipulator::ClickCancelMessage message at the ClickNode node.
    // The ClickManipulator manipulator generates this message when the user first presses down
    // the node, then moves the pointer outside of the node area, and lifts the pointer.
    clickNode->addMessageHandler(ClickManipulator::ClickCancelMessage, bind(&MyProject::onNodeClickCanceled, this, placeholders::_1));
}

```
Copy to clipboard
  8. Build and run your application. See [Deploying Kanzi applications](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/deploying-applications/deploying-kanzi-applications.html).
In the application:
     * Click the node for which you enabled the click gesture. The application executes the behavior you defined in the handler for the `ClickManipulator::ClickMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13162.html#a5ec459cf339d2a9fa47a77a1e245cb8c)` message.
     * Press down the node for which you enabled the click gesture, then move the pointer outside of the node area, and lift the pointer. The application executes the behavior you defined in the handler for the `ClickManipulator::ClickCancelMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13162.html#a7b9cd5c8924d8715ce9fbd5dc53f3461)` message.


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Handling user input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html)
[Using the Multi-Click Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/multi-click-manipulator.html)
[Using the Long-Press Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/long-press-manipulator.html)
[Deploying Kanzi applications](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/deploying-applications/deploying-kanzi-applications.html)
[Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html)

# Using the Empty Node nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#using-the-empty-node-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Empty Node nodes to group nodes and to set property values of their child nodes.
By default, Empty Node nodes do not have a visual representation, or any functionality other than a transparent background and that they can act as a parent node to other nodes. Empty Node nodes do not have any properties specific only to them.
For example, use Empty Node nodes to:
  * Edit the origin of nodes. See [Editing the origin of nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/editing-the-origin-of-nodes.html).
  * Apply transformation to all its child nodes. See [Tutorial: Create reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/reflections/reflections.html).
  * Replace the root node of a node prefab. See [Replacing the root node of a node prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#replacing-the-root-node-of-a-node-prefab).


An Empty Node is a node into which you can put any other node and has these properties:
  * It allows absolute positioning of its child nodes.
  * Does not restrict the movement of its child nodes.
  * Is not a compacting layout.


Empty Node does not have inherent layout characteristics. Empty Node does not resize its child nodes, but places them to a position you specify. The default values of the Layout Height and Layout Width properties of an Empty Node are 0, but it stretches by default to take all the space its child nodes need.
You can use the Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment properties to align the child nodes of an Empty Node only after you specify the Layout Height and Layout Width properties of that Empty Node.
## Creating an Empty Node node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#creating-an-empty-node-node "Link to this heading")
To create an Empty Node node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create an Empty Node node and select either Empty Node 3D, or Empty Node 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
  2. In the Node Tree add items to the Empty Node node.
For example, if you created an Empty Node 3D node, add Sphere nodes, if you created an Empty Node 2D node, add Image nodes.
  3. (Optional) In the Node Tree select the Empty Node node, in the Properties click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png), add and set the property you want all its child nodes to inherit.


## Setting the appearance of an Empty Node 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#setting-the-appearance-of-an-empty-node-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png)


## Using the Empty Node 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#using-the-empty-node-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create an Empty Node 3D node using the API:

```
// Create an Empty Node 3D named Empty3D
EmptyNode3DSharedPtr emptyNode = EmptyNode3D::create(domain, "Empty3D");

// Create and add a cube to the Empty Node 3D
ModelSharedPtr cube = Model::createCube(domain, "Cube", 1.0f, KanziThemeOrange);
emptyNode->addChild(cube);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `EmptyNode3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13750.html)` class.
## Using the Empty Node 2D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#using-the-empty-node-2d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create an Empty Node 2D node using the API:

```
// Create an Empty Node 2D named Empty2D
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr empty2D = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty2D");

// Create and add an Image to the Empty Node 2D
ImageSharedPtr image = Image::create(domain, "Image");
image->setTextureResourceID(ResourceID("DefaultTexture"));
empty2D->addChild(image);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `EmptyNode2D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13746.html)` class.
##  Empty Node property types and messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#empty-node-property-types-and-messages "Link to this heading")
For lists of the available property types and messages for the Empty Node nodes, see [Empty Node 2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/empty-node-2d-reference.html) and [Empty Node 3D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/empty-node-3d-reference.html).
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Property system](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/kanzi-fundamentals/property-system.html)
[Property types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/property-types.html)
[Tutorial: Create reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/reflections/reflections.html)
[Editing the origin of nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/editing-the-origin-of-nodes.html)
[Using node prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html)

# Editing the origin of nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/editing-the-origin-of-nodes.html#editing-the-origin-of-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use an Empty Node node to set the origin of 3D and 2D nodes and to create an external transformation pivot point. This is particularly useful when you want to edit the origin of a mesh, but want to keep the pivot point centered to the mesh.
When the pivot point of a mesh is centered to the mesh, you can use the half-float accuracy for the vertex attributes. When you use half-float accuracy for vertex attributes, instead of float, you decrease the mesh data size by half.
To set the origin of a 2D node you can also use the Render Transformation Origin property
For example, edit the origin of a node when you want to reposition the pivot point of a gauge needle.
To edit the origin of a node to create an external transformation point:
  1. In the Node Tree create an Empty Node node and add to it a node the origin of which you want to edit.
For example, use a Box, a Sphere, a Plane, or a Model that points to the mesh whose origin you want to edit.
![../../_images/needle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/needle.png) ![../../_images/needle-initial-position.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/needle-initial-position.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select the node the origin of which you want to edit and do either of these:
     * In the Properties add and set the Render Transformation property to place the node to the position of the new origin.
For example, if the node is 4 units wide and you want to set the origin of the node to the rightmost side of the node, set the Render Transformation Translation X property field to -2.
![../../_images/needle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/needle.png) ![../../_images/position-needle-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/position-needle-properties.png)
     * In the Preview select the Node tool ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png), set the target transformation to Render Transformation (![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-transformation-render-transformation.png)), and use the Node tool to place the node to the position of the new origin. See [Editing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html).
![../../_images/position-needle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/position-needle.png)
  3. To use the new origin of the node, target the Empty Node node that contains the node whose origin you edited.
For example, to animate the node around the new origin, animate the Empty Node node. See [Using keyframe animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/triggering-animations-with-the-play-animation-action.html).
  4. (Optional) To position the node whose origin you edited, in the Node Tree select the Empty Node and do either of these:
     * In the Properties add and set the Render Transformation property to place the Empty Node node where you want to position its child nodes.
![../../_images/empty-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/empty-node.png) ![../../_images/position-empty-node-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/position-empty-node-properties.png)
     * In the Preview select the Node tool ![image2](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png), set the target transformation to Render Transformation (![image3](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-transformation-render-transformation.png)), and use the Node tool to place the Empty Node node where you want to position its child nodes.
![../../_images/position-empty-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/position-empty-node.png)


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/editing-the-origin-of-nodes.html#sa "Link to this heading")

#  Factory Content assets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#factory-content-assets "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
The Factory Content asset packages contain ready-made components and materials that you can use to create prototype projects faster.
Here you can find all the Factory Content assets:
  * 2D interactivity control components that you can use to make your application interactive. See [Interactivity control components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#interactivity-control-components).
  * Progress components that you can use to indicate that a task is in progress. See [Progress components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-components).
  * List components that you can use to present collections of items arranged in scrollable lists. See [List components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#list-components).
  * Complete user interface components that you can use to add functionality to your application. See [Complete user interface components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#complete-user-interface-components).
  * Materials that you can apply to 3D content in your project. See [Materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#materials).
  * Render Passes that you can use to add effects to your project. See [Render Passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#render-passes).


To use the Factory Content assets in your Kanzi Studio project, from the Asset Packages drag an asset to a node in the Node Tree, to the Prefabs, or to the Preview. See [Using the Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html).
![../../_images/asset-packages-factory-content-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-factory-content-selected.png)
## Interactivity control components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#interactivity-control-components "Link to this heading")
Use 2D interactivity control components to make your application interactive.
###  Button[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#button "Link to this heading")
Use the Button to create a button that receives user input.
![../../_images/button.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button.gif)
To adjust the appearance and behavior of the Button, after you add the Button to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Label to set the text in the button.
  * Main Color to set the color of the button background.
  * Highlight Color to set the color of the button background when the user presses the button.
  * Border Color to set the color of the button border that is visible when the user presses the button.
  * Border Thickness to set the width of the button border that is visible when the user presses the button.
  * Rounding Radius to set the roundness of the button corners.
For example, to make the button corners right-angle, set Rounding Radius to 0.

![../../_images/button-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-properties.png)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the button reacts to user input. See [Using the Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
The Button uses a state manager that sets the appearance and behavior of the Button when:
  * The user presses the button.
  * The value of the Enabled property changes.
When you disable the Enabled property in the Button node, the button does not react to user input.
![../../_images/node-enabled-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-enabled-disabled.png)


###  Checkbox[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#checkbox "Link to this heading")
Use the Checkbox to create a checkbox that receives user input.
![../../_images/checkbox.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/checkbox.gif)
The Checkbox uses a state manager that sets the appearance and behavior of the Checkbox when:
  * The user toggles the checkbox.
  * The value of the Enabled property changes.
When you disable the Enabled property in the Checkbox node, the checkbox does not react to user input.
![../../_images/node-enabled-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-enabled-disabled.png)


###  Radio Buttons[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#radio-buttons "Link to this heading")
Use the Radio Buttons to create radio buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/radio-buttons.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/radio-buttons.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how radio buttons react to user input. See [Using the Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
###  Slider[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#slider "Link to this heading")
Use the Slider to create a slider that receives user input.
![../../_images/slider1.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider1.gif)
To adjust the appearance and behavior of the Slider, after you add the Slider to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Maximum Value to set the highest value of the slider. The default value is 100.
  * Minimum Value to set the lowest value of the slider. The default value is 0.
  * Step Value to set the increment by which the knob moves on the rail. The default value is 1.
  * Value to set the initial position of the knob on the rail. You can use bindings to control another property with the position of the slider. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
  * Knob Style to set the shape of the knob to square or circle, or to not show the knob.
  * Knob Size to set the size of the knob.
  * Knob Color to set the color of the knob.
  * Rail Thickness to set the thickness of the rail.
  * Rail Rounded Ends to set whether to round the ends of the rail.
  * Rail Background Color to set the color of the rail from the knob until the end of the rail.
  * Rail Fill Color to set the color of the rail from the start of the rail until the knob.

![../../_images/slider-range-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-range-properties1.png) ![../../_images/slider-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-properties.png)
The Slider uses a state manager that sets the appearance and behavior of the slider when the value of the Enabled property changes. When you disable the Enabled property in the Slider node, the slider does not react to user input.
![../../_images/node-enabled-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-enabled-disabled.png)
###  Toggle Button[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#toggle-button "Link to this heading")
Use the Toggle Button to create a toggle button that receives user input.
![../../_images/toggle-button.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-button.gif)
The Toggle Button uses a state manager that sets the appearance of the Toggle Button when the user toggles it.
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the toggle button reacts to user input. See [Using the Toggle Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
## Progress components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-components "Link to this heading")
Use the progress components to show that a task is in progress.
###  Processing Indicator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#processing-indicator "Link to this heading")
Use the Processing Indicator to show that the application is processing a task.
![../../_images/processing-indicator.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/processing-indicator.gif)
To adjust the appearance of the Processing Indicator, after you add the Processing Indicator to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Color to set the color of the processing indicator.
  * Masked to set whether to mask the processing indicator with the texture that you set using the Masking Texture property.
  * Masking Texture to a texture to use to mask the processing indicator.
In the masking texture:
    * Black pixels form the mask that hides areas of the processing indicator.
    * White pixels form the gaps in the mask that show areas of the processing indicator.
By default the Processing Indicator is masked by a texture that shows a ring of circles.
  * Offset to set the rotation angle of the processing indicator.
  * Step Count to set the number of segments in the processing indicator.

![../../_images/processing-indicator-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/processing-indicator-properties.png)
###  Progress Bar[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-bar "Link to this heading")
Use the Progress Bar to show that a task is in progress, expressed both visually and as a percentage.
![../../_images/progress-bar.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-bar.gif)
To set the value of the Progress Bar, in the Properties set the value of the Progress property. You can use bindings to control the Progress property. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
To set the length of the gradient in the end of the progress bar, in the Properties set the value of the Smoothing property.
![../../_images/progress-bar-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-bar-properties.png)
###  Progress Indicator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-indicator "Link to this heading")
Use the Progress Indicator to show that a task is in progress, expressed both visually and as a percentage.
![../../_images/progress-indicator.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-indicator.gif)
To set the value of the Progress Indicator, in the Properties set the value of the Progress property. You can use bindings to control the Progress property. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
To adjust the appearance of the Progress Indicator, after you add the Progress Indicator to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Brush Color to set the color of the progress indicator ring.
  * Progress Smoothness to set the length of the gradient in the end of the progress indicator.
  * Ring Smoothness to set the edge smoothness of the progress indicator ring.
  * Ring Thickness to set the width of the progress indicator ring.

![../../_images/progress-indicator-brush-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-indicator-brush-color.png) ![../../_images/progress-indicator-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-indicator-properties1.png)
## List components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#list-components "Link to this heading")
Use the list components to present collections of items arranged in scrollable lists.
Each list component uses a List Box node to arrange its items. See [List Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html).
Use a data source to display your own data in a list component. See [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html), and [Tutorial: Get application data from a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-sources/data-sources.html).
###  Contact List[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#contact-list "Link to this heading")
Use the Contact List to create a contact list that shows the name, profile picture, and phone number for each contact.
![../../_images/contact-list.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contact-list.gif)
To set the content and behavior of the Contact List, in the Properties add and set:
  * Items Source to provide a data source for the list items.
  * Selection Behavior to set whether the list box brings an item to the center of the list box area when the user selects that item.

![../../_images/items-source-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/items-source-property.png) ![../../_images/selection-behavior-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-behavior-property.png)
###  Cover Flow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#cover-flow "Link to this heading")
Use the Cover Flow to present album covers.
![../../_images/cover-flow.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cover-flow.gif)
To set the content and behavior of the Cover Flow, in the Node Tree or Prefabs select the Cover Flow > Scene> Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties add and set:
  * Items Source to provide a data source for the list items.
  * Selection Behavior to set whether the list box brings an item to the center of the list box area when the user selects that item.

![../../_images/items-source-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/items-source-property.png) ![../../_images/selection-behavior-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-behavior-property.png)
###  Poster Flow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#poster-flow "Link to this heading")
Use the Poster Flow to present media posters.
![../../_images/poster-flow.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/poster-flow.gif)
To adjust the roundness of poster corners, in the Prefabs select the Poster prefab and in the Properties set the Rounding Radius property.
![../../_images/poster-flow-rounding-radius.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/poster-flow-rounding-radius.png)
To set the content and behavior of the Poster Flow, in the Node Tree or Prefabs select the Poster Flow > Scene> Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties add and set:
  * Items Source to provide a data source for the list items.
  * Selection Behavior to set whether the list box brings an item to the center of the list box area when the user selects that item.

![../../_images/items-source-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/items-source-property.png) ![../../_images/selection-behavior-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-behavior-property.png)
## Complete user interface components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#complete-user-interface-components "Link to this heading")
Factory Content includes complete user interface components that you can use to add functionality to your application.
###  Car[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#car "Link to this heading")
Use the Car to add a car model.
![../../_images/car-asset.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-asset.png)
To position the car, in the Preview use either the Node tool or the Camera tool. See [Editing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html) and [Using the Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html).
To set the material for the different parts of the car, you can drag materials from the Assets window to the Car in the Preview window. See [Using the Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html).
###  Music Player[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#music-player "Link to this heading")
Use the Music Player to create a music player with buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/music-player.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/music-player.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the Music Player buttons react to user input. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
###  Navigation Bar[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#navigation-bar "Link to this heading")
Use the Navigation Bar to create a navigation bar with toggle buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/navigation-bar.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-bar.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the Navigation Bar buttons react to user input. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html)
###  Notification Popup[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#notification-popup "Link to this heading")
Use the Notification Popup to create a notification dialog with buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/notification-popup.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/notification-popup.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the Notification Popup buttons react to user input. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
###  Traditional Gauges[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#traditional-gauges "Link to this heading")
Use the Traditional Gauges to create a car cluster with speed, RPM, fuel, and temperature gauges.
![../../_images/traditional-gauges.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/traditional-gauges.gif)
To control the visibility of the speed and RPM gauges, in the Properties add and set the Gauge State property.
To move the indicators, in the Properties add and set:
  * Fuel to move the fuel indicator.
  * RPM to move the RPM indicator.
  * Speed to move the speed indicator.
  * Temperature to move the temperature indicator.

![../../_images/gauges-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/gauges-properties.png)
## Materials[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#materials "Link to this heading")
Factory Content includes materials that you can apply to 3D content in your project.
![../../_images/aluminium.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/aluminium.png)
Aluminium Material
Uses normal map textures.
![../../_images/car-paint-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-paint-material.png)
Car Paint Material
![../../_images/carbon-fiber-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/carbon-fiber-material.png)
Carbon Fiber Material
Uses normal map textures.
![../../_images/chrome-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/chrome-material.png)
Chrome Material
![../../_images/glass-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/glass-material.png)
Glass Material
![../../_images/leather-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/leather-material.png)
Leather Material
Uses normal map textures.
![../../_images/mask-texture-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-texture-material.png)
Mask Texture Material
![../../_images/rubber-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rubber-material.png)
Rubber Material
Uses normal map textures.
To learn about using Factory Content materials in your Kanzi application, see [Using Factory Content materials in your project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html#using-fc-materials).
## Render Passes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#render-passes "Link to this heading")
Factory Content includes render passes that you can use to add effects to your project.
###  Skybox render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#skybox-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Use the Skybox render pass to draw a Cubemap as a background into your Scene.
![../../_images/skybox-asset.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/skybox-asset.gif)
To set up the Skybox render pass
  * In Asset Packages > Factory Content, right-click Skybox and select Import to bring the package as a prefab in to the Library > Render Pass Prefabs folder.
  * If you do not have a custom Render Pass Prefab selected in your Viewport 2D, in Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs, right-click and Create > Default render pass. In the Properties of your Viewport 2D, set the Default render pass as the value of the Render Pass Prefab property.
  * In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs, drag the Skybox render pass from its root node under the Draw Objects Opaque node of the Render Pass Prefab assigned to the target Viewport 2D.
  * To adjust the Skybox background, select and adjust the properties on the Skybox Render Pass View in the previous step.
    * To adjust the color of the background, adjust the CubemapColor property.
    * To select the background cubemap texture, use the TextureCube property.
    * To override the tracking camera, use the Override Camera property.
    * To adjust the orientation of the background, use the Skybox Orientation property.

![../../_images/skybox-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/skybox-properties.png)
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Using the Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html)

# Using the Factory Content assets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html#using-the-factory-content-assets "Link to this heading")

You can add assets from the Factory Content asset source to your Kanzi application in Kanzi Studio. For a list of the Factory Content, see [Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html).
## Using Factory Content in your project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html#using-factory-content-in-your-project "Link to this heading")
To use Factory Content in your project:
  1. In the Asset Packages window select the Factory Content asset source.
The Factory Content asset packages contain ready-made components and materials that you can use to create prototype projects faster.
![../../_images/asset-packages-factory-content-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-factory-content-selected.png)
  2. From the Asset Packages drag the item that you want to use in your project to a node in the Node Tree, to the Prefabs, or to the Preview.
For example, drag the Car to the Preview. When you drag an item from the Asset Packages to the Preview or a node in the Node Tree or Pages, Kanzi Studio instantiates that item as a prefab, and adds it to the Prefabs.
![../../_images/select-car-asset.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-car-asset.png) ![../../_images/car-asset.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-asset.png) ![../../_images/car-prefab-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-prefab-in-project.png)


## Using Factory Content materials in your project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html#using-factory-content-materials-in-your-project "Link to this heading")
To use Factory Content materials in your project:
  1. In the Asset Packages window select the Factory Content asset source.
The Factory Content asset packages contain ready-made components and materials that you can use to create prototype projects faster.
![../../_images/asset-packages-factory-content-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-factory-content-selected.png)
  2. From the Asset Packages drag the material that you want to use in your project to a node in the Preview, or a node in the Node Tree.
For example, to use a material for a car body, drag that material to either:
     * Preview and drop it on the car body.
     * Node Tree and drop it on the Model node that shows the mesh for the car body.
![../../_images/drag-carbon-fiber-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/drag-carbon-fiber-material.png) ![../../_images/carbon-fiber-car.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/carbon-fiber-car.png)
When you use a Factory Content material in your project, Kanzi Studio adds that material to the Library > Materials and Textures > Materials, and the shaders used by the material to the Library > Resource Files > Shaders.
![../../_images/carbon-fiber-material-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/carbon-fiber-material-in-library.png) ![../../_images/carbon-fiber-shaders.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/carbon-fiber-shaders.png)
To use a material that uses normal map textures, the 3D model where you want to use such material must have tangents. These Factory Content materials use normal map textures:
     * Aluminium Material
     * Carbon Fiber Material
     * Leather Material
     * Rubber Material
To use a material with a normal map texture on a primitive mesh, select the primitive mesh node and in the Properties enable the Generate Tangents property.
![../../_images/enable-generate-tangents.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enable-generate-tangents.png)

# Filters[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/filters.html#filters "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Filters collect and reorganize 3D nodes in your Kanzi project. You can use filters to determine which 3D nodes to render in different render passes.
After you set one or more filters or object sources, a filter collects and outputs a set of 3D nodes that match the requirements you define in that filter.
Use filters to adjust the rendering for the whole or parts of your Kanzi application. To use a filter, either:
  * In a Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass set the Object Source property so that the render pass renders only those nodes that the filter passes to the render pass.
  * In a Node List render pass set the Filter property so that the Node List render pass holds only those nodes that the filter passes to that Node List render pass.
Use a Node List render pass when you want to filter anything but the 3D nodes that you want to render, such as Light nodes. Draw Objects render pass, Draw Objects With Material render pass, and Gather Lights render passes can use the result node list of the same Node List render pass.


See [Rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html).
For example, you can use filters to:
  * Create reflections for nodes. See [Tutorial: Create reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/reflections/reflections.html).
  * Apply a stencil to 3D content. See [Tutorial: Apply a stencil to 3D content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/stencil/stencil.html).
  * Distribute rendering across several frames. See [Tutorial: Progressive rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/progressive-rendering/progressive-rendering.html).
  * Render only transparent nodes. See [Rendering partially transparent nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/rendering-transparent-objects.html).


These filters are available in Kanzi Studio in the Library > Rendering > Object Sources:
  * Contains Property Filter collects 3D nodes that contain, or do not contain a specific property.
See [Using the Contains Property Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-contains-property-filters.html).
  * Object Type Filter collects 3D nodes based on their type. See [Using the Object Type Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-object-type-filters.html).
  * Property Is Equal Filter collects 3D nodes that contain, or do not contain a specific property the value of which matches a specific value.
See [Using the Property Is Equal Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-property-is-equal-filters.html).
  * Sorting Filter either orders 3D nodes by their position on the z axis or groups them by their material type.
See [Using the Sorting Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-sorting-filters.html).
  * Tag Filter collects 3D nodes that have a specific tag assigned.
See [Using the Tag Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-tag-filters.html).

![../../_images/create-filters.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-filters.png)

Contains Property Filter collects 3D nodes that contain, or do not contain a specific property.
To use the Contains Property Filter:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Rendering > Object Sources and select Contains Property Filter.
![../../_images/create-contains-property-filter.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-contains-property-filter.png)
  2. In the Properties set:
     * Source to the source from where you want to collect nodes for filtering. For example, to apply your filter to all nodes in your project, select Root Object Source. You can select the output of another filter as the source from where you collect nodes for filtering.
     * Property Type to the property for which you want to filter your nodes.
     * Operation to either:
       * Include to collect the nodes that contain the property you set in the Property Type property.
       * Exclude to leave out the nodes that contain the property you set in the Property Type property.
![../../_images/contains-property-filter-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contains-property-filter-properties.png)
  3. To take the Contains Property Filter into use, either:
     * In the Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass that you use to render the 3D nodes to which you want to apply the filter, set the Object Source property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.
     * In the Node List render pass that you use to hold the nodes that you want to render using other render passes, set the Filter property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.
Use a Node List render pass when you want to filter anything but the 3D nodes that you want to render, such as Light nodes. Draw Objects render pass, Draw Objects With Material render pass, and Gather Lights render passes can use the result node list of the same Node List render pass.
For example:
    1. In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs create a Group render pass and inside it create:
       * Clear render pass
       * Gather Lights render pass and inside it a Draw Objects render pass
![../../_images/render-passes-for-filters.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-passes-for-filters.png)
    2. In the Library select the Draw Objects render pass that you created and in the Properties set the Object Source property to the filter that you created or to an object source which collects the filter.
See [Using object sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/object-sources/using-object-sources.html).
    3. In the Node Tree select the Viewport 2D node to which you want to apply the filter and in the Properties set the Render Pass Prefab property to the Group render pass whose descendant Draw Objects render pass uses as its object source the filter that you created.
![../../_images/render-pass-prefab-set-to-group-render-pass.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-pass-prefab-set-to-group-render-pass.png)
Kanzi Studio renders the nodes collected by the filter.

Use Object Type Filter to collect 3D nodes based on their type.

For example:
       * To collect all Light nodes, select Light.
Kanzi filters lights in the same way it filters other nodes. When you create a filter that picks specific nodes, the lights that light those nodes are not included in the filter.
       * To collect all nodes that can be rendered, select All renderables.
By default this value includes the Box, Model, Plane, Sphere, and Text Block 3D node.
You can set the rendering of nodes in the Kanzi Engine API by calling

kzuObjectNodeSetIsRenderable(objectNode, KZ_TRUE);

# Using the Sorting Filter[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-sorting-filters.html#using-the-sorting-filter "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Sorting Filter either orders 3D nodes by their position on the z axis or groups them by their material type.
For example, use sorting filters to optimize the performance of your Kanzi application:
  * **Preventing overdraw.**
Excessive overdraw can decrease performance on the GPU in the form of increased fill-rate. See [Preventing overdraw with the Sorting Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/preventing-overdraw-with-sorting-filters.html).
  * **Rendering transparent objects.**
Because visualization of transparent nodes relies on having proper data behind them, in order to solve the blending equations properly, to correctly render transparent nodes, you must render them from back to front. See [Rendering partially transparent nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/rendering-transparent-objects.html).
  * **Reducing shader switches.**
If nodes are presented in an order that requires excessive switching between shader programs, the rendering can slow down. See [Reducing shader switches](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/shaders/reducing-shader-switches.html).


To use the Sorting Filter:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Rendering > Object Sources and select Sorting Filter.
![../../_images/create-sorting-filter.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-sorting-filter.png)
  2. In the Properties set:
     * Source to the source from where you want to collect nodes for filtering. For example, to apply your filter to all nodes in your project, select Root Object Source. You can select the output of another filter as the source from where you collect nodes for filtering.
     * Sorting Type to either:
       * View z to arrange the nodes by their position along the z axis. By arranging nodes into front-to-back ordering before rendering you can prevent overdraw.
Overdraw issues occur when one node is first drawn to an area of pixels in the back buffer, after which another node is presented that occludes the first node, and the same pixels are filled again. Excessive overdraw can decrease performance on the GPU in the form of increased fill-rate. If you order nodes so that the occluding node is drawn first, the occluded pixels do not have to be rendered again because of the depth buffering.
See [Preventing overdraw with the Sorting Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/preventing-overdraw-with-sorting-filters.html).
       * Material type to group the nodes by their material type.
By grouping nodes by their material type you can optimize your Kanzi application, because that way Kanzi can decrease the number of shader switches. See [Reducing shader switches](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/shaders/reducing-shader-switches.html).
     * Either enable or disable the Reverse Order property:
       * When enabled it reverses the current order of nodes.
       * When disabled it keeps the current order of nodes.
![../../_images/sorting-filter-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/sorting-filter-properties.png)
  3. To take the Sorting Filter into use, either:
     * In the Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass that you use to render the 3D nodes to which you want to apply the filter, set the Object Source property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.
     * In the Node List render pass that you use to hold the nodes that you want to render using other render passes, set the Filter property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.
Use a Node List render pass when you want to filter anything but the 3D nodes that you want to render, such as Light nodes. Draw Objects render pass, Draw Objects With Material render pass, and Gather Lights render passes can use the result node list of the same Node List render pass.
For example:
    1. In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs create a Group render pass and inside it create:
       * Clear render pass
       * Gather Lights render pass and inside it a Draw Objects render pass
![../../_images/render-passes-for-filters.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-passes-for-filters.png)
    2. In the Library select the Draw Objects render pass that you created and in the Properties set the Object Source property to the filter that you created or to an object source which collects the filter.
See [Using object sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/object-sources/using-object-sources.html).
    3. In the Node Tree select the Viewport 2D node to which you want to apply the filter and in the Properties set the Render Pass Prefab property to the Group render pass whose descendant Draw Objects render pass uses as its object source the filter that you created.
![../../_images/render-pass-prefab-set-to-group-render-pass.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-pass-prefab-set-to-group-render-pass.png)
Kanzi Studio renders the nodes collected by the filter.


## Using Sorting Filter filters in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-sorting-filters.html#using-sorting-filter-filters-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `SortObjectSource[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13122.html)` class.

Tag Filter collects 3D nodes that have a specific tag assigned.
For example, with tag filters you can:
  * Create reflections of nodes. See [Tutorial: Create reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/reflections/reflections.html).
  * Apply a stencil to 3D content. See [Tutorial: Apply a stencil to 3D content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/stencil/stencil.html).
  * Distribute rendering across several frames. See [Tutorial: Progressive rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/progressive-rendering/progressive-rendering.html).


To use the Tag Filter:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Rendering > Object Sources and select Tag Filter.
![../../_images/create-tag-filter.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-tag-filter.png)
  2. In the Properties set:
     * Source to the source from where you want to collect nodes for filtering. For example, to apply your filter to all nodes in your project, select Root Object Source. You can select the output of another filter as the source from where you collect nodes for filtering.
     * Included Tags to tags of the nodes you want to include in the filter results. If you include more than one tag, the filter returns nodes that contain at least one of the listed tags. See [Using tags](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/tags/using-tags.html).
     * Excluded Tags to tags of the nodes you do not want to include in the filter results. If a node contains only one of the tags listed in the Excluded Tags, the filter does not return that node. This is so even when the same node contains tags you added to the Included Tags.
![../../_images/tag-filter-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/tag-filter-properties.png)
Note
Kanzi filters lights in the same way it filters other nodes. When you create a filter that only includes a specific tag, the lights that light the tagged nodes are included in the filter only when you add the tag to those light nodes. It is often more convenient to either:
     * Exclude the nodes you do not want to render.
     * Tag all light nodes with a separate tag and include that tag in all your filters.
  3. To take the Tag Filter into use, either:
     * In the Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass that you use to render the 3D nodes to which you want to apply the filter, set the Object Source property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.
     * In the Node List render pass that you use to hold the nodes that you want to render using other render passes, set the Filter property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.
Use a Node List render pass when you want to filter anything but the 3D nodes that you want to render, such as Light nodes. Draw Objects render pass, Draw Objects With Material render pass, and Gather Lights render passes can use the result node list of the same Node List render pass.
For example:
    1. In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs create a Group render pass and inside it create:
       * Clear render pass
       * Gather Lights render pass and inside it a Draw Objects render pass
![../../_images/render-passes-for-filters.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-passes-for-filters.png)
    2. In the Library select the Draw Objects render pass that you created and in the Properties set the Object Source property to the filter that you created or to an object source which collects the filter.
See [Using object sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/object-sources/using-object-sources.html).
    3. In the Node Tree select the Viewport 2D node to which you want to apply the filter and in the Properties set the Render Pass Prefab property to the Group render pass whose descendant Draw Objects render pass uses as its object source the filter that you created.
![../../_images/render-pass-prefab-set-to-group-render-pass.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-pass-prefab-set-to-group-render-pass.png)
Kanzi Studio renders the nodes collected by the filter.

# Focus[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/focus/focus.html#focus "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
