# Using the Grid Layout nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#using-the-grid-layout-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Grid Layout nodes to arrange nodes in a grid.
You can let a Grid Layout node arrange its child nodes automatically from the top-left towards the bottom-right corner, or you can manually assign each child node to a specific row and column in the grid.
The depth of a Grid Layout 3D node is the maximum depth for all the child nodes in that Grid Layout 3D node.
![../../_images/grid-layout.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout.gif)
## Creating a Grid Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#creating-a-grid-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Grid Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Grid Layout node and select either Grid Layout 2D or Grid Layout 3D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/create-grid-layout-2d-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-grid-layout-2d-node.png)
Tip
In the Preview tools, use the Grid Layout 2D tool ![grid-layout-2d-tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout-2d-tool.png) to click and drag in the Preview to create a Grid Layout 2D node. To scale the columns and rows, click and drag those columns and rows in the Preview.
  2. In the Node Tree, add child nodes to the layout that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you created a Grid Layout 2D node, add several Image nodes, if you created a Grid Layout 3D node, add several Sphere nodes.
As you add child nodes, the Grid Layout node positions them in the grid from the top-left towards the bottom-right corner of the grid. To manually set the position of each child node in the Grid Layout node, in each child node set the Column and Row properties. See [Assigning nodes to cells in a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#setting-custom-node-and-column).
![../../_images/add-image-nodes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-image-nodes.png) ![../../_images/image-nodes-in-grid-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-nodes-in-grid-layout.png) ![../../_images/image-nodes-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-nodes-in-preview.png)


## Setting the direction in which a Grid Layout node arranges its child nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#setting-the-direction-in-which-a-grid-layout-node-arranges-its-child-nodes "Link to this heading")
When you let a Grid Layout node arrange its child nodes automatically, you can set the direction in which that Grid Layout node arranges its child nodes.
To set the direction in which a Grid Layout node arranges its child nodes:
  1. In the Node Tree, select the Grid Layout node for which you want to set the direction.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Layout Direction property to:
     * Down to make the Grid Layout node first place its child nodes in the first column. When the first column is full, the Grid Layout node starts placing its child nodes in the second column, and so on.
     * Right to make the Grid Layout node first place its child nodes in the first row. When the first row is full, the Grid Layout node starts placing its child nodes in the second row, and so on. This is the default value.
![../../_images/grid-layout-2d-layout-direction-down.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout-2d-layout-direction-down.png) ![../../_images/layout-direction-in-preview-images.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-direction-in-preview-images.png)


## Assigning nodes to cells in a Grid Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#assigning-nodes-to-cells-in-a-grid-layout-node "Link to this heading")
You can manually assign each child node to a specific row and column in a Grid Layout node.
To assign nodes to cells in a Grid Layout node:
  1. Create a Grid Layout node and add several child nodes to it. See [Creating a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#creating-grid-layout-node).
  2. In the Node Tree, select the child nodes of the Grid Layout node. In the Properties, add the Grid Layout > Column and Grid Layout > Row properties.
![../../_images/assign-nodes-to-cells-child-nodes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assign-nodes-to-cells-child-nodes.png) ![../../_images/assign-nodes-to-cells-row-column-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assign-nodes-to-cells-row-column-properties.png)
  3. Use the Column and Row properties to specify a zero-based index of a column and a zero-based index of a row that a node occupies in a Grid Layout node.
For example, to arrange three images in a checkerboard pattern, set:
     * For the second child node: Column to 1, Row to 1.
You assign this node to the second column and second row.
     * For the third child node: Column to 0, Row to 2.
You assign this node to the first column and third row.
![../../_images/layout-custom-row-column-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-custom-row-column-in-preview.png)


Tip
To assign a node to another Grid Layout 2D cell in the Preview:
  1. In the Node Tree, select the node.
  2. Hold down the Ctrl key.
  3. In the Preview, drag the node to the cell where you want to assign it.

![../../_images/preview-assign-node-to-cell.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-assign-node-to-cell.gif)
## Spanning columns and rows in a Grid Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#spanning-columns-and-rows-in-a-grid-layout-node "Link to this heading")
For each cell in a Grid Layout node, you can set the number of columns and rows that cell spans.
To span a cell across columns and rows of a Grid Layout node:
  1. Create a Grid Layout node and add several child nodes to it. See [Creating a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#creating-grid-layout-node).
![../../_images/span-rows-columns-create-child-nodes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/span-rows-columns-create-child-nodes.png)
  2. In each child node of the Grid Layout node, add the Grid Layout > Column and Grid Layout > Row properties. See [Assigning nodes to cells in a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#setting-custom-node-and-column).
A Grid Layout node by default has three columns and three rows. For example, you can arrange the first five child nodes in a Grid Layout on the top row and left column. The sixth child node can occupy the rest of the space. In the child nodes of the Grid Layout node, set these properties:  
| Child node  | Column  | Row  | Layout Width  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| 1  | 0  | 0  | 200  |  
| 2  | 1  | 0  | 200  |  
| 3  | 2  | 0  | 200  |  
| 4  | 0  | 1  | 200  |  
| 5  | 0  | 2  | 200  |  
| 6  | 1  | 1  | 400  |  
A Grid Layout node by default calculates the size of its columns and rows automatically based on the size of the largest child node in that column and row. Here the sixth image, which is larger than the other images, stretches the second column and second row of the Grid Layout node. This leaves gaps in the layout.
![../../_images/span-rows-columns-set-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/span-rows-columns-set-properties.png)
  3. In the Grid Layout node, select a child node that you want to span across multiple columns and rows. In the Properties, add and set the Column Span and Row Span properties to the number of columns and rows you want that cell to span.
The cell spans across columns to its right and across rows downwards.
For example, to set the last image to span two rows and two columns, set the Column Span and Row Span properties to 2.
![../../_images/add-columns-span.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-columns-span.png) ![../../_images/column-and-row-span.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/column-and-row-span.png) ![../../_images/span-rows-columns-result.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/span-rows-columns-result.png)


## Setting how a Grid Layout node calculates the size of its columns and rows[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#setting-how-a-grid-layout-node-calculates-the-size-of-its-columns-and-rows "Link to this heading")
When you create columns and rows in a Grid Layout node, you can set how that Grid Layout node calculates the size of its columns and rows. For example, to distribute content equally in a Grid Layout node, you can use proportional sizes for rows and columns.
To set how Grid Layout node calculates the size of its columns and rows:
  1. Create a Grid Layout node and add several child nodes to it. See [Creating a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#creating-grid-layout-node).
![../../_images/create-grid-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-grid-layout-2d.png)
  2. In the Properties, set the size of the Grid Layout node by setting its Layout Width and Layout Height properties.
For example, set Layout Width to 500 and Layout Height to 300.
![../../_images/layout-width-and-height.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-width-and-height.png)
  3. Set the values of Columns and Rows properties in the Grid Layout node to:
     * Automatic to let the Grid Layout node automatically calculate the size of its columns and rows based on the size of the largest child node in that column and row.
![../../_images/columns-and-rows-automatic.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/columns-and-rows-automatic.png) ![../../_images/automatic-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/automatic-in-preview.png)
     * Fixed to set the exact size of a column and row, regardless of the size of the child nodes in that column and row.
![../../_images/columns-and-rows-fixed.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/columns-and-rows-fixed.png) ![../../_images/fixed-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fixed-in-preview.png)
     * Proportional to set the size of a column and row in proportion to the remaining size of other columns and rows that use this same setting, and the size of the entire Grid Layout node.
For example:
       * To equally distribute the content in columns, select Proportional and for each column use the same value.
       * If you have three columns and you want the first one to occupy half of the Grid Layout node width, select Proportional, use value 2 for the first column, and 1 for the other two columns.
![../../_images/columns-and-rows-proportional.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/columns-and-rows-proportional.png) ![../../_images/proportional-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/proportional-in-preview.png)


## Using Grid Layout nodes to create user interfaces for different screen sizes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#using-grid-layout-nodes-to-create-user-interfaces-for-different-screen-sizes "Link to this heading")
You can use Grid Layout nodes to create applications with consistent user interfaces across devices with different screen sizes. A Grid Layout node can distribute its child nodes so that they occupy the same relative amount of space in the application interface, regardless of screen size or device orientation. For example, with a Grid Layout node, you can place the user interface controls in the top-left and bottom-right corners, with strictly defined distances from the edges of the screen.
For a more advanced approach to creating user interfaces for different screen sizes, see [Tutorial: Making applications with dynamic layout](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/dynamic-layout/dynamic-layout.html).
To use Grid Layout nodes to create consistent user interface for different screen sizes:
  1. Create a Grid Layout node and add several child nodes to it. See [Creating a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#creating-grid-layout-node).
  2. Select the Grid Layout node. In the Properties, set:
     * Columns and Rows to Proportional.
     * Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment to Stretch.
To keep images pixel perfect, instead of setting the Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment properties to Stretch, add the Snap to Pixel property to child nodes whose position changes with the application layout.
![../../_images/columns-and-rows-proportional-default.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/columns-and-rows-proportional-default.png) ![../../_images/alignment-stretch.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/alignment-stretch.png) ![../../_images/horizontal-alignment-strech-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/horizontal-alignment-strech-in-preview.png)
With these settings, you set the Grid Layout node to distribute its content equally across its entire width and height, and set the Grid Layout node to stretch across the entire screen.
  3. In the Node Tree, select the third child in the Grid Layout node. In the Properties, add and set:
     * Column to 2
     * Row to 2
     * Horizontal Alignment to Right
     * Vertical Alignment to Bottom
     * Horizontal Margin property Right property field to 20
     * Vertical Margin property Bottom property field to 20
With these settings, you position the third child node of the Grid Layout node in the third column and third row of the Grid Layout node, and place it 20 pixels from the bottom-right corner of the screen. The third child node in the Grid Layout node stays in that position regardless of the screen size or orientation.
![../../_images/column-and-row-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/column-and-row-settings.png) ![../../_images/third-image-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/third-image-settings.png) ![../../_images/third-image-aligned.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/third-image-aligned.png)
  4. In the Node Tree, select the first child node of the Grid Layout node. In the Properties, add and set:
     * Horizontal Margin property Left property field to 20
     * Vertical Margin property Top property field to 20
With these settings you create a 20 pixel margin between the first child node and the edge of the screen.
![../../_images/first-image-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/first-image-settings.png) ![../../_images/first-image-aligned.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/first-image-aligned.png)
  5. In the Node Tree, select the second child node of the Grid Layout node. In the Properties, add and set:
     * Column to 1
     * Row to 1
     * Horizontal Alignment to Center
     * Vertical Alignment to Center
With these settings, you position the second child node in the second column and second row of the Grid Layout.
![../../_images/column-and-row-third-image.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/column-and-row-third-image.png) ![../../_images/second-image-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/second-image-settings.png) ![../../_images/proportional-alignment-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/proportional-alignment-in-preview.png)


## Setting the appearance of a Grid Layout 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#setting-the-appearance-of-a-grid-layout-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png)


## Using the Grid Layout 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#using-the-grid-layout-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create a Grid Layout 3D node with two columns and two rows with automatic cell size, and set the grid to arrange the items in the grid columns from top to bottom:

```
// Create a GridLayout3D named Grid.
GridLayout3DSharedPtr grid = GridLayout3D::create(domain, "Grid");

// Set the grid so that it arranges the items in the grid by first adding them
// in the rows of the first column. When all the rows in the first column are full,
// grid starts adding the items in the rows of the second column, and so on.
grid->setDirection(GridLayoutConcept::GridDirectionDown);

// Set the grid to have two automatic columns and rows that get their size from
// the size of their content.
grid->addAutomaticColumn();
grid->addAutomaticColumn();
grid->addAutomaticRow();
grid->addAutomaticRow();

// Create and add four cubes, one to each cell in the grid. Let the grid
// automatically set which cells the child nodes occupy. Since #GridDirection is
// set to GridDirectionDown, the grid automatically arranges the items in the grid
// by first adding items to both rows in the first column from top to bottom,
// then both rows in the second column from top to bottom.
Model3DSharedPtr child1 = Model3D::createBox(domain, "Box1", Vector3(2.0f, 2.0f, 2.0f), ThemeRed);
grid->addChild(child1);
Model3DSharedPtr child2 = Model3D::createBox(domain, "Box2", Vector3(3.0f, 3.0f, 3.0f), ThemeBlue);
grid->addChild(child2);
Model3DSharedPtr child3 = Model3D::createBox(domain, "Box3", Vector3(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f), ThemeOrange);
grid->addChild(child3);
Model3DSharedPtr child4 = Model3D::createBox(domain, "Box4", Vector3(4.0f, 4.0f, 4.0f), ThemeGreen);
grid->addChild(child4);

```
Copy to clipboard
This example creates a Grid Layout 3D node with two columns and two rows, using both fixed and automatic cell size. By default, the Grid Layout 3D node automatically sets which cells its items occupy.

```
// Create a GridLayout3D named Grid.
GridLayout3DSharedPtr grid = GridLayout3D::create(domain, "Grid");

// Set the grid to have two columns and two rows.
// Set the size of the first column to five units, but let the second column adapt
// its size from the size of its content.
grid->addFixedColumn(5.0f);
grid->addAutomaticColumn();
// Set the size of the first row to four units, but let the second row adapt its size
// from the size of its content.
grid->addFixedRow(4.0f);
grid->addAutomaticRow();

// Create and add three cubes to the grid and let the grid automatically set
// which cells the child nodes occupy. In this example, the three child nodes occupy
// the entire first row and the first column of the second row. The last cell (bottom-right)
// of the grid stays empty.
Model3DSharedPtr child1 = Model3D::createBox(domain, "Box1", Vector3(2.0f, 2.0f, 2.0f), ThemeOrange);
grid->addChild(child1);
Model3DSharedPtr child2 = Model3D::createBox(domain, "Box2", Vector3(3.0f, 3.0f, 3.0f), ThemeBlue);
grid->addChild(child2);
Model3DSharedPtr child3 = Model3D::createBox(domain, "Box3", Vector3(1.0f, 2.0f, 1.0f), ThemeGreen);
grid->addChild(child3);

```
Copy to clipboard
This example creates a Grid Layout 3D node with two columns and three rows whose sizes the Grid Layout 3D node calculates in proportion to the sizes of other columns and rows in the grid. The example manually sets which cells each item in the grid occupies.

```
// Create a GridLayout3D named Grid.
GridLayout3DSharedPtr grid = GridLayout3D::create(domain, "Grid");

// Set the width and height of the entire grid to six units.
grid->setWidth(6.0f);
grid->setHeight(6.0f);

// Set the grid to have two weighted columns and three weighted rows.
// The first column gets one third and the second column two thirds
// of the entire grid width.
grid->addWeightedColumn(1.0f);
grid->addWeightedColumn(2.0f);
// Each row gets one third of the entire grid height.
grid->addWeightedRow(1.0f);
grid->addWeightedRow(1.0f);
grid->addWeightedRow(1.0f);

// Create an orange cube named Box1 and add it to the cell in the first row and the first column
// (the upper-left corner of the grid).
Model3DSharedPtr child1 = Model3D::createBox(domain, "Box1", Vector3(2.0f, 2.0f, 2.0f), ThemeOrange);
GridLayout3D::setColumn(*child1, 0);
GridLayout3D::setRow(*child1, 0);
grid->addChild(child1);
// Create a blue cube named Box2 and add it so that it spans the second and third cells in the first column.
Model3DSharedPtr child2 = Model3D::createBox(domain, "Box2", Vector3(3.0f, 3.0f, 3.0f), ThemeBlue);
GridLayout3D::setColumn(*child2, 0);
GridLayout3D::setRow(*child2, 1);
GridLayout3D::setRowSpan(*child2, 2);
grid->addChild(child2);
// Create a green cube named Box3 and add it to the cell in the third row and the second column.
// (the bottom-right corner of the grid).
Model3DSharedPtr child3 = Model3D::createBox(domain, "Box3", Vector3(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f), ThemeGreen);
GridLayout3D::setColumn(*child3, 1);
GridLayout3D::setRow(*child3, 2);
grid->addChild(child3);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `GridLayout3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18674.html)` class.
## Using the Grid Layout 2D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#using-the-grid-layout-2d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create a Grid Layout 2D node with two columns and two rows with automatic cell size, and set the grid to arrange the items in the grid columns from top to bottom:

```
// Create a GridLayout2D named Grid.
GridLayout2DSharedPtr grid = GridLayout2D::create(domain, "Grid");

// Set the grid so that it arranges the items in the grid by first adding them
// in the rows of the first column. When all the rows in the first column are full,
// grid starts adding the items in the rows of the second column, and so on.
grid->setDirection(GridLayoutConcept::GridDirectionDown);

// Set the grid to have two automatic columns and rows that get their size from
// the size of their content.
grid->addAutomaticColumn();
grid->addAutomaticColumn();
grid->addAutomaticRow();
grid->addAutomaticRow();

// Create and add four empty nodes, one to each cell in the grid. Let the grid
// automatically set which cells the child nodes occupy. Since #GridDirection is
// set to GridDirectionDown, the grid automatically arranges the items in the grid
// by first adding items to both rows in the first column from top to bottom,
// then both rows in the second column from top to bottom.
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr child1 = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty1", 128.0f, 128.0f, ThemeRed);
grid->addChild(child1);
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr child2 = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty2", 256.0f, 256.0f, ThemeBlue);
grid->addChild(child2);
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr child3 = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty3", 128.0f, 128.0f, ThemeOrange);
grid->addChild(child3);
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr child4 = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty4", 128.0f, 128.0f, ThemeGreen);
grid->addChild(child4);

```
Copy to clipboard
This example creates a Grid Layout 2D node with two columns and two rows, using both fixed and automatic cell size. By default, the Grid Layout 2D node automatically sets which cells its items occupy.

```
// Create a GridLayout2D named Grid.
GridLayout2DSharedPtr grid = GridLayout2D::create(domain, "Grid");

// Set the grid to have two columns and two rows.
// Set the size of the first column to 200 units, but let the second column adapt
// its size from the size of its content.
grid->addFixedColumn(200.0f);
grid->addAutomaticColumn();
// Set the size of the first row to 100 units, but let the second row adapt its size
// from the size of its content.
grid->addFixedRow(100.0f);
grid->addAutomaticRow();

// Create and add three empty nodes to the grid and let the grid automatically set
// which cells the child nodes occupy. In this example, the three child nodes occupy
// the entire first row and the first column of the second row. The last cell (bottom-right)
// of the grid stays empty.
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr child1 = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty1", 128.0f, 128.0f, ThemeRed);
grid->addChild(child1);
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr child2 = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty2", 256.0f, 256.0f, ThemeBlue);
grid->addChild(child2);
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr child3 = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty3", 128.0f, 128.0f, ThemeOrange);
grid->addChild(child3);

```
Copy to clipboard
This example creates a Grid Layout 2D node with two columns and three rows whose sizes the grid calculates in proportion to the sizes of other columns and rows in the grid. For each item in the grid, the example sets which cells that item occupies.

```
// Create a GridLayout2D named Grid.
GridLayout2DSharedPtr grid = GridLayout2D::create(domain, "Grid");

// Set the width and height of the entire grid to six hundred units.
grid->setWidth(600.0f);
grid->setHeight(600.0f);

// Set the grid to have two weighted columns and three weighted rows.
// The first column gets one third and the second column two thirds
// of the entire grid width.
grid->addWeightedColumn(1.0f);
grid->addWeightedColumn(2.0f);
// Each row gets one third of the entire grid height.
grid->addWeightedRow(1.0f);
grid->addWeightedRow(1.0f);
grid->addWeightedRow(1.0f);

// Create an empty node named Empty1 and add it to the cell in the first row and the first column
// (the upper-left corner of the grid).
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr child1 = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty1", 128.0f, 128.0f, ThemeRed);
GridLayout2D::setColumn(*child1, 0);
GridLayout2D::setRow(*child1, 0);
grid->addChild(child1);
// Create an empty node named Empty1, add it to the cell in the second row and the first column
// and make it span across the second and third rows of the first coloumn in the grid.
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr child2 = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty2", 256.0f, 256.0f, ThemeBlue);
GridLayout2D::setColumn(*child2, 0);
GridLayout2D::setRow(*child2, 1);
GridLayout2D::setRowSpan(*child2, 2);
grid->addChild(child2);
// Create an empty node named Empty3, add it to the cell in the third row and the second column
// (the bottom-right corner of the grid).
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr child3 = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty3", 128.0f, 128.0f, ThemeOrange);
GridLayout2D::setColumn(*child3, 1);
GridLayout2D::setRow(*child3, 2);
grid->addChild(child3);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `GridLayout2D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18670.html)` class.
##  Grid Layout property types and messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#grid-layout-property-types-and-messages "Link to this heading")
For lists of the available property types and messages for the Grid Layout nodes, see [Grid Layout 2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/grid-layout-2d-reference.html) and [Grid Layout 3D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/grid-layout-3d-reference.html).

Use image files to bring bitmap assets to Kanzi Studio.
Use image files to bring bitmap assets to Kanzi Studio. You can import images to Kanzi in these file formats:
  * .png, including the alpha channel
  * .tga, including the alpha channel
  * .psd, including layers. See [Importing Adobe Photoshop PSD files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-photoshop-files-with-layers.html).
  * .dds, can contain cubemaps, mipmaps, or both

## Image Compression[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/images.html#image-compression "Link to this heading")
While most image formats contain pixel data in compressed form, the data is usually taken into GPU uncompressed. However, when images are stored in compression formats that are natively supported by GPUs, images are transferred and stored on the GPU in a compressed form. This reduces the time needed for uploading the image data to the GPU and can boost the performance.
The best performing compression level depends on your target device. High compression levels use more CPU but less memory bandwidth, whereas low compression levels use less CPU but more memory bandwidth.
Kanzi supports these compression formats natively supported by GPUs:
  * **Adaptive Scalable Texture Compression (ASTC)** ARM and AMD’s block-based compression algorithm. ASTC creates smaller files and better image quality than the ETC algorithm. An ASTC block takes 128 bits, and you can set the size of the block in pixels. Fewer pixels in a block result in better image quality of the compressed image, but create larger file sizes.
  * **Ericsson Texture Compression (ETC)** ETC compression saves 5/6 of the memory used by the image on the GPU. However, the space taken by the image in the kzb file is likely to be increased compared to, for example, PNG or JPEG formats.


See [Compressing textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html).
## Mipmaps[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/images.html#mipmaps "Link to this heading")
Mipmaps are pre-calculated collections of images that increase the rendering speed and reduce rendering artifacts.
The compression of images and the generation of mipmaps take some time. Kanzi asks you to preprocess the images before exporting the kzb file. Because your Kanzi application can run without the preprocessed data, if the preprocessed data is not available, your application runs without it. See [Using mipmaps](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html).

# Importing Adobe Photoshop PSD files[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-photoshop-files-with-layers.html#importing-adobe-photoshop-psd-files "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

You can import Adobe Photoshop PSD files to your Kanzi Studio project and preserve the structure of the PSD file. This allows you to use each layer from a PSD file as a separate node in your Kanzi Studio project.
When you import a PSD file, Kanzi Studio:
  1. Copies the PSD file to the `<ProjectName>/Images` or `<ProjectName>/Tool_project/Images` directory.
  2. Crops the transparent borders from each PSD layer and saves them as png images to the `<ProjectName>/Images` or `<ProjectName>/Tool_project/Images` directory. In Kanzi Studio you can see these files in the Library > Resource Files > Images in a directory with the same name as the PSD file.
  3. In the Prefabs creates an Empty Node 2D node named after the PSD file and a hierarchy of Empty Node 2D nodes corresponding to the structure of the PSD image. Kanzi Studio uses:
     * Empty Node 2D nodes for the PSD layer groups
     * Image nodes for PSD layers
     * Either Image or Text Block 2D nodes for PSD text layers. Which node Kanzi Studio uses depends on the option that you select when you import a PSD file.
  4. Applies transformation to each imported PSD layer using the Render Transformation property to position the nodes to the same position as they are in the PSD file.


For example, when you import a PSD file that contains one layer for the background and another layer that contains a small logo in the corner of the screen, Kanzi Studio creates two png images in your Kanzi Studio project and two Image nodes. Kanzi Studio removes the trashbands from the small logo, meaning that you end up with two images of different sizes. Kanzi Studio positions both nodes in relation to each other using the Render Transformation.
Kanzi Studio does not support all types of Photoshop layers and layer styles. If Kanzi Studio does not import a layer or a style layer, merge or rasterize such layers in Photoshop before you import them to Kanzi Studio.
To maintain pixel precision, use integers for all Kanzi Studio 2D layer transformations and avoid stretching or scaling the content.
## Importing a PSD file[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-photoshop-files-with-layers.html#importing-a-psd-file "Link to this heading")
To import a PSD file:
  1. In the Kanzi Studio main menu select File > Import > Import PSD and select the PSD file that you want to import.
Import PSD tool window opens and all layers in that PSD file are selected for importing.
![../../_images/import-psd.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/import-psd.png)
  2. In the right-hand pane select the layers and layer groups that you want to import. If your PSD file contains text layers, you can import them as Kanzi Text Block 2D nodes so that you can edit the text in Kanzi Studio. In the Import psd text layers as option select:
     * Image nodes to import PSD text layers only as Kanzi Image nodes.
     * Text Block 2D nodes to import PSD text layers only as Kanzi Text Block 2D nodes.
     * Image and Text Block 2D nodes inside Empty Node to import PSD text layers as both Kanzi Image and Text Block 2D nodes both stored in an Empty Node 2D node.
![../../_images/psd-example.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/psd-example.png)
Tip
To set your preferred way of importing text layers from PSD files:
    1. In the main menu select Edit > User Preferences.
![../../_images/edit-user-preferences.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/edit-user-preferences.png)
    2. In the Advanced tab set the value of the Import text layers as setting.
![../../_images/user-preferences-import-psd-text-layers-as.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/user-preferences-import-psd-text-layers-as.png)
  3. Click Import.
Kanzi Studio imports the layers that you selected and preserves the rendering of nodes based on the layer hierarchy in the PSD file. The order in which Kanzi renders nodes is set by their order in the Node Tree: Kanzi renders child nodes and sibling nodes lower in the node tree on top of the parent node and sibling nodes that are higher in the node tree. See [Configuring nodes for efficient rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/setting-layers-for-efficient-rendering.html).


## Reimporting a PSD file[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-photoshop-files-with-layers.html#reimporting-a-psd-file "Link to this heading")
When you make a change to a PSD file, to bring the changes from the PSD file that you already imported to your Kanzi Studio project, reimport that PSD file.
To reimport a PSD file, in the Library > Resource Files > Images right-click the PSD file where you made changes, and select Reimport PSD.
![../../_images/reimport-psd.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reimport-psd.png)
Kanzi Studio imports the content from the PSD file. When reimporting, Kanzi Studio resets the values of properties that the content in a PSD file sets, such as the Render Transformation property to position the content and the Text property to set the text in a Text Block 2D node. However, Kanzi Studio keeps the values of all the properties that you added after you imported the PSD file.

When you import images Kanzi Studio automatically creates textures from those images.
Use image files to bring bitmap assets to Kanzi Studio. You can import images to Kanzi in these file formats:
  * .png, including the alpha channel
  * .tga, including the alpha channel
  * .psd, including layers. See [Importing Adobe Photoshop PSD files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-photoshop-files-with-layers.html).
  * .dds, can contain cubemaps, mipmaps, or both
  * .bmp, .exr, .gif, .hdr, .ico, .iff, .jng, .jpg, .jpeg, .jif, .mng, .pcx, .pmb, .pgm, .ppm, .pfm, .pict, .ras, .sgi, .tiff, .tif, .wbmp, .xmb, and .xpm


## Importing images to a Kanzi Studio project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-images.html#importing-images-to-a-ks-project "Link to this heading")
To import images:
  1. In the Assets window click Import Assets.
![../../_images/assets-import-assets.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assets-import-assets.png)
  2. Select the files that you want to import and click Open.


When you import images, Kanzi Studio adds those images to the Library > Resource Files > Images, and creates from them textures in the Library > Materials and Textures > Textures:
  * For dds images that contain cubemaps, mipmaps, or both, Kanzi Studio automatically extracts the cubemap faces and mipmap images, creates a Cubemap Texture, and assigns to the Cubemap Texture the cubemap faces from the dds image. See [Using cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-cubemap-textures.html).
  * For hdr and exr images Kanzi Studio asks you what type of textures you want to create:
    * Single Texture. See [Using single textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-single-textures.html).
    * Environment cubemap texture. See [Using environment textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html).
    * Irradiance and specular cubemap textures for image-based lighting. See [Using image-based lighting cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html).
  * For other images Kanzi Studio creates a Single Texture.

![../../_images/library-resource-files-images1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-resource-files-images1.png) ![../../_images/library-textures.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-textures.png)

In many third-party tools, animations contain information about the target of animations. When you import animations to Kanzi Studio, Kanzi organizes objects and animations in the following way:
  * The visual content is placed inside a scene that contains the objects.
  * Kanzi Studio creates a timeline sequence, adds for the scene an Animation Player, and sets the Target Animation Timeline property of the Animation Player to the timeline sequence.
  * For each animated object, Kanzi Studio creates a timeline entry and sets the animation target for that timeline entry for that target.
  * Kanzi Studio places all animation data under the corresponding timeline entries.


Keep this in mind before you move objects from the imported scene to another scene, or when you want to use the animations in event-driven and background animations.

# Handling user input[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#handling-user-input "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
You can set how and which elements in your application react to user input. In Kanzi, to handle user input you can:
  * Enable gesture and key recognition for nodes. See [Using input manipulators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#using-input-manipulators).
  * Control how nodes react to input. See [Controlling how a node reacts to input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#controlling-how-a-node-reacts-to-input).
  * Define which nodes receive input. See [Defining which node receives input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#defining-which-node-receives-input).
  * Set the size of the input area of 3D nodes. See [Setting the size of the input area of 3D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#setting-the-size-of-the-input-area).

![../../_images/input.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/input.gif)
For these Kanzi nodes you do not have to create input manipulators manually, because they handle input by default:
  * Button nodes. See [Using the Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html).
  * Toggle Button nodes. See [Using the Toggle Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html).
  * List Box nodes. See [List Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html).
  * List Box Item Container prefabs. See [Using the List Box Item Container prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html).
  * Scroll View nodes. See [Using the Scroll View nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scroll-views/using-scroll-views.html).
  * Slider nodes. See [Using the Slider nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/sliders/using-sliders.html).
  * Text Box nodes. See [Using the Text Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html).


Use triggers and actions to create interactions based on user input.
See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
## Using input manipulators[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#using-input-manipulators "Link to this heading")
Kanzi provides low and high-level access to input:
  * The high-level system provides input in terms of gestures, such as click, pan, pinch, and so on. It is recommended to use the high-level system to bind gestures to the UI components or application functionality.
  * The low-level input system reports raw touch events as they happen in nodes.


Kanzi provides input manipulators to enable gesture recognition for nodes in your Kanzi application. You can create and configure the manipulators:
  * In Kanzi Studio using the Input Manipulators node components and input manipulator triggers
  * Through the Kanzi Engine API


Kanzi provides these input manipulators:  
|  ![../../_images/click-manipulator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-manipulator.png)  |  Use the Click Manipulator to enable users to click nodes in your Kanzi application. See [Using the Click Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html).  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ![../../_images/long-press-manipulator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/long-press-manipulator.png)  |  Use the Long-Press Manipulator to enable users to long-press nodes in your Kanzi application. See [Using the Long-Press Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/long-press-manipulator.html).  |  
|  ![../../_images/multi-click-manipulator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/multi-click-manipulator.png)  |  Use the Multi-Click Manipulator to enable users to multi-click nodes in your Kanzi application. See [Using the Multi-Click Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/multi-click-manipulator.html).  |  
|  ![../../_images/key-manipulator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/key-manipulator.png)  |  Use the Key Manipulator to set the keys that the user can use to navigate your application. For example, you can override the default focus navigation keys and use a specific key to set focus to a node, set a key to open or close a popup-type window, or move focus in the focus chain. See [Using the Key Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/key-manipulator.html).  |  
|  ![../../_images/navigation-manipulator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-manipulator.png)  |  Use the Navigation Manipulator to set the keys that the user can use to navigate to different directions in your application. See [Using the Navigation Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/navigation-manipulator.html).  |  
|  ![../../_images/drag-and-drop-manipulator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/drag-and-drop-manipulator.png)  |  Use the Drag-And-Drop Manipulator to enable users to drag and drop nodes in your Kanzi application. See [Using the Drag-And-Drop Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/drag-and-drop-manipulator.html).  |  
|  ![../../_images/pan-manipulator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/pan-manipulator.png)  |  Use the Pan Manipulator to enable users to move nodes in your Kanzi application. See [Using the Pan Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/pan-manipulator.html).  |  
|  ![../../_images/pinch-manipulator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/pinch-manipulator.png)  |  Use the Pinch Manipulator to enable users to zoom and rotate nodes in your Kanzi application. See [Using the Pinch Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/pinch-manipulator.html).  |  
In Kanzi Studio when you select a node and in the Node Components > Input Manipulators create an input manipulator node component, Kanzi installs to that node the corresponding input manipulator. Kanzi Studio provides these input manipulator components for enabling gesture recognition:
  * Click Manipulator
  * Key Manipulator
  * Long-Press Manipulator
  * Multi-Click Manipulator
  * Navigation Manipulator
  * Pan Manipulator

![../../_images/input-manipulator-components.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/input-manipulator-components.png)
In the Kanzi Engine API `InputManipulator[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13362.html)` is the base class for input manipulators, and functions, such as `ClickManipulator::create[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13162.html#a2126bc1e0e9c78d1ba5871a4389281f1)` and `PanManipulator::create[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13454.html#a00e56340da66fbfc93ca29960fb2d69c)` create input manipulators responsible for the corresponding gesture recognition.
When you create an input manipulator, to recognize a gesture, attach it to the node with `Node::addInputManipulator[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13774.html#ae35b5926d8bac8bf3cd764d7e33cb8ce)`. This function attaches all the children of that node, too.
The attached input manipulator generates messages in response to user actions. Each manipulator uses messages to report different events during gesture recognition, such as `PanManipulator::StartedMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13454.html#a34fda88fb49719e26df5eb5c92669bbd)`, `PanManipulator::MovedMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13454.html#a6391057a0abc9cc3a4b7779d5923cbb4)`, `PanManipulator::FinishedMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13454.html#a67f9ab0931b26161aa63971fe4a5c4f4)` for the pan manipulator, and so on.
## Controlling how a node reacts to input[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#controlling-how-a-node-reacts-to-input "Link to this heading")
Use the Input > Enabled property to control how a node reacts to input.
Tip
The Button, List Box, Scroll View, Slider, and Text Box nodes handle input by default and do not react to input when they are disabled.
When you disable the Enabled property of a node, you effectively disable that node and its descendant nodes in the same overlay focus scope.
This means that when you disable the Enabled property of a node that contains an overlay focus scope node, the nodes in that overlay stay effectively enabled.
Kanzi delivers input also to effectively disabled nodes. This enables you to control the behavior of a disabled node.
When you effectively disable a node:
  * When the node is focused, it receives key input until the focus moves to another node.
  * When the node is not focused, it is not part of the focus chain and does not receive key input.


To observe whether a node is effectively enabled, use the Input > Effectively Enabled property in a state manager or a binding. For example, to visually indicate to the user whether a node is in use, create a state manager and use the Effectively Enabled property as its controller property.
To learn more about focus, see [Focus](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/focus/focus.html) and [Using focus](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/focus/setting-focus.html).
To learn more about the Kanzi state manager, see [State manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/state-managers.html).
To control how a node reacts to input:
  1. In the Node Tree or Prefabs select the node, in the State Tools create a state group, and name it.
For example, name the state group Enabled.
![../../_images/select-button1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-button1.png) ![../../_images/button-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-in-preview.png) ![../../_images/create-state-group.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-state-group.png) ![../../_images/enabled-state-group.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enabled-state-group.png)
  2. In the State Tools create two states, one that defines the appearance and behavior of the node when it is in use, and another that defines the node when it is not in use.
For example, name the states Enabled and Disabled.
![../../_images/enabled-disabled-states.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enabled-disabled-states.png)
  3. For each state, define the appearance and behavior of the node in that state.
For example, to set how the node looks when it is not in use, in the Disabled state set the Opacity property to 0.3.
![../../_images/opacity-0.3.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/opacity-0.3.png) ![../../_images/set-to-disabled-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-to-disabled-state.png) ![../../_images/opacity-set-disabled-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/opacity-set-disabled-state.png)
  4. In the State Tools set the Controller Property to Input > Effectively Enabled.
The Effectively Enabled property indicates whether a node and its ancestor nodes are enabled.
![../../_images/set-effectively-enabled-controller-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-effectively-enabled-controller-property.png)
  5. In the State Tools set the value of the Effectively Enabled controller property in the Disabled state to False.
This way you set your application to use:
     * The Disabled state when the node is not in use and does not react to input.
     * The Enabled state when the node is in use and reacts to input.
![../../_images/set-effectively-enabled-false.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-effectively-enabled-false.png)
  6. In the State Tools, click Edit State Manager to deactivate the State Tools.
![../../_images/exit-state-tools.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/exit-state-tools.png)


When you change the value of the Input > Enabled property, the appearance of the node changes. When you disable the Enabled property and try to interact with the node in the Preview, the node does not react.
![../../_images/node-enabled-disabled.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-enabled-disabled.gif)
## Defining which node receives input[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#defining-which-node-receives-input "Link to this heading")
When creating a user interface, pay attention to how your application handles input, because only one node can receive input at a time. For example, define whether a click is handled by the node in the front or by the one behind it.
Kanzi uses hit testing to determine the nodes that receive input. In practice, hit testing projects a ray from the camera towards the 3D scene based on the screen coordinates of the input event.
By default hit testing is enabled for the Button, Toggle Button, List Box Item Container, Scroll View, Slider, and Text Box nodes.
To enable hit testing for a node of any other node type, add and enable the Input > Hit Testable property to that node. A 3D node has hit testing enabled when that node or its ancestor has the Hit Testable property enabled.
The first 3D node from the Camera node whose bounding box is intersected and has hit testing enabled, receives the input, consumes the event, and generates set actions, such as sending a click message.
For example, if you place two Box nodes so that the BoxFront node is in front of the BoxRear node and occludes it:
  * The BoxFront node receives the input when the Hit Testable property of the BoxFront node is enabled.
  * The BoxRear node receives the input even though it is occluded by the BoxFront node when:
    * Hit Testable property of the BoxFront node is disabled
    * Hit Testable property of the BoxRear node is enabled

![../../_images/hit-testable.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/hit-testable.gif)
## Setting the size of the input area of 3D nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#setting-the-size-of-the-input-area-of-3d-nodes "Link to this heading")
In Kanzi, hit testing for a 3D node is by default based on the bounding box of that node.
When you want to change the area within which your 3D content receives input, use the Input > Hit Testable Container property.
When you enable the Hit Testable Container property, Kanzi includes in the input area the actual layout size of the 3D node that has the property and the actual layout size of any of its child nodes. The actual layout size of a 3D node is determined by the values of the Actual Layout Width, Actual Layout Height, and Actual Layout Depth properties.
For these nodes, the Hit Testable Container property is enabled by default:
  * Button 3D
  * List Box Item Container 3D
  * Scroll View 3D
  * Slider 3D


To set the size of the input area for a 3D node of some other type, add and enable these properties:
  * Hit Testable Container
  * Hit Testable


Keep in mind that if a node is not a layout control node or the child of a layout control node, the actual layout size of that node is zero. For example, the actual layout size of an Empty Node 3D or a Model node whose parent node is not a layout control node, is zero. When you want to use such a node to set the size of the input area, place that node in a layout control node. See [Layout control nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/layouts.html).
For example, a Stack Layout 3D node which contains a Box node receives click input:
  * When the Hit Testable Container property of the Stack Layout 3D node is disabled, from the area defined by the Width, Height, and Depth properties of the Box node
  * When the Hit Testable Container property of the Stack Layout 3D node is enabled, from the area defined by the Layout Width, Layout Height, and Layout Depth properties of either the Stack Layout 3D or the Box node

![../../_images/hit-testable-container.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/hit-testable-container.gif)
## Disabling input handling in your application[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#disabling-input-handling-in-your-application "Link to this heading")
A Kanzi application handles input by default. To optimize performance, you can disable input handling in an application that does not need it. When you disable input, Kanzi does not spend CPU resources on the input events that it receives from the platform. Keep in mind that when you disable input handling, the application cannot manage the key focus, either.
To disable input handling and key focus management, override the `Application::setScreenOverride[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a89d527d839a1936d3cad10944d623370)` function:

```
// To disable input handling and key focus management, leave the implementation empty.
void setScreenOverride() override
{
}

```

# Using the List Box Item Container prefabs[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#using-the-list-box-item-container-prefabs "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the List Box Item Container prefabs to set the appearance and behavior of items in List Box nodes. For example, use a List Box Item Container prefab to add decorative elements to List Box items or change the appearance of the currently selected item.
![../../_images/list-box-item-container.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/list-box-item-container.gif)
Learn how to use a List Box Item Container 2D prefab to set the appearance of the selected item in a Grid List Box 2D node by completing a tutorial. See [Tutorial: Create a contacts list with a Grid List Box](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/list-box/list-box.html).
For an example of how to use a List Box Item Container 3D prefab to set the appearance of the selected item in a Trajectory List Box 3D node, see the [Trajectory list box example](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/examples/trajectory-list-box/trajectory-list-box.html).
## Creating a List Box Item Container prefab[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#creating-a-list-box-item-container-prefab "Link to this heading")
To create a List Box Item Container prefab:
  1. In the Prefabs, click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-prefab.png) and select List Box Item Container 2D or List Box Item Container 3D. List Box Item Container must always be a prefab. See [Using node prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html).
Use List Box Item Container 2D with Grid List Box 2D nodes and List Box Item Container 3D with Grid List Box 3D and Trajectory List Box 3D nodes. See [Using the Grid List Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html) and [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html).
![../../_images/list-box-item-container-2d-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/list-box-item-container-2d-in-project.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, select the List Box node with which you want to use the List Box Item Container. In the Properties, add the List Box > Item Container Template property and set it to the List Box Item Container prefab that you created.
The Item Container Template property allows you to share functionality between the items in a List Box node. When you set the Item Container Template property, each item in the List Box node inherits the functionality from the List Box Item Container prefab. Kanzi by default places the list box item as a child node of the List Box Item Container prefab.
![../../_images/contactslist-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contactslist-in-project.png) ![../../_images/item-container-template-in-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/item-container-template-in-properties.png)
  3. To make a List Box Item Container 2D prefab stretch to the cell size of a Grid List Box 2D node, add and set the Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment properties to Stretch.
![../../_images/list-box-item-container-2d-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/list-box-item-container-2d-in-project.png) ![../../_images/alignment-stretch1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/alignment-stretch1.png)
  4. In the List Box Item Container prefab, set the functionality and decoration that is common to all List Box items. For example, you can:
     * Set the placement of the list box item in the node tree of the List Box Item Container prefab. See [Setting the placement of List Box items in a List Box Item Container](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#list-box-item-placement-container).
     * Set the appearance of the selected list box item. See [Using a List Box Item Container to set the appearance of the selected item in a List Box](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#list-box-item-container-selected-item).
The List Box Item Container prefab is by default a focus group and handles the key focus and key input. This enables Kanzi to synchronize the item selection and key focus in the List Box node that uses the List Box Item Container. See [Handling the key focus in a List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html#lb-handling-key-focus).


## Setting the placement of List Box items in a List Box Item Container[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#setting-the-placement-of-list-box-items-in-a-list-box-item-container "Link to this heading")
When you set a List Box Item Container prefab as the Item Container Template of a List Box node, Kanzi by default places the list box item as a child node of the List Box Item Container prefab. You can set a Content Layout node in the List Box Item Container prefab as the root node of the list box item.
To set the placement of List Box items in a List Box Item Container:
  1. Create a List Box Item Container prefab. See [Creating a List Box Item Container prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#create-list-box-item-container).
  2. In the List Box Item Container prefab, create the nodes that you want to use to define the appearance of the list box item, and a Content Layout node that you use as the root node of the list box item.
![../../_images/content-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-2d.png)
  3. Create an alias that Kanzi uses to tell the List Box Item Container prefab which Content Layout node to use as the root node of the list box item:
    1. In the Prefabs, select the List Box Item Container prefab. In the Dictionaries, click + Add Resource, and select Create > Alias.
This way, you create an alias in the resource dictionary of the List Box Item Container 2D.
![../../_images/list-box-item-container-2.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/list-box-item-container-2.png) ![../../_images/create-new-alias-resource.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-new-alias-resource.png)
    2. Name the alias $layout and set it to point to the Content Layout node that you want to use as the root node of the list box item.
This way, you set Kanzi to place the list box item in the Content Layout node. If you do not specify the $layout alias, Kanzi places the list box item as the last child node of the List Box Item Container prefab.
![../../_images/content-layout-alias.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-alias.png)


## Using a List Box Item Container to set the appearance of the selected item in a List Box[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#using-a-list-box-item-container-to-set-the-appearance-of-the-selected-item-in-a-list-box "Link to this heading")
You can use the List Box Item Container prefabs to change the appearance of the currently selected item in a List Box node. For example, to highlight the selected item, you can make it slightly larger than the other items or change its background color.
To use a List Box Item Container to set the appearance of the selected item in a List Box:
  1. Create a List Box Item Container prefab and set it as the Item Container Template of a List Box node. See [Creating a List Box Item Container prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#create-list-box-item-container).
For example:
    1. Create a List Box Item Container 2D prefab and set it as the Item Container Template of a Grid List Box 2D node that presents address book contacts.
![../../_images/list-box-item-container-2d-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/list-box-item-container-2d-in-project.png) ![../../_images/contactslist-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contactslist-in-project.png) ![../../_images/item-container-template-in-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/item-container-template-in-properties.png) ![../../_images/contacts-list.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contacts-list.png)
    2. In the Prefabs, select the List Box Item Container 2D prefab. In the Properties, add the Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment properties and set them to Stretch.
This way, you make the List Box Item Container 2D prefab stretch to the cell size of the Grid List Box 2D node.
![../../_images/list-box-item-container-2d-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/list-box-item-container-2d-in-project.png) ![../../_images/alignment-stretch1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/alignment-stretch1.png)
  2. In the Prefabs, select the List Box Item Container prefab. In the State Tools, create a State Manager with two states. See [Using state managers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html).
For example, name one state NotSelected and the other Selected.
The Selected state defines the state of your application when an item in the list box is selected, the NotSelected state when the item is not selected.
![../../_images/rename-states1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rename-states1.png)
  3. In the State Tools, click <No Controller Property>, select the List Box Item Container > Selected property, and set the value of the controller property for the Selected state to True.
In a state manager, the value of the property that you select as the Controller Property defines the conditions when each state in a state group is active.
![../../_images/selected-controller-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selected-controller-property.png) ![../../_images/set-controller-property-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-controller-property-selected.png)
  4. In the Prefabs, select the List Box Item Container prefab. In the Properties, add and set the properties whose values you want to change when a list box item is selected. Save different values of the properties to each state. You can also add nodes to the List Box Item Container prefab and make them visible only for the selected item.
For example, to change the background color of the selected list box item, add the Background Brush property, and set it to a color brush that you want to use to fill the background of the selected list box item. In the State Tools, click ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/store-current-values.png) below the Selected state to save the property value to that state.
![../../_images/selected-state-background-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selected-state-background-brush.png) ![../../_images/finished-states.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/finished-states.png)
  5. In the State Tools, click Edit State Manager to deactivate the State Tools.


In the Preview, when you click an item in the List Box node to select it, its appearance changes.
![../../_images/contacts-list-item-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contacts-list-item-selected.png)
## Enabling the double-click gesture for List Box items[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#enabling-the-double-click-gesture-for-list-box-items "Link to this heading")
When you add to a List Box node items that support the double-click gesture, you must enable the double-click gesture for those items in the List Box Item Container prefab.
To learn how to enable the double-click gesture for a node, see [Enabling the multi-click gesture for a node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/multi-click-manipulator.html#enabling-the-multi-click-gesture-for-a-node).
To enable the double-click gesture for List Box items:
  1. Create a List Box Item Container prefab and set it as the Item Container Template of the List Box node. See [Creating a List Box Item Container prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#create-list-box-item-container).
  2. In the Prefabs, select the List Box Item Container prefab. In the Properties, add and enable the Input > Double-Click Enabled property.
When you enable the Double-Click Enabled property, Kanzi installs in the List Box Item Container prefab a multi-click manipulator that generates double-click messages.
![../../_images/double-click-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/double-click-enabled.png)


## Using the List Box Item Container 3D prefab in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#using-the-list-box-item-container-3d-prefab-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `ListBoxItemContainer3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18694.html)` class.
## Using the List Box Item Container 2D prefab in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#using-the-list-box-item-container-2d-prefab-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `ListBoxItemContainer2D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18698.html)` class.
##  List Box Item Container property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#list-box-item-container-property-types "Link to this heading")

# Using the Long-Press Manipulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/long-press-manipulator.html#using-the-long-press-manipulator "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
