When Kanzi Studio loads a project, it shows in the Preview your project as if it was run as an application on a target device. You can control the Preview from the Project menu or use the shortcut keys.
![../../_images/preview-menu-preview-controls.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-menu-preview-controls.png)  
| Shortcut key  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `F5`  | Start the Preview in paused mode.  |  
| `F6`  | Start playing the Preview.  |  
| `F7`  | Pause the Preview.  |  
| `F8`  | Exit the Preview.  |  
| `F9`  | Stop the Preview.  |  
| `Ctrl` `F5`  |  Start the Preview in play mode. This is the default Preview setting when you open a Kanzi Studio project. To change this setting, go to Edit > User Preferences > Advanced > Preview.  |  
| `Ctrl` `F8`  | Restart the Preview.  |  
## Controlling keyboard input in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#controlling-keyboard-input-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
To control how the Preview handles keyboard input, when the Preview has focus and is in the Interact mode ![interact-mode](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/interact.png), in the Preview click ![keyboard-input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/keyboard-input.png).
For example, to set the Preview to pass to a Text Box node keyboard input also from the keys and key combinations that are reserved as Kanzi Studio shortcuts, enable the Keyboard Input mode.
![../../_images/keyboard-input-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/keyboard-input-enabled.png)
## Setting the font engine for the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#setting-the-font-engine-for-the-preview "Link to this heading")
You can set which font engine you want the Kanzi Studio Preview to use to render the text in your application.
To set the font engine for the Preview:
  1. In the main menu select Project > Properties.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png)
  2. In the Properties set the Font Engine property:
     * FreeType uses the FreeType rasterizer, HarfBuzz shaper, and ICU bidirectional library, and libunibreak for line breaking. This is the default font engine.
     * iType uses the Monotype iType rasterizer and WorldType® Shaper™ for shaping. See [Installing the iType font engine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#installing-the-itype-font-engine).
     * None to not load a font engine. When you do not load a font engine, the Preview does not render the text in your application.
![../../_images/font-engine.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-engine.png)


To learn how to set which font engine to load at application startup, see [FontEngine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#fontengine).
## Installing the iType font engine[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#installing-the-itype-font-engine "Link to this heading")
Submit the request for the Kanzi iType font engine through [support.rightware.com](http://support.rightware.com/).
To install the iType font engine for Kanzi Studio:
  1. Extract the zip file that contains the iType font engine Kanzi Engine plugin.
  2. Copy the dll file for each build configuration to the `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/EnginePlugins` directory.
For example, copy the `GL_vs<Version>_Release/kzitypeplugin.dll` to the `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/EnginePlugins/GL_vs<Version>_Release` directory.


## Setting the Graphics API for the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#setting-the-graphics-api-for-the-preview "Link to this heading")
To set the Graphics API used by the Preview:
  1. In the main menu, select Project > Properties.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png)
  2. In the Properties, set the Preview Graphics API Configuration property:
     * OpenGL is the default setting.
     * OpenGL ES creates an OpenGL ES context using the regular OpenGL driver. OpenGL ES differs from regular OpenGL in features such as depth mipmaps, color formats, texture compression, and shader language.
     * Vulkan is a newer graphics API that allows efficient usage of graphics card resources.
You can set the default value for all your Kanzi Studio projects in the Edit > User Preferences > Advanced, by setting Preview Graphics API Configuration.
![../../_images/preview-opengl-es.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-opengl-es.png)


## Setting the background color of the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#setting-the-background-color-of-the-preview "Link to this heading")
The background of the Preview is by default black. To make your content stand out from the background when the Preview is in the Interact mode ![interact-mode](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/interact.png), you can set the background color:
  * For all your Kanzi Studio projects.
In the main menu, select Edit > User Preferences. In the Preview tab, set the Background Color property to the desired color.
![../../_images/edit-user-preferences.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/edit-user-preferences.png) ![../../_images/preview-background-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-background-color.png)
  * For a specific Kanzi Studio project.
In the main menu, select Project > Properties. In the Properties > Preview property category, add and set the Preview Background Color property to the desired color.
When you do not set this property, the project uses the color that you set in the User Preferences.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/properties-project-preview-background-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-project-preview-background-color.png)

![../../_images/preview-with-background-color-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-with-background-color-set.png)
## Showing only the content of Page nodes and prefabs in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#showing-only-the-content-of-page-nodes-and-prefabs-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
By default the Preview shows your entire Kanzi project as when it is run as an application on a target device. However, you can isolate parts of your application and view each as a separate item in the Preview. This means that you can work on the content of a prefab without instantiating the prefab.
  * To show only the content of a prefab in the Preview, in the Prefabs double-click that prefab.
Kanzi Studio opens the prefab in a new Preview tab and shows the content of that prefab in the Preview.
![../../_images/prefab-composition-open.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefab-composition-open.png)
  * To show only the content of a Page node, in the Node Tree or Pages double-click that page.
Kanzi Studio opens the Page node in a new tab and shows the content of that Page node in the Preview.
![../../_images/page-composition-open.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/page-composition-open.png)


When you isolate content in this way, in the Preview, you can control that part of your application in the Preview with the timeline controls you can find in the bottom of Kanzi Studio. To show the timeline, in the Kanzi Studio main menu select Window > Toolbar > Timeline.
![../../_images/timeline.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/timeline.svg)
The Preview shows prefabs in your application either in play or paused mode:
  * In the play mode the prefab functions just as it would as a standalone application: user interface components are interactive and animations are playing.
  * In the paused mode the animations stop, but the user interface components remain active. If components execute animations, these are not played until you enter the playing mode.


When the Preview is in paused mode, you can set the application time in the timeline bar.
You can use these playback modes in the Preview.  
| Playback mode  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/continuous-play.png)  | In the continuous play mode the Preview starts playing at start time you set in the timeline bar, but does not have a set end time.  |  
| ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/play-range.png)  | In the play range mode the Preview plays in a loop the range between the start and end times you set in the timeline bar.  |  
| ![image2](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/play-range-and-stop.png)  | In the play range and stop mode the Preview plays once the range between the start and end times you set in the timeline bar.  |

# Analyzing your application in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html#analyzing-your-application-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
In the Preview, click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to analyze the performance and structure of your application.
When in the Analyze mode, right-click ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png) or use the Preview main menu to select the type of items that you want to analyze.
![../../_images/debug-mode.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/debug-mode.png)
In addition to the Preview Analyze mode, Kanzi provides other ways to help you analyze your application. See [Troubleshooting the performance of your application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/performance/measuring-performance-of-your-application.html) and [Best practices](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/best-practices.html).
Tip
To customize how Kanzi Studio shows different types of items in the Analyze mode, select Edit > User Preferences, and in the Preview tab set the color and line thickness for the items.
![../../_images/preferences-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preferences-preview.png)
## Selection and layout[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html#selection-and-layout "Link to this heading")  
|  ![../../_images/selection.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection.png)  | Selection highlights the selected nodes. See [Editing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html).  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ![../../_images/debug-objects.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/debug-objects.png)  |  Debug objects shows:
  * Visualization nodes, such as light, camera, and layout nodes.
  * Debug visualizations that you create for your custom 3D nodes. For an example of such visualization, see the [Node3D plugin example](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/examples/node3d-plugin/node3d-plugin.html).

 |  
|  ![../../_images/allocated-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/allocated-layout.png)  | Allocated layout shows bounding boxes of the spaces allocated to items under layouts. See [Layout control nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/layouts.html).  |  
|  ![../../_images/actual-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/actual-layout.png)  | Actual layout shows bounding boxes of spaces used by items under layouts. See [Layout control nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/layouts.html).  |  
|  ![../../_images/grid-cells.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-cells.png)  | Grid cells shows the cells of Grid Layout 2D nodes. See [Using the Grid Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html).  |  
## Rulers, guides, and borders[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html#rulers-guides-and-borders "Link to this heading")  
|  ![../../_images/rullers-and-guide.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rullers-and-guide.png)  | Rulers and guides shows rulers and guides which help you position the elements in your application. See [Using rulers and guides](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/using-rulers-and-guides.html).  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ![../../_images/border-of-2d-nodes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/border-of-2d-nodes.png)  | Borders of 2D nodes outlines the borders of 2D nodes with striped lines.  |  
## 3D content[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html#d-content "Link to this heading")  
|  ![../../_images/3d-grid.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/3d-grid.png)  | 3D Grid shows the ground plane grid in Scene nodes.  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ![../../_images/bounding-volumes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/bounding-volumes.png)  | Bounding volumes shows meshes in closed volumes.  |  
## Rendering[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html#rendering "Link to this heading")  
|  ![../../_images/framebuffer.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/framebuffer.png)  |  Framebuffer objects marks with translucent yellow moving stripes node which are rendered into textures and cause a framebuffer object switch. See [Rendering best practices](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/rendering-best-practices.html).  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ![../../_images/undrawn.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/undrawn.png)  | Undrawn area shows the updating of the areas beyond the application screen and the areas with content not rendered.  |  
|  ![../../_images/transparency.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/transparency.png)  | Transparency marks transparent nodes with translucent blue moving stripes. See [Configuring nodes for efficient rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/setting-layers-for-efficient-rendering.html).  |  
|  ![../../_images/overdrawn.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/overdrawn.png)  |  Overdraw visualization indicates areas where Kanzi renders multiple times to the same pixel. Lighter green color indicates higher amount of overdraw. See [Preventing overdraw with the Sorting Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/preventing-overdraw-with-sorting-filters.html).  |  
|  ![../../_images/wireframe.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/wireframe.png)  |  Wireframe draws all content in wireframe mode, which shows the geometry of meshes. Keep in mind that Kanzi applies the wireframe mode to the content globally. For example, the mode renders as wireframes also post-processing effects and the content that you blit on the screen using render passes.  |  
|  ![../../_images/vertex-normals.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/vertex-normals.png)  |  Vertex normals visualizes the normals of mesh vertices as RGB colors. The values of the red, green, and blue color channels represent the x, y, and z values of the normal direction vector in the local space of the mesh. Kanzi calculates the value of each color channel from the value of the corresponding direction vector component according to this formula: ColorChannel=0.5+0.5∗VectorComponent  |  
## Performance[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html#performance "Link to this heading")
  * Performance HUD shows the overall performance indicators of your Kanzi application during the last 500 frames including:
    * Frame Duration (ms) shows the time in milliseconds it took to render the last frame, and the average, highest, and lowest times.
The top value in the Frame Duration (ms) graph shows the longest, and the bottom value the average time it took to render a frame during the last 500 frames.
Use this information to identify performance bottlenecks in your Kanzi application. For example, you can use it to find out how to improve the performance of your application by distributing rendering across several frames. See [Distributing rendering across several frames](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/distributing-rendering.html).
    * API shows the rendering API used by Kanzi. For Example, OpenGL ES or Vulkan. It also shows an identifier of the video card and driver version.
![../../_images/frame-duration-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/frame-duration-graph.png)
    * Frames Per Second shows the number of frames rendered per second.
    * Animation Duration (μs) shows the time in microseconds it takes to execute all animations in the application for the last frame, and the average, highest, and lowest times.
    * Draw Count shows how many individual draw calls were executed.
The top value in the Draw Count graph shows the highest number of batches during the last 500 frames, and the bottom value the number of batches in the last frame.
![../../_images/draw-count-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-count-graph.png)
    * Triangle Count shows an estimated total of individual triangles drawn during a frame.
    * Pipeline Count shows how many times a new render pipeline was bound for the last frame. See [Reducing shader switches](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/shaders/reducing-shader-switches.html).
    * Pass Count shows how many render passes were used in the last frame. See [Rendering best practices](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/rendering-best-practices.html).
    * Memory Upload shows how many bytes of rolling staging memory were used on the last frame as well as the total buffer size. Staging memory contains uniform data and temporary storage used for updating GPU resources like vertex buffers or textures. On some platforms unique buffers are used for each type of data.
    * Dispatch Count shows how many compute dispatches were used in the last frame.
    * Kanzi Graphics Objects shows a summary of the created Kanzi Graphics objects. In parenthesis is the number of created and deleted objects in the last frame.
    * View Camera shows the name of the Camera node that is used for displaying the scene in your application.
    * Resource Memory Use shows an estimated amount of local GPU memory (VRAM) and non-local GPU memory (RAM) that your Kanzi application uses.
The values that the Performance HUD shows in the Kanzi Studio Preview and when you run the Kanzi application on a target device differ because Kanzi Studio loads and keeps in memory all resources in the application.
    * Timers shows the number of registered timer handlers in the `MainLoopScheduler[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13618.html)`. Too many timer handlers can decrease the performance of your application. See [Adding timers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html#adding-timers).
You can access the number of timer subscriptions in the Kanzi Engine API by calling `MainLoopScheduler::getTimersCount[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13618.html#adb14c61cae8da0bafd9075ce9bbe843c)`.
    * Recurring Tasks shows the total number of tasks that were added to the stages in the main loop scheduler. The Kanzi Engine adds some tasks by default. See [Adding recurring tasks](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html#adding-recurring-tasks).
You can access the number of recurring tasks in the Kanzi Engine API by calling `MainLoopScheduler::getTasksTotalCount[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13618.html#ad2f01ce01e69e3a92f0046a65ba050ee)`.
    * Animations shows the number of active and all animations in your Kanzi application.
You can access the number of animations in the Kanzi Engine API:
      * To get the number of active animations, use `TimelineClock::getActiveTimelinePlaybackCount[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11342.html#a0e214a8ff26ac6d9f508fcd6ef0f3029)`.
      * To get the number of all animations, use `TimelineClock::getTimelinePlaybackCount[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11342.html#a5bb2a2aec4b32baeb21c134faab6c998)`.
  * Frame time HUD shows these frame time indicators of your Kanzi application during the last 500 frames:
    * Frame Duration (ms) shows the time in milliseconds it took to render the last frame, and the average, highest, and lowest times.
    * Frames Per Second shows the number of frames rendered per second.
    * Animation Duration (μs) shows the time in microseconds it takes to execute all animations in the application for the last frame, and the average, highest, and lowest times.


## The Preview log file[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html#the-preview-log-file "Link to this heading")
Kanzi Studio stores the Preview log messages in the `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Temp\KanziStudioLogs\KanziPreview.log` file.
To set the level of logging detail, in the `<KanziInstallation>\Studio\Bin\KanziPreview.exe.config` file set the value of the `logLevel` key:
  * `NORMAL` sets Kanzi Studio to log the regular Kanzi Studio Preview flow, including errors and exceptions.
  * `VERBOSE` sets Kanzi Studio to log all low-level communication between Kanzi Studio and the Preview at a millisecond-level of precision.
When you set the log level to `VERBOSE`, the large amount of log messages can reduce the performance of Kanzi Studio.
  * `NONE` sets Kanzi Studio to not log any messages to the `KanziPreview.log` file.


For example, to log all communication between Kanzi Studio and the Preview, open the `KanziPreview.exe.config` file in a text editor, and set:

```
<add key="logLevel" value="VERBOSE"/>

```
Copy to clipboard
To apply the changes to the `KanziPreview.exe.config`, save the `KanziPreview.exe.config` file and press `Ctrl` `F8` to restart the Preview. See [Controlling the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html).
Every time you restart the Preview, Kanzi Studio overwrites the contents of the `KanziPreview.log` file.
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html#sa "Link to this heading")

Rulers and guides help you position the elements in your application.
To use rulers and guides, in the Preview:
  1. Select the Node tool ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png).
  2. Click ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to enter the Analyze mode.
  3. Right-click ![image2](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png), and select Rulers and guides.

![../../_images/visualize-rulers-and-guides.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/visualize-rulers-and-guides.png)
## Adding a guide[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/using-rulers-and-guides.html#adding-a-guide "Link to this heading")
To add a guide, in the Preview select the Node tool ![image3](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png) and drag a ruler to the preview area. Drag from the horizontal ruler to add a horizontal guide, and from the vertical ruler to add a vertical guide.
Tip
Use the Snap tool to snap an element in your application to a guide. To enable snapping, in the Node Tree select a 2D node, in the Preview select the Node tool ![image4](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png) , and select ![image5](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-snap.png). When you move 2D node in your application, it snaps to the nearest guide.
![../../_images/add-guide.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-guide.gif) ![../../_images/horizontal-and-vertical-guide.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/horizontal-and-vertical-guide.png)
## Moving a guide[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/using-rulers-and-guides.html#moving-a-guide "Link to this heading")
To move a guide, in the Preview select the Node tool ![image7](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png) and drag the guide you want to move.
![../../_images/move-guide.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/move-guide.png)
## Removing a guide[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/using-rulers-and-guides.html#removing-a-guide "Link to this heading")
To remove a guide, in the Preview select the Node tool ![image9](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png), drag the guide, and drop it on the ruler.
![../../_images/remove-guide.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/remove-guide.gif)
## Removing all guides[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/using-rulers-and-guides.html#removing-all-guides "Link to this heading")
To remove all guides, in the Preview select the Node tool ![image10](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png), right-click one of the guides, and select Delete all guides.
![../../_images/delete-all-guides.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/delete-all-guides.png)

# Prism graphs[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#prism-graphs "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Prism graph editor is a visual node tool for creating render graphs. You can add or remove rendering nodes and quickly iterate on visual effects. Graphs provide a clear overview of rendering operations, let you adjust properties, and show results instantly.
Prism simplifies rendering complexities into a handful of basic primitive operations. A typical graph consists of one or more draw operations, shadow rendering operations, and post-processing effect compositions.
A Prism graph consists of nodes such as Draw, Blit, Clear and other more advanced nodes. Nodes are linked together using connections to form a render pipeline, where each operation runs according to the graph structure. Every graph has an output node that displays the final result on screen.
See [Creating Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html) for a walkthrough on creating a Prism graph.
## Prism graph presets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#prism-graph-presets "Link to this heading")
Prism offers quick presets to get started when you create a new graph. You can find the available presets when you create a new graph. Go to **Library** > **Prism Graphs** , right-click on **Prism Graphs** , and select **Create** > **Template**.
![../../_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png)
### Default Prism Graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#default-prism-graph "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/default-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/default-graph.png)
A preset configuration for a render graph similar to Kanzi’s default render pass. The preset draws opaque and transparent objects.
This is a good general starting point to start customizing your rendering.
### Empty Prism Graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#empty-prism-graph "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/empty-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/empty-graph.png)
Empty Prism graph only has an output node. By default, this graph doesn’t render anything.
### Offscreen Buffer Prism Graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#offscreen-buffer-prism-graph "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/offscreen-framebuffer-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/offscreen-framebuffer-graph.png)
A preset tailored for quickly starting with offscreen or post-processing effects. The graph renders objects to screen and then composites a full-screen shader using blit nodes.
This is a good starting point for building post-processing or offscreen rendering effects where you want to apply a shader to all pixels on screen.
## Navigating the Prism editor[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#navigating-the-prism-editor "Link to this heading")  
| Action  | Shortcut  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Select  | Left-click a node or connection  |  
| Pan  | Middle mouse button  |  
| Zoom  | Mouse wheel  |  
## Working with Prism graphs[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#working-with-prism-graphs "Link to this heading")
Here are the most common operations for editing Prism graphs.
### Creating nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#creating-nodes "Link to this heading")
**Right-click** in the graph and select a node type.
![../../_images/creating-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/creating-prism-nodes.gif)
### Deleting nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#deleting-nodes "Link to this heading")
Select a node and press `Delete`.
Or **right-click** and select **Delete**.
![../../_images/deleting-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/deleting-nodes.gif)
### Connecting nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#connecting-nodes "Link to this heading")
Drag from a socket with the **left mouse button**. Release on a valid socket to connect.
![../../_images/connecting-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/connecting-prism-nodes.gif)
### Disconnecting nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#disconnecting-nodes "Link to this heading")
Select a connection and press `Delete`.
Or right-click and select **Delete**.
![../../_images/disconnecting-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/disconnecting-prism-nodes.gif)
To delete multiple connections, hold `Shift` + `Alt` and draw a line over the connections.
![../../_images/disconnecting-multiple-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/disconnecting-multiple-prism-nodes.gif)
### Adding properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#adding-properties "Link to this heading")
Click the **+** icon on a node and select a property.
![../../_images/adding-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/adding-properties.gif)
You can add multiple properties by clicking a property category.
![../../_images/adding-multiple-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/adding-multiple-properties.gif)
Tip
Each Viewport that shares a Prism graph can override individual material property values independently. Select a property on a Prism node and click the Override value from Viewport button to set a per-Viewport value without affecting other Viewports that use the same graph.
![../../_images/prism-override-property.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prism-override-property.gif)
### Removing properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#removing-properties "Link to this heading")
Right-click a property and select **Delete**.
![../../_images/deleting-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/deleting-properties.gif)
### Adding and removing properties on a Render Pass node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#adding-and-removing-properties-on-a-render-pass-node "Link to this heading")
On a **Render Pass** node, click ![add-properties-window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png) to open the Add Properties window. Use the window to add or remove any property the render pass supports.
### Binding Render Pass node properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#binding-render-pass-node-properties "Link to this heading")
You can bind a property on a Render Pass node so its value is driven by another property or by a binding expression. The following types of property bindings are supported:
  * **Resource property bindings.** Drag a binding line directly between two resource properties of the same type.
![Animation of dragging a binding line between two resource properties on different Prism nodes.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/bind-toplevelas.gif)
  * **Text property bindings.** Right-click a non-resource property row and select Edit binding… to drive the property from a binding expression. The row then shows a binding indicator and a read-only preview of the expression.
![A Prism property row showing a binding indicator on the label and a read-only expression preview in place of the value editor.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clear-color-bound-row.gif)


See [Binding Render Pass node properties](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-prism-property-bindings.html) for worked examples.
### Minimap[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#minimap "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/minimap.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/minimap.png)
![minimap_icon](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/minimap-toggle.png)
You can enable the minimap from the top-left corner of the Prism editor.
The minimap shows an overview of your graph. A light rectangle shows the visible area in the Prism Editor. Use the minimap to navigate large graphs.  
| Action  | Shortcut  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Resize  | Drag the lower-left corner of the minimap  |  
| Zoom  | Scroll the mouse wheel  |  
| Center view  | Click in the minimap  |  
| Pan  | Drag in the minimap  |  
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Creating Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html)
[Creating Bloom Effect with Prism Graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html)
[Adding shadows to Prism render graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html)
[Binding Render Pass node properties](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-prism-property-bindings.html)

This tutorial guides you through building a basic render graph. You’ll learn how to create render graphs, add nodes, and connect nodes together to create a complete render graph.
## Creating an empty graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html#creating-an-empty-graph "Link to this heading")
Start by creating a new **Prism graph** :
  1. In the **Library** , find Rendering, right-click on Prism Graphs, and select **Create** > **Empty Prism Graph**.
![../../_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png)
A new graph is created. The graph is not used for rendering yet. It has to be connected to a viewport.
  2. Select the viewport you want to render with the graph. In the **Properties** panel, go to Render Pass Prefab and select your graph from the dropdown list.
Your viewport will now stop rendering. **This is normal** because the render graph is currently empty. Rendering will be enabled in the following steps.
![../../_images/viewport-select.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/viewport-select.png) ![../../_images/property-view.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/property-view.png)


## Add and connect nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html#add-and-connect-nodes "Link to this heading")
  1. Open your graph by double-clicking it in the **Library** folder.
The initial graph is empty and only contains an output node.
![../../_images/empty-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/empty-prism-graph.png)
Render graph is where you define how Kanzi renders each frame. The graph consists of nodes and connections between them. Nodes can be basic nodes, offscreen nodes, advanced nodes, or render pass nodes.
     * **Basic** nodes are primitive rendering operations: Draw, Clear, and Blit.
     * **Offscreen** nodes are render targets where drawing results are stored and used.
     * **Advanced** nodes are quick shortcuts to common rendering operations, such as adding shadows or rendering post-processing effects.
     * **Render Pass** nodes map directly to engine render pass types, giving you fine-grained control over the rendering pipeline. Examples include Build Acceleration Structure and Compute.
In this tutorial, we’ll cover the basic nodes to learn the fundamentals first.
  2. To add a clear node, right-click anywhere on the graph and select **Add Node** > **Basic Node** > **Clear**.
  3. Similarly, add a draw node by selecting **Add Node** > **Basic Node** > **Draw**.
![../../_images/node-creation.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-creation.gif)
**Clear node** clears the target it is connected to. Often this is a draw node, where the first operation is to clear the previously rendered frame color or depth information.
**Draw node** renders objects to screen or into a render target.
All the required nodes are now there with no errors, but they are not rendering anything on the screen yet. The next step is to make connections to complete the graph.
Tip
Use the **Object Source** property to define which objects to draw.
![../../_images/select-object-source.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-object-source.png)
  4. Connect the clear node to the draw node, and the draw node to the output node by dragging connections from the node output socket.
![../../_images/node-connections.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-connections.gif)
Once the connections are done, your graph is now valid and complete. You should now see 3D objects being rendered in your preview window.


## Modify node properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html#modify-node-properties "Link to this heading")
You can modify each node by adding new properties to it. Next, add a color property to the clear node to change rendering background color.
  1. Click the + icon below the clear node and add the **Clear Color 0** property to it.
![../../_images/add-color-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-color-property.png)
  2. Adjust the background color by adjusting the color property.
![../../_images/custom-graph-finished.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/custom-graph-finished.png)


Tip
Each Viewport that shares a Prism graph can override individual material property values independently. Select a property on a Prism node and click the Override value from Viewport button to set a per-Viewport value without affecting other Viewports that use the same graph.
![../../_images/prism-override-property.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prism-override-property.gif)
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html)

# Creating Bloom Effect with Prism Graphs[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html#creating-bloom-effect-with-prism-graphs "Link to this heading")

These steps guide you through creating a Prism graph with Bloom and tonemap post-processing effects. Learn how to set up a scene with a 3D model, configure lighting for HDR rendering, and build a complete render graph with bloom effects.
## Import and Set Up the Car Model[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html#import-and-set-up-the-car-model "Link to this heading")
  1. Ensure you are working with Linear color flow. Find this setting in **Project** > **Properties** and **Binary Export** settings > **Color Workflow** and set it to **Linear** >
  2. Import your car model into the project:
     * In the **Asset Packages** window, right-click **Asset Toolkit** > **Car** and select **Import Asset Package**.
     * The Car will appear in your **Prefabs** window when the import completes.
![../../_images/assetpackages-import-car.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assetpackages-import-car.png)
  3. Add the car model to your Scene:
     * Drag the imported model from the **Prefabs** into your Scene hierarchy.
![../../_images/add-car-to-scene.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-car-to-scene.gif)
     * Position the camera node or modify the Car model scaling and position in the **Preview** window.
![../../_images/car-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-properties.gif)


## Configure Lighting for HDR[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html#configure-lighting-for-hdr "Link to this heading")
For bloom effects to work properly, your materials should support the Emissive Factor property, which allows producing colors in the HDR range. The Asset Toolkit Car model supports this by default
  1. Select the light materials in your Scene. In the **Library** , expand the **Material Types** and navigate to **PhysicallyBased** > **PBR BrakeLight** for example
  2. Select the **PBR BrakeLight** material and in the **Properties** panel, adjust the **Emissive Factor** property.
![../../_images/adjust-emissive-factor.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/adjust-emissive-factor.gif)
Tip
Emissive Factor Intensity values greater than 0.0 produce HDR colors that will enhance the bloom effect. The higher the value, the stronger the bloom effect.
  3. Set the Emissive Factor Intensity to a grater value (for example, 7.0 ) to create bright areas that will bloom.
  4. Apply a high **Emissive Factor** property value to all of the materials where you want to enhance the bloom effects (for example, the headlights, brake lights and turn signals). In the Car model from the **Asset Toolkit** , the **PhysicallyBased** materials **PBR BrakeLight** , **PBR HeadLight** and **PBR TurnLight** are used.


## Create a Prism Graph with Bloom[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html#create-a-prism-graph-with-bloom "Link to this heading")
### Create an Empty Graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html#create-an-empty-graph "Link to this heading")
  1. In the **Library** , find Rendering, right-click on Prism Graphs, and select **Create** > **Empty Prism Graph** and name it **Prism Graph** for example.
![../../_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png)
A new graph is created. The graph is not used for rendering yet. To use it, it must have nodes, and must be set as the **Render Pass Prefab** of the Viewport 2D.
  2. Select the viewport you want to render with the graph. In the **Properties** panel, go to **Render Pass Prefab** and select your graph from the dropdown list.
Your viewport will stop rendering, because the render graph is still empty. Rendering will be enabled in the next steps.
![../../_images/viewport-car-select.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/viewport-car-select.png) ![../../_images/property-view.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/property-view.png)


### Add Rendering Nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html#add-rendering-nodes "Link to this heading")
  1. To open your graph, double-click it in the **Library** folder.
The initial graph is empty and only contains an output node.
![../../_images/empty-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/empty-prism-graph.png)
  2. To add an **Offscreen Framebuffer Node** , right-click on the graph and select **Add Node** > **Offscreen** > **Framebuffer**.
  3. To add **Color Format 0** property to the **Offscreen Framebuffer Node** , click the **+** button and select **Aspect** > **Color Format 0**. This property must be set to **R16G16B16A16_Float** to support HDR rendering.
![../../_images/add-offscreen-framebuffer.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-offscreen-framebuffer.gif)
  4. To add a **Multi-Draw node** , by select **Add Node** > **Advanced** > **Multi-Draw**.
![../../_images/multi-draw-node-creation.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/multi-draw-node-creation.gif)
     * Set the **Clear Color 0** property to your desired background color.
Tip
Use the **Object Sources** property to define which object sources to draw, and organize them in the order you want it to be done.
![../../_images/reorganize-draw-passes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reorganize-draw-passes.gif)
  5. To add a **Bloom node** , right-click on the graph and select **Add Node** > **Advanced** > **Bloom**.
![../../_images/add-bloom-node.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-bloom-node.gif)
The Bloom node creates a glow effect around bright areas of your scene, particularly useful for HDR lighting. Adjust the properties to control the intensity and spread of the bloom effect.
  6. To add a **Tonemap node** , right-click on the graph and select **Add Node** > **Advanced** > **Tonemap**.
![../../_images/add-tonemap-node.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-tonemap-node.gif)
The Tonemap node converts HDR color values to LDR (Low Dynamic Range) for display, preserving detail in both bright and dark areas.


### Connect the Nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html#connect-the-nodes "Link to this heading")
  1. Connect the nodes in the following order:
     * Connect the **Offscreen Framebuffer node** output to the **Multi-Draw node** input.
     * Connect the **Multi-Draw node** output to the **Bloom node** input.
     * Connect the **Bloom node** output to the **Tonemap node** input.
     * Connect the **Tonemap node** output to the **Output node** input.
> ![../../_images/graph-node-connections.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/graph-node-connections.gif)
  2. Once the connections are complete, your graph is now valid and you should see your car model rendered with bloom and tonemap effects applied. Use the next steps to adjust the bloom and tonemap settings to achieve your desired visual effect.


## Adjust Bloom and Tonemap Settings[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html#adjust-bloom-and-tonemap-settings "Link to this heading")
  1. Select the **Bloom node** in the graph.
  2. In the **Properties** panel, adjust the bloom settings:
     * **Bloom Intensity** controls the strength of the bloom effect. Set this value to around 0.15 to start with.
     * **Bloom Radius** controls the spread of the bloom glow. Set this value to around 0.5 to start with.
![../../_images/set-bloom-values.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-bloom-values.gif)
Tip
The **Bloom Intensity Texture** property can be used to define which areas of the scene will bloom based on brightness levels. Use a grayscale texture where white areas bloom the most.
  3. Select the **Tonemap node** in the graph.
  4. In the **Properties** panel, adjust the tonemap settings. The White Scale for example controls the overall brightness of the tonemapped image. Adjusted this to 10.0 to start with.
[![../../_images/set-tonemap-values.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-tonemap-values.gif)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-tonemap-values.gif)
  5. Adjust the **Emissive Factor** values on your materials to control which areas bloom, and in which color.
  6. Modify the **Clear Color 0** property on the **Multi-Draw** node if you want to change the background color.
  7. Preview the results in real-time as you adjust the properties.
![../../_images/final-result.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/final-result.png)


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html)

# Adding shadows to Prism render graphs[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#adding-shadows-to-prism-render-graphs "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
![../../_images/car-shadows.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-shadows.png)
These steps show how to add different shadow types to Prism render graphs and how to define which objects cast shadows.
For an introduction to Prism graphs, see [Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html) for a walkthrough on creating a basic Prism graph first.
## Scene setup[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#scene-setup "Link to this heading")
Creating a basic scene where shadows can be tested.
  1. Add objects you want to cast shadows into the scene.
This example uses a ground box and a car model from the Kanzi Studio Asset Toolkit package. You can follow along with any objects you have.
  2. Navigate to **Asset Packages** and select **Asset Toolkit** > **Car** from the asset browsing view. Use your mouse to drag and drop the car model into your scene.
![../../_images/drag-drop-car.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/drag-drop-car.gif)
  3. Add a ground box to the scene by right clicking on **Scene** > **Create** > **Box**.
![../../_images/create-box-ground.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-box-ground.png)
  4. Use the **Transform 3D** property in the **Properties** panel to adjust the position and scale of the box.
![../../_images/ground-box-transform.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/ground-box-transform.png)
  5. Select the ground box from the scene. In the **Properties** , go to the **Mesh Material** property and click the **Navigate to selected item** button to highlight the material of the model.
![../../_images/select-model.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-model.png)
  6. Switch the material type to **SmartPhysicallyBased** by selecting it from the **Material Type** dropdown menu.
This switches the material to use **Smart Physically Based Material** type, which is the easiest way to use shadows. Smart materials make it easy to enable or disable shader features on demand. To learn more about smart materials, see [Using smart materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-smart-materials.html).
![../../_images/select-smart-physically-based-material.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-smart-physically-based-material.gif)


Note
If you do not already have Smart Physically Based Material type in your project, you can create one by right-clicking in the **Library** > **Materials and Textures** > **Material Types** and selecting **Create** > **Material Type** > **SmartPhysicallyBased**.
Creating a new material type will automatically also add a matching material to the project. Use that material on the ground box.
![../../_images/create-smart-pbr-type.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-smart-pbr-type.png)
### Shadow material properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#shadow-material-properties "Link to this heading")
The material type does not have shadow features enabled by default. The shaders must be enabled to support each shadow type.
  1. Click **Navigate to selected item** on the **Material Type** field to select the SmartPhysicallyBasedMaterial type in the Library.
![../../_images/select-material-type.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-material-type.png)
  2. Click the **Add Properties** button on the bottom-right corner of the **Properties** menu. Enable **Shadow for Directional Light** , **Shadow for Point Light** , and **Shadow for Spot Light**.
The smart materials are now ready to receive shadows.
![../../_images/select-shadow-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-shadow-properties.gif)


Tip
When the project does not use smart materials, enabling shadows on custom materials requires setting preprocessor definitions in the material.
Open the **Material Type** and scroll down to the **Preprocessor Definitions** section. Enable KANZI_SHADER_RECEIVE_SPOT_SHADOW, KANZI_SHADER_RECEIVE_POINT_SHADOW, and KANZI_SHADER_RECEIVE_DIRECTIONAL_SHADOW by setting their values to 1.
This enables each corresponding shadow type on the material.
![../../_images/set-shader-preprocessor-definitions.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-shader-preprocessor-definitions.png)
## Creating a Prism graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#creating-a-prism-graph "Link to this heading")
  1. Go to **Library** > **Rendering** > **Prism Graphs**.
  2. Right-click the **Prism Graphs** folder and select **Create** > **Default Prism Graph**.
Default Prism graph is a great starting point for most render graphs.
![../../_images/create-default-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-default-prism-graph.png)
  3. Select the **Viewport 2D** to render with the graph. From the viewport **Properties** , find the **Render Pass Prefab** property and select the created Prism graph from the dropdown.
The rendering may look the same as before, but the created Prism graph is now in use.
![../../_images/select-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-prism-graph.png)


## Spot shadows[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#spot-shadows "Link to this heading")
  1. On the scene object, hold down `Alt` and right-click to open object creation menu. Select **Spot Light** to create a new spotlight. Move the spotlight to a position where it lights an object to cast shadows.
![../../_images/create-spotlight.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-spotlight.png)
  2. Open the Prism graph by **double-clicking** it in the **Library**.
![../../_images/open-default-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-default-prism-graph.png)
  3. Add a new **Generate Shadow Map** node to the graph. Select the spot light from the **Light** dropdown.
  4. Add the **Spot Shadow Map** property to the **Multi-Draw** node by clicking the **+** icon and selecting **Shadows** > **Spot Shadow Map**.
  5. Connect the output socket of the **Generate Shadow Map** node, to the **Spot Shadow Map** socket of the **Multi-Draw** node.
![../../_images/building-spotlight-graph.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/building-spotlight-graph.gif)
The graph is now complete and objects should cast spot shadows.
![../../_images/car-spot-shadows.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-spot-shadows.png)


### Adjusting shadow contact point[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#adjusting-shadow-contact-point "Link to this heading")
Sometimes shadows may appear to float slightly above the surface. Shadows have near and far plane settings that define the depth range of the shadow map. Both of these settings affect how shadows align with the surface.
These settings can be adjusted by adding **Camera Near** , **Camera Far** , and **Shadow Bias** properties to the light source.
![../../_images/fix-foating-shadows.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fix-foating-shadows.gif)
Tip
A common issue is shadow acne, where shadows appear speckled or have artifacts. This is often due to precision issues in the shadow map. Adding **Spot Shadow Bias** , **Point Shadow Bias** , or **Directional Shadow Bias** to the corresponding light type can help.
### Adjusting shadow resolution[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#adjusting-shadow-resolution "Link to this heading")
Shadow map resolution can be adjusted in Prism editor.
Click the **+** icon on the **Generate Shadow Map** node and add the **Width** and **Height** properties and adjust the values.
Increasing the resolution improves shadow quality at the cost of performance.
![../../_images/adding-size-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/adding-size-properties.gif)
## Point shadows[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#point-shadows "Link to this heading")
Point shadows are largely similar to spot shadows, but they cast shadows in all directions from a point in space.
In Kanzi, the main difference is how shadow map resolution is set up in the Prism graph.
  1. Hold down `Alt` and right-click on **Scene**. Select **Point Light**.
  2. Open the Prism graph by double-clicking it in the **Library**.
  3. Add a new **Generate Shadow Map** node to the graph and add a **Point Shadow Map** property to the **Multi-Draw** node.
The **Point Shadow Map** node composites a given cubemap depth into the Multi-Draw pass. It expects a cubemap depth texture as input to its socket.
  4. Connect the **Generate Shadow Map** node’s output socket to the **Multi-Draw** node’s **Point Shadow Map** socket.
  5. Select the point light from the **Light** dropdown.
The light must be **Point Light** type for point shadows to work.
![../../_images/building-pointlight-graph.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/building-pointlight-graph.gif)


Similar to spot shadows, **Camera Near** , **Camera Far** , and **Shadow Bias** properties can be added to the light source to adjust shadow appearance. See [Adjusting shadow contact point](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#adjusting-shadow-contact-point) for more details.
The Prism graph is now complete and objects should cast point shadows.
![../../_images/final-graph-spotlights.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/final-graph-spotlights.png) ![../../_images/car-point-and-spot-shadows.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-point-and-spot-shadows.png)
### Increasing point light shadow resolution[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#increasing-point-light-shadow-resolution "Link to this heading")
The resolution can be increased from the **Generate Shadow Map** node properties if the default resolution needs adjusting.
  1. Click the **+** icon on the **Generate Shadow Map** node and add the **Cubemap Resolution** property.
  2. Increase the resolution to a higher value, such as 256, to increase the shadow quality.


Note that higher resolution shadows may impact performance.
![../../_images/pointlight-shadow-resolution.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/pointlight-shadow-resolution.png)
## Directional shadows[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#directional-shadows "Link to this heading")
Directional shadows are often used to simulate sunlight or other distant light sources.
The process is similar to other shadow types, but directional shadows require additional properties to define the shadow area.
  1. Right-click on **Scene** and select **Create** > **Directional Light**.
  2. Select the light and click the **Add Properties** button on the bottom-right of the **Properties** panel. Add the **Z Far** , **Z Near** , and **Orthographic Plane Size** properties to it.
These properties define the area where shadows are rendered. Adjust these values to cover the area where shadows are needed. Orthographic Plane Size defines the size of the shadow casting area, while Z Near and Z Far define the depth range.
![../../_images/select-directional-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-directional-properties.gif)
After configuring the light properties, set up the shadow map in the Prism graph.
  3. Open the Prism graph by double-clicking it in the **Library**.
  4. Add a new **Generate Shadow Map** node to the graph and add a **Directional Shadow Map** property to the **Multi-Draw** node.
  5. Connect the output socket of the **Generate Shadow Map** node to the **Directional Shadow Map** socket of the **Multi-Draw** node.
  6. Select the directional light from the **Light** dropdown.
The light must be **Directional Light** type for directional shadows to work.
See [Adjusting shadow resolution](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#adjusting-shadow-resolution) to learn how to adjust shadow resolution.
The graph is now complete.


The final Prism graph with all three shadow types configured looks like this:
![../../_images/complete-shadow-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/complete-shadow-graph.png)
All shadow types should now be visible in the scene.
![../../_images/car-spot-point-and-directional-shadows.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-spot-point-and-directional-shadows.png)
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-shadows.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html)
[Creating Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html)
[Creating Bloom Effect with Prism Graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html)

Kanzi applications use kzb Kanzi files as the source of application content and event logic.
You can use one or more Kanzi Studio projects to create your Kanzi application.
See [Combining Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/using-assets-from-another-project.html).
You can configure your project in Kanzi Studio by selecting Project > Properties.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png)
In Kanzi Studio you can have only one project open at a time.
## Kanzi Studio project structure[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/projects.html#ks-project-structure "Link to this heading")
Your Kanzi Studio project consists of project objects and resources. Each object in the project has a parent, a name, and a set of properties that define it. Additionally, most objects have either child or item objects.
In addition to the parent link and the child links in the children collection, items can also refer to other branches in the project tree. For example, animation objects have animation library as their parent but have a list of references to animation that act as their child nodes. This allows animation instancing where several animation nodes can share a single child node in their child node lists.
## Project directory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/projects.html#project-directory "Link to this heading")
By default, Kanzi Studio projects are stored in the `<KanziWorkspace>/Projects` directory. For every project Kanzi Studio creates a directory that contains:
  * **Project files**. Kanzi Studio stores the project data in kzm files. The root project file has the `.proj.kzm` extension. While you can manually modify the project files, they are designed to be modified only by Kanzi Studio.
  * **Project file backups**. When you save your project, Kanzi Studio makes a copy of the project file and stores it in a file with the `.proj.kzm_N` extension, where N is the consecutive number of the backup.
  * **Project file lock**. When you open a project, Kanzi Studio creates a lock file in the project directory. The project lock file prevents the opening of more than one copy of a project. Kanzi Studio deletes the project lock file when you close the project.
  * **Resource file directories**. These directories contain files that are part of a Kanzi Studio project but their contents are not included in the project file. For example, this includes image files and shader source files.
You can access most of the contents of the resource file directories in Kanzi Studio in Library > Resource Files. When you add a file to any of these directories in the file system, that file is automatically added to the Library, with the following exceptions:
    * Mesh Data and Animations directories are used only by Kanzi Studio. The files in these directories contain the vertex and index data of the meshes and animation keyframe data of the animations. If you are using source control system, remember to add these files to the source control whenever you import meshes or create new animations in your Kanzi Studio project.
    * Source Assets directory is a storage place for the native files where you can store image processing applications and digital content creation tools so that they remain with the project. Kanzi Studio does not handle these files and does not export them into the kzb file of your Kanzi application. You cannot access the Source Assets directory from the Kanzi Studio.
  * Restore Points directory. Use restore points to return to an earlier version of your project. When you create a restore point for a project, Kanzi Studio makes the complete copy of your project into a timestamped directory in the `<ProjectName>/Restore Points` directory. See [Creating restore points](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#creating-restore-points).

# Creating backups of your projects[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#creating-backups-of-your-projects "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

In Kanzi Studio you can create:
  * **Automatic backups**. Every time Kanzi Studio automatically saves your project it makes a copy of the project and stores it in a file with .autosave extension. Kanzi Studio stores only one copy of the .autosave file. See [Setting automatic backups](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#setting-automatic-backups) and [Restoring your project from an automatic backup](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#restorin).
  * **Manual backups**. Every time you save your project, Kanzi Studio makes a copy of the project and stores it in a file with extension _N, where N is the consecutive number of the backup. Kanzi Studio stores the ten latest project file backups. For example, if the name of your project is Orchard, project file is Orchard.proj.kzm, latest backup is Orchard.proj.kzm_1, second to latest backup is Orchard.proj.kzm_2, and so on. See [Restoring your project from a manual backup](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#restorin2).
  * Restore Points. Use restore points to return to an earlier version of your project. When you create a restore point for a project, Kanzi Studio makes the complete copy of your project into a timestamped directory in the `<ProjectName>/Restore Points` directory. See [Creating restore points](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#creating-restore-points) and [Restoring a project from a restore point](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#restorin3).


## Setting automatic backups[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#setting-automatic-backups "Link to this heading")
Every time Kanzi Studio automatically saves your project it makes a copy of the project and stores it in a file with .autosave extension. Kanzi Studio stores only one copy of the .autosave file.
By default Kanzi Studio automatically saves your project every 15 minutes. Kanzi Studio automatically saves your project only if you make a change in the project.
To set the automatic backups, select Edit > User Preferences and in the Autosave:
  * To take automatic backups into use, enable the Enabled setting.
  * To set the time between automatic backups, enter the number of minutes in the Interval text box.
![../../_images/user-preferences-autosave-interval.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/user-preferences-autosave-interval.png)


## Restoring your project from an automatic backup[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#restoring-your-project-from-an-automatic-backup "Link to this heading")
To restore your project from an automatic backup, select File > Open Backup Save and select Autosave to open the automatic backup.
![../../_images/open-autosave-backup.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-autosave-backup.png)
## Restoring your project from a manual backup[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#restoring-your-project-from-a-manual-backup "Link to this heading")
Every time you save your project, Kanzi Studio makes a copy of the project and stores it in a file with extension _N, where N is the consecutive number of the backup. Kanzi Studio stores the ten latest project file backups. For example, if the name of your project is Orchard, project file is Orchard.proj.kzm, latest backup is Orchard.proj.kzm_1, second to latest backup is Orchard.proj.kzm_2, and so on.
To restore your project from a manual backup, select File > Open Backup Save and select Backup and the version you want to open.
![../../_images/open-manual-save-backup.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-manual-save-backup.png)
## Creating restore points[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#creating-restore-points "Link to this heading")
Use restore points to return to an earlier version of your project. When you create a restore point for a project, Kanzi Studio makes the complete copy of your project into a timestamped directory in the `<ProjectName>/Restore Points` directory.
Making restore points for your project is useful so that you can return to the state of your project before you made, for example, a significant change to your project.
To create a restore point, while you have your project open in Kanzi Studio and before you make a significant change, select File > Save Restore Point.
Kanzi Studio makes the complete copy of your project into a timestamped directory in the `<ProjectName>/Tool_project/Restore Points` directory.
![../../_images/save-restore-point.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/save-restore-point.png)
## Restoring a project from a restore point[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#restoring-a-project-from-a-restore-point "Link to this heading")
To restore a project from a restore point:
  1. Go to the project directory of the project you want to restore and open the `Tool_project/Restore Points` directory.
  2. Open the timestamped directory from which you want to restore your project and open the Kanzi Studio project file. The project from the restore point you selected opens in a new instance of Kanzi Studio.


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Cleaning up your project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/cleaning-up-a-project.html)
[Configuring Kanzi Studio projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/configuring-projects.html)
[Projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/projects.html)
