# Creating a project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#creating-a-project "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
To create a project:
  1. In Kanzi Studio, either:
     * In the main menu, select File > New Project.
     * In the Quick Start window, click New.
The Quick Start window is available when you open Kanzi Studio or close a project. If the Quick Start window is not visible, to open it, in the main menu select File > Show Quick Start.
![../../_images/new-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/new-project.png)
  2. In the New tab of the Quick Start window:
     * Select an appropriate project template from the list of available options.
>      * To create an application using the Kanzi Engine C++ API, see [C++](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#c).
>      * To create an application for Android using the Kanzi Engine Java API, see [Android (Java, Kotlin)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#android-java-kotlin).
>      * To create only a Kanzi Studio project, see [Kanzi Studio project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#ks-project).
     * Set Project Name to the name that you want to use for the project.
     * Set Location to the directory where you want to create the project.
If you do not want to create a directory for the project, deselect Create folder.
     * Materials to the materials that you want to import to your project. See [Material types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#material-types).
Click Create.
![../../_images/kanzi-engine-plugin-new-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/kanzi-engine-plugin-new-project.png)


Kanzi Studio creates a project. You can see the structure of the project in the Kanzi Studio Node Tree and in the directory that you set in Location.
![../../_images/new-project-in-project-window.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/new-project-in-project-window.png)
After you create a project, you can import 2D and 3D content that you created outside of Kanzi Studio and start building your Kanzi application. See [Tutorials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/tutorials.html).
You can configure your project in Kanzi Studio. See [Configuring Kanzi Studio projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/configuring-projects.html).
## Application types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#application-types "Link to this heading")
### C++[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#c "Link to this heading")
To create application logic using the Kanzi Engine C++ API, in the New tab of the Quick Start window, select an appropriate project template from the list to one of these templates:
  * Application template creates a Kanzi Studio project with a Kanzi Engine application.
Use this template to create a Kanzi application for which you can create application logic using the Kanzi Engine C++ API. See [Tutorial: Hello world!](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/hello-world/hello-world.html)
  * Application with Kanzi Engine plugin template creates a Kanzi Studio project with a Kanzi Engine application that contains a Kanzi Engine plugin.
Use Kanzi Engine plugins to extend the functionality of Kanzi for your application. See [Extending the functionality of Kanzi Engine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/configuring-custom-components-for-kanzi-studio.html).
  * Application with data source plugin template creates a project with a Kanzi Engine application that contains a data source plugin template.
Use Kanzi Engine data source plugins to define data sources for your Kanzi application. See [Tutorial: Get application data from a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-sources/data-sources.html) and [Defining a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/defining-a-data-source.html).

![../../_images/kanzi-engine-plugin-new-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/kanzi-engine-plugin-new-project.png)
Kanzi Studio creates a project where:
  * `Application` directory contains the structure and template source code for the application and plugin of your project.
  * `Tool_project` directory contains the Kanzi Studio project.


See [Application development](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html).
### Android (Java, Kotlin)[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#android-java-kotlin "Link to this heading")
To create an application for Android with the Kanzi Engine Java API, in the New tab of the Quick Start window:
  * Select one of these project templates:
    * Android application template creates a Kanzi Studio project with a Kanzi Android framework-based application.
See [Tutorial: Getting started with Kanzi Android framework (droidfw)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/android-getting-started/android-getting-started.html)
    * Android application with Java plugin template creates a Kanzi Studio project with a Kanzi Android framework-based application that contains a Kanzi Engine Java plugin.
Use Kanzi Engine Java plugins to split your reusable application logic.
See [Tutorial: Data sources for Android](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/android-data-source/android-data-source.html), [Creating a Java Kanzi Engine plugin using a template](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-kanzi-engine-plugins.html#creating-a-java-kr-plugin-using-a-template), and [Extending the functionality of Kanzi Engine with Java](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/configuring-custom-java-components-for-kanzi.html).
  * Android Package Name to the name of the Android package for the project.

![../../_images/new-project-android-application.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/new-project-android-application.png)
Kanzi Studio creates a project where:
  * `Application` directory contains the structure and template source code for the application and possible plugin of your project.
  * `Application/configs/platforms/Android_gradle` directory contains the source code of the Android application project.
  * `Tool_project` directory contains the Kanzi Studio project.


See [Application development](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html) and [Developing with the Kanzi Android framework (droidfw)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/android/droidfw/android-droidfw.html).
### Kanzi Studio project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#ks-project "Link to this heading")
You can create a Kanzi Studio project without a Kanzi Engine application. For example, you can combine multiple Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi Studio solution. See [Combining Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/using-assets-from-another-project.html).
To create only a Kanzi Studio project, in the New tab of the Quick Start window, select Kanzi Studio project project template.
![../../_images/new-project-kanzi-studio-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/new-project-kanzi-studio-project.png)
You can deploy a Kanzi Studio-only project to Windows. See [Building and deploying Kanzi applications to Windows from Kanzi Studio](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/deploying-applications/deploying-kanzi-applications-for-windows.html#building-and-deploying-kanzi-applications-to-windows-from-kanzi-studio).
## Material types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#material-types "Link to this heading")
When you create a Kanzi Studio project, you can select the materials that you want to include in your project.
In the New tab of the Quick Start window, set Materials:
  * To start with a template that does not contain any predefined material types, select Import material types manually. You can add material types from the Kanzi Studio material library to the project when you need them, or create your own material types. See [Adding a material type to your project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-material-types.html#adding-a-material-type-to-your-project).
  * High performance vertex shaders template is intended for low precision and high performance applications. It contains vertex-based shaders. Most of the GPU specific computation, including applying lights using the Phong reflection model, is done in the vertex shader. This is a good starting point for most devices.
  * High quality fragment shaders template is intended for high-precision applications. It contains pixel-shader based materials. Most of the GPU specific computation, including applying lights using the Phong reflection model, is done in the fragment shader. This offers better image quality often at the cost of performance.
  * Physically based rendering template is intended for modern applications. It contains materials based on shaders that implement physically-based rendering (PBR) principles. The properties of these materials represent physical properties, such as metalness, and are therefore intuitive to control. Most of the GPU specific computation, including applying lights using a physically-based lighting model, is done in the fragment shader. This offers a more realistic rendering result in many lighting conditions.


High performance vertex shaders, High quality fragment shaders, and Physically based rendering project templates define a set of material types that are available in the project materials library, each with fragment and vertex shaders. See [Shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/shaders.html).
If you are not sure which set of materials to choose, select Import material types manually, and add the materials as you need them.
![../../_images/kanzi-engine-plugin-new-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/kanzi-engine-plugin-new-project.png)
## Developing the application logic in Visual Studio[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#developing-the-application-logic-in-visual-studio "Link to this heading")
When you create a project using the Application, Application with data source plugin, or Application with Kanzi Engine plugin template, Kanzi creates in the `Application` directory the structure and template source code for the application of your project. To use Visual Studio to develop the application logic, you must generate a Visual Studio solution with CMake.
To develop the application logic in Visual Studio:
  1. In Kanzi Studio, create a project using one of these templates:
     * Application
     * Application with data source plugin
     * Application with Kanzi Engine plugin
Kanzi creates a Kanzi Studio project in the `<ProjectName>/Tool_project` directory and the structure for the application code of your project in the `<ProjectName>/Application` directory:
     * `bin` directory contains the kzb and configuration files of your project.
     * `configs` directory contains the configuration files for different platforms. By default, Kanzi creates configuration files for several different platforms. The recommended platform for developing Kanzi applications is Microsoft Visual Studio. See [Deploying Kanzi applications](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/deploying-applications/deploying-kanzi-applications.html).
     * `src` directory contains the source code for your application.
     * `CMakeLists.txt` file contains the instructions for CMake to generate the Visual Studio solution for the Kanzi application.
     * `generate_cmake_vs<Version>_solution.bat` is a script that you can use to generate a Visual Studio solution for the Kanzi application. The script generates the Visual Studio solution in the `<ProjectName>/Application/build_vs<Version>` directory.
See [Creating a project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#creating-a-project).
  2. In Kanzi Studio, select File > Open Kanzi Command Prompt.
The Kanzi Command Prompt opens the Windows Command Prompt with the Kanzi environment variables set for the version of Kanzi for which you open a Kanzi Command Prompt.
Use the Kanzi Command Prompt to access Kanzi utilities and build tools, such as Gradle and CMake, without using absolute paths or setting environment variables.
![../../_images/open-kanzi-command-prompt.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-kanzi-command-prompt.png)
Tip
You can find the Kanzi Command Prompt in the Windows Start Menu in the Rightware directory.
When you have more than one version of Kanzi installed, make sure that you launch a Kanzi Command Prompt for the version of Kanzi with which you want to work in that command prompt.
  3. In the Kanzi Command Prompt in the `<ProjectName>/Application` directory, run the script that generates a Visual Studio solution for the application.

```
generate_cmake_vs2022_solution.bat

```
Copy to clipboard
This script generates a Visual Studio solution for the application in the directory `<ProjectName>/Application/build_vs2022`.
  4. In Visual Studio, open the `<ProjectName>/Application/build_vs<Version>/<ProjectName>.sln` Visual Studio solution.
For example, if you used the Application with data source plugin or Application with Kanzi Engine plugin template, the Visual Studio solution contains:
     * The project for the Kanzi Engine plugin named `<ProjectName>`. Define your Kanzi Engine plugin in this project.
     * The project for the C++ application named <ProjectName>_executable. Define the logic of your Kanzi application in this project.
![../../_images/mykanziengineplugin-project-contents.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mykanziengineplugin-project-contents.png)
  5. In Visual Studio, create the logic for your Kanzi application and your Kanzi Engine plugin, and configure the custom components in your Kanzi Engine plugin for Kanzi Studio. See [Application development](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html), [Creating Kanzi Engine plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-kanzi-engine-plugins.html), [Defining a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/defining-a-data-source.html), and [Extending the functionality of Kanzi Engine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/configuring-custom-components-for-kanzi-studio.html).
When you add or remove files that your Kanzi application or Kanzi Engine plugin use, update in the `CMakeLists.txt` the list of files in the `set` command and run the `generate_cmake_vs<Version>_solution.bat` script:
     * When you change the files that you use in your Kanzi application, update `<ProjectName>/Application/src/executable/CMakeLists.txt`
     * When you change the files that you use in your Kanzi Engine plugin, update `<ProjectName>/Application/src/plugin/CMakeLists.txt`
For example, to add the `tinyxml2.cpp` and `tinyxml2.h` files to your Kanzi Engine plugin, update `<ProjectName>/Application/src/plugin/CMakeLists.txt` to include these files

```
set(sources_plugin
    src/tinyxml2.cpp
    src/tinyxml2.h
    src/mykanziengineplugin.cpp
    src/mykanziengineplugin.hpp
    src/mykanziengineplugin.rc
    src/mykanziengineplugin_module.cpp
    src/mykanziengineplugin_module.hpp)

```
Copy to clipboard
  6. Select the solution configuration that you want to use.
During development select the Debug configuration. When you are ready to create a version for production, select the Release configuration.
![../../_images/debug-configuration.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/debug-configuration.png)
  7. Build your application:
     * To build only the Kanzi Engine plugin DLL, right-click the `<ProjectName>` project and select Build.
![../../_images/mykanziengineplugin-vs-build.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mykanziengineplugin-vs-build.png)
     * To build the Kanzi Engine plugin DLL and your Kanzi application, right-click the <ProjectName>_executable project and select Build.
![../../_images/mykanziengineplugin_executable-vs-build.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mykanziengineplugin_executable-vs-build.png)
Visual Studio builds:
     * Plugin DLL in the `<ProjectName>/Application/lib/<PlatformName>/<ConfigurationName>` and the `<ProjectName>/Application/build_vs<Version>/runtime/<ConfigurationName>` directories
Kanzi Studio uses the plugin DLL in the `<ProjectName>/Application/lib` directory.
     * Application executable in the `<ProjectName>/Application/build_vs<Version>/runtime/<ConfigurationName>` directory.
  8. Run your application:
    1. In Kanzi Studio, select File > Export > Export KZB.
Kanzi Studio exports the project kzb and configuration files to the `<ProjectName>/Application/bin` directory.
![../../_images/export-kzb-binary.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-kzb-binary.png)
    2. Place these files to the same directory:
       * From the `<ProjectName>/Application/build_vs<Version>/runtime/<ConfigurationName>` the exe and DLL files.
       * From the `<ProjectName>/Application/bin` directory copy the kzb and cfg files.
       * From the `<KanziWorkspace>/Engine/lib/<PlatformName>/<ConfigurationName>` copy all DLL files.
For example, place these files to the `<ProjectName>/Application/bin` directory.
    3. Run your application by executing the exe file that Visual Studio built.


Tip
To build and run your application from Visual Studio:
  1. In Kanzi Studio, export the kzb file.
![../../_images/export-kzb-binary.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-kzb-binary.png)
  2. In Visual Studio, right-click the <ProjectName>_executable and select Set as StartUp Project.
![../../_images/visual-studio-set-as-startup-project-plugin.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/visual-studio-set-as-startup-project-plugin.png)
  3. Select the solution configuration that you want to use and run the application.
![../../_images/visual-studio-run-application.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/visual-studio-run-application.png)


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Configuring Kanzi Studio projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/configuring-projects.html)
[Application development](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html)
[Developing with the Kanzi Android framework (droidfw)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/android/droidfw/android-droidfw.html)
[Creating Kanzi Engine plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-kanzi-engine-plugins.html)
[Combining Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/using-assets-from-another-project.html)

# Configuring Kanzi Studio projects[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/configuring-projects.html#configuring-ks-projects "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
To configure a Kanzi Studio project:
  1. Open the project and in the main menu select Project > Properties.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png)
  2. In the Properties set the properties in these property categories to configure your project:
     * Description to document the project. See [Documenting a project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/documenting-a-project.html).
     * Application Settings to set the directories to which Kanzi Studio exports the kzb file and kzb Player version of the project. See [Using kzb files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/kzb-binaries/using-kzb-binaries.html).
     * Binary Export to configure the contents of the kzb file. For example, use these properties to:
       * Optimize the export of meshes and images. See [Images and textures best practices](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/images-and-textures-best-practices.html) and [Optimizing meshes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/editing-meshes.html).
       * Set how Kanzi loads kzb files. See [Setting how Kanzi loads a kzb file](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/configuring-projects.html#setting-how-kanzi-loads-kzb-file).
       * Set the color workflow. See [Color workflow](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html).
     * Building to set the application configuration that Kanzi Studio uses to build the project. See [Configuring Android builds](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/deploying-applications/deploying-kanzi-applications-for-android.html#configuring-android-builds).
     * Default Assets to set which assets you want to use when you create nodes and resources. See [Setting the default assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/configuring-projects.html#setting-the-default-assets).
     * Preview to configure the Preview to work with Kanzi Engine plugins. See [Creating Kanzi Engine plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-kanzi-engine-plugins.html).
     * Profile to set:
       * The name of the kzb file and project descriptions file. See [Using kzb files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/kzb-binaries/using-kzb-binaries.html) and [Documenting a project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/documenting-a-project.html).
       * The graphics API. See [Using OpenGL ES 3.0+ in Kanzi](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-opengl-es-30.html).
       * The font engine for the Kanzi Studio Preview. See [Setting the font engine for the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#setting-font-engine-for-preview) and [FontEngine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#fontengine).
       * A project to be an asset package. See [Creating an asset package](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-packages/asset-packages.html#creating-an-asset-package).
     * Resources to set how Kanzi and Kanzi Studio handle resources. See [Setting how Kanzi Engine handles unused resources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/unused-resources.html).
     * Timeline to set the start and end times of the global timeline of the project.
To view the timeline, select Window > Toolbar > Timeline.
![../../_images/project-properties-in-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties-in-properties.png)


## Setting the default assets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/configuring-projects.html#setting-the-default-assets "Link to this heading")
You can set which assets you want to use when you create new nodes and resources.
To set the default assets:
  1. Open the project and in the main menu select Project > Properties.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png)
  2. In the Properties in the Default Assets category set which assets you want to use by default:
     * Default Material sets the material that Kanzi Studio sets to models you create and import that do not have a material.
     * Default Texture sets the single texture that Kanzi Studio sets to all new Image nodes and materials that use textures.
     * Default Cubemap Texture sets the cubemap texture that Kanzi Studio sets to all new materials that use cubemap textures.
     * Import Material Type sets the material type to which Kanzi Studio assigns the materials that you import with 3D asset files.
![../../_images/default-assets.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/default-assets.png)


## Setting how Kanzi loads a kzb file[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/configuring-projects.html#setting-how-k-loads-a-kzb-file "Link to this heading")
The presence of the Screen node in a kzb file determines how Kanzi loads a kzb file.
To set whether Kanzi Studio exports the Screen node to the kzb file of that project, in the Node Tree select the Screen node and in the Properties set the Disable KZB Export property to:
  * Disabled to export the kzb file with the Screen node. This is the default setting. You can start your Kanzi application with a kzb file that has a Screen node. If you load during application runtime a kzb file that contains a Screen node, you replace the Screen node that the application uses.
  * Enabled to export the kzb file without the Screen node. You can load a kzb file without a Screen node only during application runtime, when your Kanzi application already has a Screen node.

![../../_images/export-project-settings-to-kzb.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-project-settings-to-kzb.png)
## Project property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/configuring-projects.html#project-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for a Kanzi Studio project, see [Project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/project-reference.html).

# Migrating projects from Kanzi 3.9 to Kanzi 4[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrating-projects-from-k-3-9-to-k-4 "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
The project and plugin templates changed substantially between Kanzi 3.9 and Kanzi 4. Kanzi 4 Kanzi Studio can open and convert a Kanzi 3.9 Kanzi Studio project, but the surrounding build structure (CMake files, build scripts, platform configurations, plugin build setup) and the default materials and shaders do not migrate automatically. This guide explains how to move a Kanzi 3.9 application or plugin onto the Kanzi 4 template structure.
This guide covers the **project and build structure**. For the source-code and API changes you must also apply, see the [Kanzi 4.0.0 migration guide](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/release-notes/kanzi-4.0/kanzi-4.0.0-migration-guide.html) and the [Kanzi 4.1.0 migration guide](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/release-notes/kanzi-4.0/kanzi-4.1.0-migration-guide.html).
## Before you start[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#before-you-start "Link to this heading")
**Back up your 3.9 project, or keep it in version control.** Converting a Kanzi 3.9 project to Kanzi 4 is **in-place and irreversible** : when you open a 3.9 `<ProjectName>.kzproj` in Kanzi 4 Kanzi Studio and save, Kanzi Studio rewrites the entire project — including every resource file — to the Kanzi 4 `<ProjectName>.proj.kzm` format, and cannot convert it back. Always migrate a copy and keep the original 3.9 project intact.
## Read this first: removed functionality[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#read-this-first-removed-functionality "Link to this heading")
Kanzi 4 removes some functionality that Kanzi 3.9 projects can depend on. If your project depends on any of the following, plan a different upgrade strategy before you start, because this guide does not restore them:  
| Removed in Kanzi 4  | Notes  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Visual Studio 2017 and 2019 solution generators  | The `generate_cmake_vs2017_solution.bat` and `generate_cmake_vs2019_solution.bat` scripts are gone. Kanzi 4 supports Visual Studio 2022 only, through `generate_cmake_vs2022_solution.bat`.  |  
| The Linux `linux_x11_glx_cpp98` platform  | The pre-C++11 Linux platform and its `SConstruct` file are removed. Kanzi 4 requires a C++17 toolchain.  |  
| SCons build helpers  | The `configs/platforms/common/config.py` and `start_build.py` scripts are removed. All platforms build with CMake.  |  
Kanzi 4 also raises the minimum required CMake version from 3.10 to 3.25.
## Choosing your path[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#choosing-your-path "Link to this heading")
For most projects, **migrate your project** : open and convert it in Kanzi 4 Kanzi Studio, then transplant the Kanzi 4 build structure and default resources. See [Migrate your project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrate-your-project).
If your project is small or a throwaway prototype, **start fresh** : create a new Kanzi 4 project and bring your content into it. See [Start fresh and rebuild](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#start-fresh-and-rebuild).
When starting fresh you must rebuild the application structure by hand — node-tree hierarchy, prefab placement, cross-prefab bindings, and render/composition setup — on top of migrating your resources.
## What changes between Kanzi 3.9 and Kanzi 4[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#what-changes-between-k-3-9-and-k-4 "Link to this heading")
Whichever path you take, these change between Kanzi 3.9 and Kanzi 4:
  * **Project file format.** The 3.9 root project file is `<ProjectName>.kzproj`; the Kanzi 4 file is `<ProjectName>.proj.kzm`. Kanzi 4 Kanzi Studio converts the older project when you open it (it asks you to confirm), then writes the new format when you save. The conversion is irreversible (see [Before you start](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#before-you-start)).
  * **Build system.** Kanzi 4 adds command-line build wrappers (`build.bat` / `build.sh`) and a resolver concept: the `cmake/kanzi-bootstrap.cmake` dispatcher selects between the classic `cmake` resolver (a local Kanzi SDK, the default, closest to Kanzi 3.9) and the `kpm` resolver (Kanzi Package Manager) through the `KANZI_RESOLVER` CMake cache variable.  
| Command  | What it does  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `build.bat`  | Builds with the `cmake` resolver in the Release configuration.  |  
| `build.bat <config>`  | Builds with the `cmake` resolver in a specific configuration (`Debug`, `Release`, `Profiling`).  |  
| `build.bat kpm`  | Builds with the `kpm` resolver.  |  
Replace `build.bat` with `./build.sh` on Linux and macOS. The classic resolver locates a local SDK with the `KANZI_HOME` environment variable, exactly as in Kanzi 3.9. If you passed `-DKANZI_ROOT=<path>` on the command line, rename it to `-DKanzi_ROOT=<path>`.
`generate_cmake_vs2022_solution.bat` generates the Visual Studio 2022 solution; on macOS, `generate_cmake_xcode_ios_project.sh` generates an Xcode project for iOS (a new Kanzi 4 platform).
  * **Plugin.** Rebuild your Kanzi Engine plugin with Visual Studio 2022 against the Kanzi 4 SDK and re-import it. See [Migrating a Kanzi Engine plugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrating-a-kanzi-engine-plugin).
  * **Default materials and shaders.** Kanzi 4 reworked the graphics system and updated the default material types and shaders to new GLSL. A converted 3.9 project keeps its old shaders, which Kanzi 4 rejects. See [Migrating materials and shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrating-materials-and-shaders).
  * **Exported binaries.** You re-export the `.kzb` in Kanzi 4. Do not reuse a Kanzi 3.9 `.kzb`.


## Migrate your project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrate-your-project "Link to this heading")
  1. **Convert a copy of your 3.9 project.** In Kanzi 4 Kanzi Studio, select File > Open Project, open the copy’s `<ProjectName>.kzproj`, confirm the conversion prompt, and save. Kanzi Studio writes the Kanzi 4 `<ProjectName>.proj.kzm`.
  2. **Create a donor project to copy from.** In Kanzi 4 Kanzi Studio, create a new project from the template that matches your project (for example **Application with Kanzi Engine plugin**), with materials that match your project (for example **High-performance vertex shaders**). See [Creating a project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html). Use the same project name to avoid renaming files later. This project is the donor: the source of the Kanzi 4 build files and default resources you copy in the next steps.
  3. **Swap in the build scaffolding:**
    1. Overwrite the donor’s `.cpp` and `.hpp` files under `Application/src` with ones from the converted project.
    2. Delete the converted project’s `Application` folder.
    3. Copy the donor’s `Application` into the converted project.
  4. **Rebuild and import your plugin.** Follow [Migrating a Kanzi Engine plugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrating-a-kanzi-engine-plugin).
  5. **Replace the default materials and shaders.** Keep your custom materials, but delete the converted project’s default Materials, Material Types, and Shaders. Replace them with the ones in the donor project.
  6. **Finish.** Fix any custom material or shader that fails to build (see [Migrating materials and shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrating-materials-and-shaders)), apply the C++ API changes (see the 4.0.0 and 4.1.0 migration guides), then build and re-export the `.kzb`.


## Start fresh and rebuild[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#start-fresh-and-rebuild "Link to this heading")
  1. **Create a new project** from the template that matches your project (for example **Application with Kanzi Engine plugin**), with materials that match your project (for example **High-performance vertex shaders**). See [Creating a project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html). This project has Kanzi 4’s build files and default resources.
  2. **Bring in and import your plugin.** Copy your plugin source files (`.cpp` and `.hpp`) into the new project’s `src/plugin/src` directory, then follow [Migrating a Kanzi Engine plugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrating-a-kanzi-engine-plugin).
  3. **Bring your authored content** into the `Tool_project` of the new project: your scenes and prefabs, imported assets (3D assets and their mesh data, images, fonts), and any materials and shaders you created. **Keep the new project’s default Materials, Material Types, and Shaders** — do not copy the 3.9 defaults over them. See [Sharing project items](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/sharing-project-items.html) and [Combining Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/using-assets-from-another-project.html).
Note
When you import a 3D asset, Kanzi Studio populates the 3D Assets and the mesh-data directories. If the mesh data does not come across, the mesh does not rebuild.
  4. **Rebuild your node tree.** Reassemble your application’s hierarchy under Screen from your imported prefabs and content.
  5. **Finish.** Fix any custom material or shader that fails to build (see [Migrating materials and shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrating-materials-and-shaders)), apply the C++ API changes (see the 4.0.0 and 4.1.0 migration guides), then build and re-export the `.kzb`.


## Migrating a Kanzi Engine plugin[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrating-a-kanzi-engine-plugin "Link to this heading")
  1. **List your source files.** Ensure all source files are listed in the `set` command of the matching `CMakeLists.txt` (`src/plugin` or `src/executable`).
  2. Build the plugin with Visual Studio 2022 against the Kanzi 4 SDK: set `KANZI_HOME` to your Kanzi 4 SDK, then run `build.bat` or `generate_cmake_vs2022_solution.bat`. If you previously built against a different SDK, delete the build directory first.
  3. Register the rebuilt plugin in Library > Kanzi Engine Plugins: delete the existing plugin entry, then right-click Kanzi Engine Plugins > Import Kanzi Engine Plugin and select the rebuilt DLL.
  4. Set the Preview Build Configuration (in Project > Properties) to the configuration you built the plugin for.


Port your plugin manually if your plugin uses Kanzi Engine APIs that changed in Kanzi 4 — primarily rendering, graphics, and platform. See: [Kanzi 4.0.0 migration guide](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/release-notes/kanzi-4.0/kanzi-4.0.0-migration-guide.html) and [Kanzi 4.1.0 migration guide](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/release-notes/kanzi-4.0/kanzi-4.1.0-migration-guide.html).
## Migrating materials and shaders[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrating-materials-and-shaders "Link to this heading")
Kanzi 4 reworked the graphics system and updated the default material types and shaders to new GLSL. A converted Kanzi 3.9 project still carries its old default materials and shaders, which use legacy GLSL that Kanzi 4 rejects, so you replace them with Kanzi 4’s.
  * **Use the new default materials and shaders, never the 3.9 ones.**
  * **Migrate shaders you wrote yourself** to Kanzi 4 GLSL. See the shader-migration steps in the [Kanzi 4.1.0 migration guide](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/release-notes/kanzi-4.0/kanzi-4.1.0-migration-guide.html) and [Setting the OpenGL ES version](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/editing-shaders.html#setting-the-opengl-es-version).
  * **Fix any custom material or shader that fails to build.** Migrate its shader to Kanzi 4 GLSL as above, or re-create the material on a Kanzi 4 default material type. Because materials are shared, you fix this per material, not per node.


## Troubleshooting[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#troubleshooting "Link to this heading")
  * **Materials fail to acquire, or shader compilation errors such as** `ES shaders for SPIR-V require version 310 or higher`. You are still using 3.9 default shaders. Replace them with Kanzi 4’s (or migrate the GLSL).
  * **Preview reports an undefined metaclass, or the plugin does not load.** The plugin DLL’s build configuration does not match the Preview Build Configuration, or `KANZI_HOME` pointed at the wrong SDK when you built it. Rebuild against the correct SDK and re-import, and align the Preview Build Configuration.
  * **Font-engine warnings, an empty Font Engine list (only “None”), or “Preview cannot start” / “cannot find a font engine”.** These are downstream symptoms of the engine not initializing — usually because the materials and shaders fail to build, or the Preview Build Configuration does not match your rebuilt plugin. Fix those first. Once the engine initializes, the warnings clear and the Font Engine list populates with the available engines (FreeType, iType) on its own; you do not select a font engine manually to resolve this.


## Per-template notes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#per-template-notes "Link to this heading")
### Basic application[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#basic-application "Link to this heading")
The single source file (for example, `src/basic_application.cpp`) carries over. There is no plugin subtree.
### Kanzi Engine plugin and data source plugin[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#kr-plugin-and-data-source-plugin "Link to this heading")
The plugin subtree under `src/plugin` is self-contained in Kanzi 4: it has its own `cmake/` directory and `packages.json`. Plugin deployment uses the `create_and_deploy_plugin` scripts in the `Application` directory. Follow [Migrating a Kanzi Engine plugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#migrating-a-kanzi-engine-plugin).
### Android changes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#android-changes "Link to this heading")
Kanzi 4 uses Android Gradle Plugin 8 and moves dependency versions to `configs/platforms/android_gradle/gradle/libs.versions.toml`. The native build now lives in a `kanzinative` Gradle module, and the per-plugin Gradle module that Kanzi 3.9 generated for plugin templates is removed. Kanzi 4 also requires NDK 28.2.13676358 and CMake 3.25 or newer; set the Gradle CMake version to 3.30.5, the lowest version the Android SDK provides. Re-apply your Kanzi 3.9 Gradle customizations against this layout rather than copying your old Gradle files. See the [Kanzi 4.1.0 migration guide](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/release-notes/kanzi-4.0/kanzi-4.1.0-migration-guide.html).
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/migrating-projects-from-kanzi-3-9-to-kanzi-4.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Kanzi 4.0.0 migration guide](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/release-notes/kanzi-4.0/kanzi-4.0.0-migration-guide.html)
[Kanzi 4.1.0 migration guide](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/release-notes/kanzi-4.0/kanzi-4.1.0-migration-guide.html)
[Creating a project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/creating-a-new-project.html)

# Property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/property-types.html#property-types "Link to this heading")

Properties provide the means to specify and examine the state, appearance, and behavior of nodes. For example, a property can define a color, indicate whether a button is pressed, or specify the alignment of an item.
Properties provide a uniform way to access data of Kanzi nodes, so that many Kanzi subsystems can manipulate the data. That way you can, for example, animate property values, provide bindings between property values, and monitor property value changes.
Each property in Kanzi is described by a property type. The property type describes the name and category of the property and type of data and values the property can have.
You can create custom property types to support the logic of your Kanzi application:
  * In Kanzi Studio. See [Creating property types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/creating-custom-property-types.html).
  * In a Kanzi Engine plugin. See [Kanzi Engine plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/plugins-kanzi-engine.html).


To learn how to work with properties in Kanzi Studio, see [Using properties in Kanzi Studio](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/using-properties.html).
To learn about how the Kanzi property system works, see [Property system](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/kanzi-fundamentals/property-system.html).
For a list of default property types, see [Property types reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/property-types-reference.html).

# Using properties in Kanzi Studio[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/using-properties.html#using-properties-in-ks "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Properties define the characteristics of content in your Kanzi application. You can add, remove, and modify properties in the Properties window.
You can find the Properties window on the right side of the Node Tree window.
![../../_images/properties-window.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-window.png)
Tip
In the Kanzi Studio Node Tree window, an indicator next to a node shows when a State Manager, Binding, Data Source Binding, or an Animation overrides the values of some properties in that node.
![../../_images/node-override-notice.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-override-notice.png)
To navigate to the source of the override in the Kanzi Studio project, right-click the override indicator and select the source you wish to navigate to from the context menu.
## Adding a property[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/using-properties.html#adding-a-property "Link to this heading")
To add a property, in the Node Tree, Prefabs, or Library, select the item to which you want to add a property, and either:
  * In the Properties, click ![add-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-property.png) next to the property that you want to add to the currently selected node or resource.
With the ![add-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-property.png) button, you can add only the most frequent properties for the selected node or resource type.
  * In the Properties, right-click, select Add Property, and select the property that you want to add.
![../../_images/properties-right-click-to-add.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-right-click-to-add.png)
  * In the bottom-right corner of the Properties, click ![add-properties-window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png), in the search field enter the name of a property, and double-click the property that you want to add.
![../../_images/add-properties-window.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-properties-window.gif)


## Removing a property[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/using-properties.html#removing-a-property "Link to this heading")
Remove the properties that your content does not use.
To remove a property, in the Properties, right-click a property and select Remove.
![../../_images/properties-remove-property.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-remove-property.gif)
## Editing resource properties from a node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/using-properties.html#editing-resource-properties-from-a-node "Link to this heading")
When a property points to a resource, you can quickly edit the properties of that resource from the item that uses that resource.
In the Properties, click ![access](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) next to a property to access and edit the resource to which the property points without moving away from the currently selected node.
![../../_images/properties-quick-edit.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-quick-edit.png)
## Using a Properties window for a specific item[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/using-properties.html#using-a-properties-window-for-a-specific-item "Link to this heading")
When you want the Properties window to show the properties of a specific node or resource, in the Node Tree, Prefabs, or Library:
  * Select any item and in the bottom panel of the Properties window, click ![lock-properties-window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-lock.png).
This way you lock the main Properties window so that it always shows the properties of the node that was selected when you locked the window.
To unlock the window, click ![lock-properties-window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-lock.png) again.
  * Right-click any item and select Open New Properties Window.
The Properties window that opens always shows only the properties of the item from which you opened the window.
![../../_images/open-new-properties-window.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-new-properties-window.png)

# Rendering[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#rendering "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use render passes to define the rendering of 3D content in your Kanzi application.
For example, in render passes you can define:
  * Which Camera that render pass and its descendants use for rendering. See [Setting the camera for render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html#setting-the-camera-for-render-passes).
  * What nodes the render pass renders. See [Collecting nodes for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/filtering-node-lists.html).
  * What lights to use to light the content. See [Using lights in rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/lights-rendering.html).
  * What material to use to render the content. [Setting materials for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-materials.html).
  * The format of the composition target. See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html).
  * Post-processing effects. [Creating a post-processing effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/post-processing-grayscale.html).


In a render pass prefab, you can create a hierarchy of render passes to achieve a specific rendering result.
In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs each top-level render pass is the root of a render pass prefab.
Kanzi executes the render passes in each render pass prefab from top to bottom the way they appear in the render pass prefab in the Library. Each render pass applies its settings and renders its children. See [Using render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html).
For example, the Default render pass, which is one of the render pass presets that come with Kanzi Studio, creates a basic set of render passes that first render opaque nodes and then transparent nodes. See [Using the Default render pass](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html#using-drp).
![../../_images/rendering.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rendering.svg)
## Render passes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#render-passes "Link to this heading")
These render passes are available in Kanzi:
###  Blit render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#blit-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Blit render pass blits one or more single textures or cubemap textures on the screen using a specific material.
See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html), [Rendering multiple render passes or textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-multiple.html), and [Creating a post-processing effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/post-processing-grayscale.html).
![../../_images/blit-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blit-render-pass.svg)
###  Clear render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#clear-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Clear render pass clears some or all of the buffers of the current render context.
You can set the values to which Kanzi clears the color, depth, and stencil buffer.
![../../_images/clear-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clear-render-pass.svg)
###  Composition Target render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#composition-target-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Composition Target render pass renders itself and its descendant render passes to one or more composition targets.
See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html).
![../../_images/composition-target-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/composition-target-render-pass.svg)
###  Cubemap render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#cubemap-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Cubemap render pass renders itself and its child render passes to an active composition target, such as a Cubemap Render Target Texture and the Result Texture of the Cubemap render pass.
See [Creating cubemap reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/cubemap-render-pass.html).
![../../_images/cubemap-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cubemap-render-pass.svg)![../../_images/preview-cubemap-reflections.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-cubemap-reflections.gif)
###  Draw Objects render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#draw-objects-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Draw Objects render pass allows you to set a Camera node to render a specific list of nodes using specific light nodes.
The Draw Objects render pass:
  * By default uses the default Camera node to render all nodes in a Scene node, or the nodes passed to it by its nearest ancestor Node List render pass. See [Setting the camera for render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html#setting-the-camera-for-render-passes) and [Collecting nodes for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/filtering-node-lists.html).
  * By default renders nodes using the light nodes provided by its nearest ancestor Gather Lights render pass. See [Using lights in rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/lights-rendering.html).
  * Uses the rendering parameters that you set in its nearest ancestor Pipeline State render pass.
  * Allows you to control frustum culling. See [Controlling frustum culling](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/meshes/setting-culling.html#controlling-frustum-culling).

![../../_images/draw-objects-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-objects-render-pass.svg)![../../_images/draw-objects-render-pass-example.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-objects-render-pass-example.svg)
###  Draw Objects With Material render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#draw-objects-with-material-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Draw Objects With Material render pass works like a Draw Objects render pass but allows you to set a material that it uses to render content. See [Setting materials for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-materials.html).
![../../_images/draw-objects-with-material-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-objects-with-material-render-pass.svg)![../../_images/draw-objects-with-material-render-example.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-objects-with-material-render-example.svg)
###  Gather Lights render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#gather-lights-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Gather Lights render pass allows you to collect from a list of nodes the light nodes for lighting 3D nodes in a scene.
See [Using lights in rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/lights-rendering.html).
![../../_images/gather-lights-render-pass1.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/gather-lights-render-pass1.svg)
###  Group render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#group-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Group render pass allows you to collect render passes so that you can refer to a single render pass prefab in your Viewport 2D node.
If your topmost render pass can have all your other render passes as its children, you do not need a Group render pass.
![../../_images/group-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/group-render-pass.svg)
###  Material Setup render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#material-setup-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Material Setup render pass allows you to set properties for a material so that all successive rendering with that material uses the property values that you set in this render pass.
See [Setting materials for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-materials.html).
![../../_images/material-setup-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-setup-render-pass.svg)![../../_images/preview-infinity-mirror-completed.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-infinity-mirror-completed.png)
###  Node List render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#node-list-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Node List render pass allows you to filter and hold a list of nodes that you want to render using other render passes.
See [Collecting nodes for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/filtering-node-lists.html).
![../../_images/node-list-render-pass1.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-list-render-pass1.svg)
###  Pipeline State render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#pipeline-state-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Pipeline State render pass allows you to set for its child render passes depth and stencil testing, transparency, and culling. This render pass sets the rendering state before passing the control to its descendants. After the descendant render passes of a Pipeline State render pass execute, Kanzi restores the rendering state. See [Setting the cull mode](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/meshes/setting-culling.html#setting-the-cull-mode), [Applying a stencil to 3D content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/stencil-buffer.html), and [Rendering decals](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-decals.html).
![../../_images/pipeline-state-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/pipeline-state-render-pass.svg)
## Render Pass Presets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#render-pass-presets "Link to this heading")
###  Compose and Blit Pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#compose-and-blit-pass "Link to this heading")
Compose and Blit Pass contains the render pass structure that enables you to blit to the screen Composition Target render passes or textures using a specific material.
See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html).
![../../_images/compose-and-blit-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/compose-and-blit-pass.svg)
###  Default render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#default-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Default render pass contains a basic set of render passes that first render opaque nodes and then transparent nodes.
Use the Default render pass as a starting point for your render pass tree. See [Using the Default render pass](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html#using-drp).
![../../_images/default-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/default-render-pass.svg)
###  Render to Texture Pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#render-to-texture-pass "Link to this heading")
Render to Texture Pass creates the render passes and texture you need to render to a texture.
See [Rendering to texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html#rendering-to-texture).
![../../_images/render-to-texture-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-to-texture-pass.svg)
###  Image-Based Lighting Filter Pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#image-based-lighting-filter-pass "Link to this heading")
Image-Based Lighting Filter Pass contains the render passes that enable you to create dynamic Environment Ambient Texture and Environment Reflection Texture cubemap textures for real-time image-based lighting. See [Rendering cubemaps for dynamic image-based lighting](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html#rendering-cubemaps-for-dynamic-image-based-lighting).
![../../_images/render-passes-image-based-lighting.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-passes-image-based-lighting.svg)![../../_images/rendering-cubemaps-dynamic-ibl.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rendering-cubemaps-dynamic-ibl.gif)
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#sa "Link to this heading")

# Collecting nodes for rendering[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/filtering-node-lists.html#collecting-nodes-for-rendering "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Node List render pass to filter and hold a list of 3D nodes that you want to render using other render passes.
![../../_images/node-list-render-pass1.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-list-render-pass1.svg)
The Draw Objects render pass and Draw Objects With Material render passes draw 3D content in a scene.
By default the Draw Objects render pass and Draw Objects With Material render pass draw all the 3D content in a scene or the nodes provided by their nearest ancestor Node List render pass.
For example, in this render pass prefab the Draw Objects render pass by default draws the nodes provided by the Node List render pass:
![../../_images/node-list-gather-lights-draw-objects.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-list-gather-lights-draw-objects.png)
You can use any Node List render pass in the same Render Pass Prefab to provide nodes to a Draw Objects render pass and Draw Objects With Material render pass for rendering. To learn how to use filters to pass nodes to render passes, see [Filters](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/filters.html).
To set the Node List render pass that you want to use to collect 3D nodes for rendering:
  1. In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs select the Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass that you want to use to draw 3D nodes.
![../../_images/draw-objects-render-pass-node-list.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-objects-render-pass-node-list.png)
  2. In the Properties click + Add Binding, and in the Binding Editor set:
     * Property to Node List
     * Expression to point to the Output Node List property of the Node List render pass whose output nodes you want to render
For example, to draw the nodes provided by a sibling Node List render pass of the Draw Objects render pass, set the Expression to:

```
{@../Node List/NodeListRenderPass.OutputNodeList}

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/draw-objects-render-pass-node-list-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-objects-render-pass-node-list-binding.png)
