Single textures use a single image for the texture.
Before you can create a texture in Kanzi Studio you first have to have an image you use in that texture. You can create the texture image in a third-party tool and import the image to Kanzi Studio. See [Importing images](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-images.html).
## Creating a single texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-single-textures.html#creating-a-single-texture "Link to this heading")
To create a single texture:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures and select Single Texture.
![../../_images/create-single-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-single-texture.png)
  2. In the Properties set the Image property to the image you want to use for the texture.
Avoid creating mipmaps from .jpeg textures, because the .jpeg image format causes the quality of the mipmaps to degrade.
![../../_images/set-single-texture-image-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-single-texture-image-property.png)
  3. (Optional)
In the Properties set the Texture Settings properties.
Use the Texture Settings properties to control the texture filtering. Start by setting the Mipmap Mode property to the mipmap mode you want to use. Then set the Minification Filter and Magnification Filter properties to Linear. Note that using mipmaps increases the memory use.
Usually the best starting point for setting texture filtering is to set:
     * Minification Filter to Linear
     * Magnification Filter to Linear
     * Mipmap Mode to Nearest. If you are sure that the texture is not minified select Base, otherwise start with Nearest. For example, the default value for a Render Target Texture is Base. With this setting, the texture does not have mipmap levels and the base level is always sampled. See [Using mipmaps](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html).
![../../_images/texture-settings-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-settings-properties.png)
Note that some texture formats are available with OpenGL ES versions higher than 2.0. To set the OpenGL ES version, in the main menu select Project > Properties and in the Properties set the Target Graphics API property.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/target-graphics-api-opengl-es-30.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-graphics-api-opengl-es-30.png)
For example, set the Target Graphics API property to OpenGL ES 3.0, import HDR and floating point images in .dds format, and set the color format of textures. See [Using OpenGL ES 3.0+ in Kanzi](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-opengl-es-30.html).  
| Mipmap Mode  | Nearest sample  | Linear sample  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Base  |  Number of samples: 1 Uses the nearest pixel in the texture. This combination is equal to point sample. It returns the crudest result of all combinations and can cause aliasing when minified. Use this combination to get a very sharp result when magnifying the texture.  |  Number of samples: 4 Interpolates between four nearest pixels in the texture. Use this combination to magnify gradients. However, do not use it for minification.  |  
| Nearest  |  Number of samples: 1 Helps texture caching and helps reduce aliasing. However, it can produce a sharp transition when the texture is used on a flat surface. Use this combination when you want good performance and cannot afford better quality on your target platform. This combination is usually the fastest.  |  Number of samples: 4 Takes two samples from two mipmap levels and interpolates between these samples. Use this combination as the starting point. This combination is usually the best compromise between quality and performance. If you know there is no minification, you can set Mipmap Mode to Base.  |  
| Linear  |  Number of samples: 2 Takes one sample from two mipmap levels and interpolates between those samples. Use this combination for special effects. For example, to implement the rim light effect.  |  Number of samples: 8 Takes four samples from two mipmap levels and interpolates between these samples. Use this combination when you want the best quality and your platform is powerful enough to effortlessly render the result. This combination has the largest negative impact on performance.  |  


## Using a single texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-single-textures.html#using-a-single-texture "Link to this heading")
You can use single textures on Model and Image nodes:
  * To use a texture on a mesh, set the material that supports textures to use your texture, and then set the mesh to use that material. See [Creating textured materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/creating-textured-materials.html).
  * To use a single texture on an Image node, in the Node Tree select the Image node, and in the Properties set the Image property to the single texture you want to use on that Image node. See [Using the Image node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/using-images.html).


##  Single Texture property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-single-textures.html#single-texture-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for single textures, see [Single Texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/single-texture-reference.html) and [Texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/texture-reference.html).

Volume textures use a single 2D image, made up of many cross-section slices of a 3D shape, to define a 3D volume texture. This technique is often used for effects like smoke, fire, or clouds, where 3D data would be too resource intensive or difficult to generate procedurally.
Before you can create a volume texture in Kanzi Studio you first have to have an image to use in that texture. The image must be made up of vertical slices of the 3D shape, taken at a constant intervals and in stacked in sequence on top of each other. See [Using a volume texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-volume-textures.html#using-a-volume-texture).
You can create such a texture image in a third-party tool and import the image to Kanzi Studio. See [Importing images](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-images.html).
## Rendering example using volume textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-volume-textures.html#rendering-example-using-volume-textures "Link to this heading")
Below is an example of how volume textures can be used in Kanzi Studio for:
  * Rendering signed distance fields to create a realistic looking surface with accurate ambient occlusion, reflections and soft shadow calculations.
  * Using 3D texture data to raymarch a volume representing density, creating a realistic smoke effect.


## Creating a volume texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-volume-textures.html#creating-a-volume-texture "Link to this heading")
To create a volume texture:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures and select Volume Texture.
![../../_images/create-volume-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-volume-texture.png)
  2. In the Properties set the Image property to the image you want to use for the volume texture.
![../../_images/set-volume-texture-image-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-volume-texture-image-property.png)
  3. In the Properties set the Slice Count to specify how many depth slices the selected image file contains.


## Using a volume texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-volume-textures.html#using-a-volume-texture "Link to this heading")
You can use volume textures on Model nodes:
  * To use a volume texture on a mesh, set the material that uses a sampler3D uniform to use your texture, and then set the mesh to use that material. See [Editing shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/editing-shaders.html) And [Shader uniforms](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/editing-shaders.html#shader-uniforms).
  * Example of a valid volume texture image containing 32 slices of size 32px x 32px.
![../../_images/volume-texture-example.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/volume-texture-example.png)


##  Volume Texture property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-volume-textures.html#volume-texture-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for volume textures, see [Volume Texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/volume-texture-reference.html) and [Texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/texture-reference.html).

Use a Render Target Texture to render content to a texture or to apply anti-aliasing to only a part of your application. You can use render target textures like any other texture. For example, you can use it in a Texture Brush or as an image in an Image node.
See [Applying anti-aliasing](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/anti-aliasing.html) and [Textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html).
For example, if your Kanzi application has more than one scene, you can use render target textures to show the content of other scenes in the current scene.
## Rendering content to a texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-render-target-textures.html#rendering-content-to-a-texture "Link to this heading")
To render content to a texture:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures and select Render Target Texture.
![../../_images/create-render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-render-target-texture.png)
  2. In the Node Tree create or select a 2D node the content of which you want to render to a texture.
For example, select a Viewport 2D node that contains the content that you want to render to a texture.
![../../_images/prefab-for-render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefab-for-render-target-texture.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the node that you created or selected in the previous step and in the Properties add and set:
     * Render Target to the Render Target Texture to which you want to render the content of the selected node.
     * Off-Screen Rendering and enable the property.
![../../_images/layer-render-target-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layer-render-target-property.png)
  4. (Optional) To set Kanzi to render the content to the texture only once, in the Properties add the Caching Mode property and set it to Enabled.
This way you set Kanzi to cache the node, and to keep rendering the node from the cache image. For example, enable caching for a node for which you want Kanzi to create the render target texture only once at application startup. See [Caching 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/caching-2d-nodes.html).
![../../_images/caching-mode-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/caching-mode-enabled.png)
  5. Apply the Render Target Texture that you created in the first step to a node where you want to show the content of the node that you created in the second step.
You can use the Render Target Texture in a Texture Brush or as an image in an Image node.
For example:
    1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click and select Empty Node 2D.
    2. In the Node Tree select the Empty Node 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and in the dropdown menu select + Texture Brush.
![../../_images/select-create-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-create-texture-brush.png)
    3. Next to the Background Brush property click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) and set the Brush Texture property of the Texture Brush to the Render Target Texture you want to show in the Empty Node 2D you created in the first step.
![../../_images/image-property-render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-property-render-target-texture.png)
    4. In the Node Tree select the Empty Node 2D, and in the Properties add and set the Layout Width and Layout Height properties to the size in which you want to show the content of the Render Target Texture.
  6. (Optional) In the Library select the Render Target Texture.
In the Properties, you can set the Height and Width of the Render Target, or use the Automatic setting to set the size of the Render Target based on the size of the node where it is used. You cannot yet use this property with a render pass.
![../../_images/render-target-automatic-size.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-target-automatic-size.png)
Use the Texture Settings properties to control the texture filtering. Start by setting the Mipmap Mode property to the mipmap mode you want to use. Then set the Minification Filter and Magnification Filter properties to Linear. Note that using mipmaps increases the memory use.
Usually the best starting point for setting texture filtering is to set:
     * Minification Filter to Linear
     * Magnification Filter to Linear
     * Mipmap Mode to Nearest. If you are sure that the texture is not minified select Base, otherwise start with Nearest. For example, the default value for a Render Target Texture is Base. With this setting, the texture does not have mipmap levels and the base level is always sampled. See [Using mipmaps](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html).
![../../_images/texture-settings-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-settings-properties.png)
Note that some texture formats are available with OpenGL ES versions higher than 2.0. To set the OpenGL ES version, in the main menu select Project > Properties and in the Properties set the Target Graphics API property.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/target-graphics-api-opengl-es-30.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-graphics-api-opengl-es-30.png)
For example, set the Target Graphics API property to OpenGL ES 3.0, import HDR and floating point images in .dds format, and set the color format of textures. See [Using OpenGL ES 3.0+ in Kanzi](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-opengl-es-30.html).  
| Mipmap Mode  | Nearest sample  | Linear sample  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Base  |  Number of samples: 1 Uses the nearest pixel in the texture. This combination is equal to point sample. It returns the crudest result of all combinations and can cause aliasing when minified. Use this combination to get a very sharp result when magnifying the texture.  |  Number of samples: 4 Interpolates between four nearest pixels in the texture. Use this combination to magnify gradients. However, do not use it for minification.  |  
| Nearest  |  Number of samples: 1 Helps texture caching and helps reduce aliasing. However, it can produce a sharp transition when the texture is used on a flat surface. Use this combination when you want good performance and cannot afford better quality on your target platform. This combination is usually the fastest.  |  Number of samples: 4 Takes two samples from two mipmap levels and interpolates between these samples. Use this combination as the starting point. This combination is usually the best compromise between quality and performance. If you know there is no minification, you can set Mipmap Mode to Base.  |  
| Linear  |  Number of samples: 2 Takes one sample from two mipmap levels and interpolates between those samples. Use this combination for special effects. For example, to implement the rim light effect.  |  Number of samples: 8 Takes four samples from two mipmap levels and interpolates between these samples. Use this combination when you want the best quality and your platform is powerful enough to effortlessly render the result. This combination has the largest negative impact on performance.  |  


##  Render Target Texture property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-render-target-textures.html#render-target-texture-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for render target textures, see [Render Target Texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/render-target-texture-reference.html) and [Texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/texture-reference.html).

# Using image-based lighting cubemap textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html#using-image-based-lighting-cubemap-textures "Link to this heading")

Use image-based lighting to light 3D nodes by treating their surrounding environment as a source of lights.
Image-based lighting cubemap textures simulate lighting coming from the environment:
  * **Irradiance cubemap texture** represents the indirect diffuse part of the environment lighting.
A fully diffuse surface is rough and reflects incoming light rays in random directions. For example, rubbery materials have a diffuse surface.
  * **Specular cubemap texture** represents the reflective part of the environment lighting.
A fully reflective surface is smooth and reflects incoming light rays in the same angle as they arrive, like a mirror. For example, metallic materials have a reflective surface.


Each image-based lighting cubemap texture combines six square-shaped images into one texture to represent environment lighting.
Use an environment cubemap texture to render the environment around your 3D content. See [Using environment textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html).
When you want to create dynamic reflections of the environment on the surface of 3D nodes, use the Cubemap render pass. See [Creating cubemap reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/cubemap-render-pass.html).
## Creating image-based lighting cubemap textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html#creating-image-based-lighting-cubemap-textures "Link to this heading")
To create image-based lighting cubemap textures:
  1. In the Assets, click Import Assets and select an hdr or exr image for which you want to create image-based lighting cubemap textures.
![../../_images/assets-import-assets.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assets-import-assets.png)
Tip
To create image-based lighting cubemap textures for an hdr or exr image that you have already imported to your Kanzi Studio project, in the Library > Resource Files > Images press `Alt` and right-click that image and select Image-Based Lighting Cubemap Textures.
![../../_images/create-ibl-textures-context-menu.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-ibl-textures-context-menu.png)
  2. In the Create Textures for HDR Images dialog:
    1. Select Image-Based Lighting Cubemap Textures.
![../../_images/create-ibl-textures-dialog.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-ibl-textures-dialog.png)
Tip
To create also an environment cubemap texture for the image, select Environment Cubemap Texture. See [Using environment textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html).
    2. (Optional) To manually set the size of the cubemap faces, disable the Automatic setting and set the Cubemap Face Resolution.
For example, to create cubemap textures where the size of each cubemap face is 512 by 512 pixels, set Cubemap Face Resolution to 512.
By default, Kanzi Studio creates cubemap textures where the width and height of each cubemap face are 256 pixels, or, if the width of the image that you import is less than 1024 pixels, one quarter of that width.
Increasing the cubemap face resolution increases the cubemap calculation time quadratically.
    3. (Optional) Set the Number of Samples to the number of pixels that you want Kanzi Studio to sample from the image and use to generate the cubemaps.
The more samples, the more accurately the cubemap approximates the environment lighting. Increasing the number of samples increases the cubemap calculation time linearly. The default value of 1024 samples is expected to be enough for most situations. However, for an image that contains very high frequency changes, such as a bright sun, using a higher sample count can reduce the amount of noise in the generated cubemap face images.
    4. Click Create.
Kanzi Studio imports the image and creates in the Library > Materials and Textures > Textures the image-based lighting cubemap textures for that image:
     * <image_name>_irradiance represents the indirect diffuse portion of the environment lighting.
     * <image_name>_specular represents the reflective lighting.
![../../_images/ibl-textures-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/ibl-textures-in-library.png) ![../../_images/my_hdr_image_irradiance.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my_hdr_image_irradiance.png) ![../../_images/my_hdr_image_specular.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my_hdr_image_specular.png)
Tip
You can restrict the brightness of strongly lit areas in the textures that you create from an HDR image.
To set the maximum brightness level in the cubemap textures that you create from an HDR image:
    1. In the Library > Resource Files > Images, select the image. In the Properties, add the Clamp Pixels property and set it to the value to which you want to restrict the color values in the cubemap face images that you create from that image.
    2. In the Library > Resource Files > Images, press `Alt` and right-click the image and select the cubemap texture that you want to create.
![../../_images/clamp-pixels.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clamp-pixels.png) ![../../_images/recreate-env-cubemap-textures.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/recreate-env-cubemap-textures.png)


Note
Kanzi Studio stores the generated cubemap faces and roughness mipmaps in cache directories that you typically exclude from version control. When they are missing, such as after a fresh clone or after you import an asset package that does not include them, Kanzi Studio regenerates them from the source image. For this reason, keep the source hdr or exr image in your project and in version control. See [Using version control systems with Kanzi](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html).
Image-based lighting cubemap textures that you created before Kanzi 4.1.0 do not store the information that Kanzi Studio needs to regenerate them. Recreate these textures so that they regenerate correctly.
## Using image-based lighting cubemap textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html#id1 "Link to this heading")
To use image-based lighting cubemap textures:
  1. In the Library > Materials and Textures, press `Alt` and right-click Material Types and select SmartPhysicallyBased.
Kanzi Studio creates the SmartPhysicallyBased material type and the SmartPhysicallyBasedMaterial material.
This material supports using the features of the Kanzi default physically-based shaders.
![../../_images/library-smart-physically-based-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-smart-physically-based-material.png)
  2. Create the 3D content that you want to light by treating their surrounding environment as a source of lights, and set that content to use the SmartPhysicallyBasedMaterial material.
For example, in the Node Tree, create a Sphere node. In the Properties, set the Mesh Material property to SmartPhysicallyBasedMaterial.
![../../_images/sphere-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/sphere-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/sphere-properties-mesh-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/sphere-properties-mesh-material.png)
  3. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Materials, select the SmartPhysicallyBasedMaterial. In the Properties, add the Configuration > Enable Image Based Lighting property and set:
     * Environment Ambient Texture to the irradiance cubemap texture that you want to use for diffuse lighting.
     * Environment Reflection Texture to the specular cubemap texture that you want to use for reflective lighting.
See [Creating image-based lighting cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html#creating-image-based-lighting-cubemap-textures).
![../../_images/properties-add-enable-image-based-lighting.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-add-enable-image-based-lighting.png) ![../../_images/physically-based-material-ibl-textures.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/physically-based-material-ibl-textures.png)
  4. (Optional) In the Properties, add and set:
     * Material > Environment Ambient Factor to set the strength of the irradiance cubemap texture.
     * Material > Environment Reflection Factor to set the strength of the specular cubemap texture.
  5. Use the material properties to control the strength of the reflections on the material surface.
For example, for a metallic-roughness material:
     * Roughness Factor sets the roughness of the material.
When you increase the roughness of a material, the reflections on the material surface get blurrier.
     * Metallic Factor sets the metalness of the material.
When you increase the metalness of a material:
       * Diffuse reflections on the material surface get weaker.
       * Specular reflections on the material surface get stronger.
![../../_images/physically-based-material-ibl-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/physically-based-material-ibl-properties.png) ![../../_images/ibl-in-preview-without-env.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/ibl-in-preview-without-env.png)


When you use an environment cubemap texture to render the environment around your 3D content, you can see how the image-based lighting textures simulate the lighting coming from the environment. See [Using an environment cubemap texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html#using-an-environment-cubemap-texture).
![../../_images/ibl-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/ibl-in-preview.png)
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Using single textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-single-textures.html)

[Images](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/images.html)

[Importing](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing.html)

# Theming your applications[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#theming-your-applications "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Themes enable you to use a single Kanzi Studio project for multiple variants of your product.
For example, in a single project you can define Kanzi applications for different car models and different visual themes for each car model.
Creating themes for your application involves the creation and use of different resources, such as, text, textures, brushes, materials, and styles, and layouts for themes that you want to use in your applications.
A Theme Group defines a collection of Themes. Each Theme in a Theme Group defines the look and feel of your application. In your Kanzi Studio project you can define more than one Theme Group, where each contains several Themes. In your Kanzi application you can apply one Theme from each Theme Group at a time. For example, you can use one Theme Group to define a car model, such as hatchback, minivan, pickup, sedan, and SUV, and another Theme Group to define the look of the interface for each of the car models, such as, classic, digital, modern, and sport.
Kanzi uses themed resources indirectly using resource IDs that hold a separate value for each Theme. In the Library > Themes you can see all Theme Group items in your Kanzi Studio project.
![../../_images/export-example-library-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-example-library-color.png)
To create a theme for your application:
  1. Create a Theme Group and add to it the resources in your project which you want to define with a Theme. See [Adding resources used in a project to a Theme Group](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#adding-resources-used-in-project-to-theme-group).
  2. Create and import resources each Theme uses. See [Setting resources for a Theme](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#setting-resources-for-theme).
  3. View a Theme in the Preview. See [Viewing a theme in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#viewing).
  4. Export resources used by a Theme to kzb files. See [Exporting Themes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/exporting-themes.html).


Learn how to theme your Kanzi applications by completing a tutorial. See [Tutorial: Theme your application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/theming/theming.html).
## Adding resources used in a project to a Theme Group[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#adding-resources-used-in-a-project-to-a-theme-group "Link to this heading")
Start creating a theme for your Kanzi application by adding resources which you want to theme to a Theme Group. The easiest way to add resources to a Theme Group is to use the Add Resources to a Theme Group command on a node in the Node Tree.
When you use the Add Resources to a Theme Group command in the Node Tree, Kanzi Studio automatically creates a resource ID for each resource in the node and nodes in its tree and sets each node to use those resource IDs.
To add resources used in a project to a Theme Group:
  1. In the Node Tree right-click the Screen node and in the context menu select Add Resources to a Theme Group.
When you use the Add Resources to a Theme Group command on the Screen node, Kanzi Studio enables you to add all resources in your project to a Theme Group and change their appearance in each Theme. To add to a Theme Group resources only from a selected node or prefab and its tree, right-click that node or prefab and select Add Resources to a Theme Group.
![../../_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png)
  2. In the Add Resources to a Theme Group window set:
    1. Theme Group to the Theme Group to which you want to add the resources. If you do not have a Theme Group yet, select <Create New>.
A Theme Group defines a collection of Themes.
    2. Select the resource type you want to show in the Add Resources to a Theme Group window.
For example, to show only text and image resources select ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resource-type-text.png) and ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resource-type-image.png).
![../../_images/show-resource-types.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/show-resource-types.png)
    3. In the table that lists all resources of the types you selected, click the checkbox next to the resource you want to add to the Theme Group you selected. To change the resource ID, double-click the resource ID and enter a new name.
Kanzi Studio creates a single resource ID for Text Block nodes which use the same value for the Text property. These nodes share the same entry in a Theme Group.
    4. Click Add.
Kanzi Studio creates resource IDs from all resources and adds them to the Theme Group you selected. You can find Theme Group items in the Library > Themes. In the Theme Group you can now create Themes and set which resource you want to use for which Theme. See [Setting resources for a Theme](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#setting-resources-for-theme).
![../../_images/library-themes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-themes.png)


## Setting resources for a Theme[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#setting-resources-for-a-theme "Link to this heading")
After you add resources used in your project to a Theme Group you can create a Theme and define the resources used by each Theme.
To set resources for a Theme:
  1. Create and import resources you want to use for each Theme. For example:
     * In the Library create the resources, such as, brushes, styles, and materials which set the appearance for each theme in your application.
     * In the Prefabs create the layouts which arrange the UI elements for each theme in your application.
     * In the Assets import the 2D and 3D assets which you want to use in a Theme.
  2. In the Library > Themes double-click the Theme Group where you want to define a Theme.
  3. In the Theme Editor click Create Theme and name the Theme.
![../../_images/create-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-theme.png)
  4. In the column of the theme you created in the previous step, double-click the cell for each resource, and set the resource you want to use for the resource ID in that row.
     * If you do not select a resource or value for a Theme, Kanzi uses the default resource or value for that Theme. The default value is listed in the Default Value column.
Black cells mark entries which use the default value.
     * To use an empty string for a text resource, enter a value, delete the value, and then press the `Enter` key.
Gray cells mark entries which use an empty string.
     * To use a resource from the file system, in the cell for which you want to set the resource select < URL >, and enter `file://` followed by the absolute or relative path to the resource in the file system.
![../../_images/theme-editor-set-resource.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/theme-editor-set-resource.png)


## Using a kzb file URL for a resource in a Theme[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#using-a-kzb-file-url-for-a-resource-in-a-theme "Link to this heading")
After you add resources used in your project to a Theme Group, you can use a kzb file URL to point to a resource in another Kanzi Studio project.
To use a kzb file URL for a resource in a Theme:
  1. In the Library > Themes double-click the Theme Group where you want to define a Theme.
  2. In the Theme Editor click Create Theme and name the Theme.
![../../_images/create-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-theme.png)
  3. In the column of the Theme you created in the previous step, double-click the cell for the resource for which you want to use a kzb file URL, and in the dropdown menu select < URL >.
![../../_images/select-url-in-theme-editor.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-url-in-theme-editor.png)
  4. In the cell enter the kzb file URL of the resource you want to use.
For example, to use a font from another Kanzi Studio project, enter the kzb file URL pointing to that font.
![../../_images/set-kzb-url-in-theme-editor.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-kzb-url-in-theme-editor.png)


## Viewing a theme in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#viewing-a-theme-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
When you are defining a Theme for your application, you can set the Preview to show that Theme without adding to the application a control for switching Themes.
To view a Theme in the Preview:
  * In the Dictionaries click Locales and Themes to enable the viewing of Localization Table and Theme Group items, and for each Theme Group select the Theme you want to see in the Preview.
![../../_images/activate-theme-dictionaries.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/activate-theme-dictionaries.png)
  * In the Library select the Theme Group which contains the Theme you want to view and in the Properties set the Selected Theme property to that Theme.
![../../_images/export-example-library-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-example-library-color.png) ![../../_images/properties-startup-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-startup-theme.png)


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Tutorial: Theme your application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/theming/theming.html)
[Exporting Themes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/exporting-themes.html)
[Using Themes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html)

Kanzi uses a Theme as an ID to select the resources associated with that Theme. If you do not define a resource for a Theme, Kanzi uses the default value for that resource ID in that Theme Group.
Learn how to theme your Kanzi applications by completing a tutorial. See [Tutorial: Theme your application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/theming/theming.html).
## Creating a Theme[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html#creating-a-theme "Link to this heading")
To create a Theme:
  1. In the Library > Themes double-click the Theme Group to which you want to add a Theme.
Kanzi Studio opens the Theme Group in the Theme Editor.
  2. In the Theme Editor click Create Theme, enter the name for the Theme, and click OK.
![../../_images/create-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-theme.png)


## Renaming a Theme[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html#renaming-a-theme "Link to this heading")
To change the name of an existing Theme:
  1. In the Library > Themes double-click the Theme Group which contains the Theme you want to rename.
![../../_images/color-theme-group-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-theme-group-in-library.png)
  2. In the Theme Editor right-click the header of the Theme you want to rename and select Rename.
![../../_images/rename-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rename-theme.png)
  3. Enter the new name for the Theme and click OK.
![../../_images/rename-theme-dialog.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rename-theme-dialog.png)


## Setting the application Theme[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html#setting-the-application-theme "Link to this heading")
You can set the application Theme in these ways:
  * To set the Theme that your application uses when a user launches the application or that you want to see in the Kanzi Studio Preview:
    * In the Library > Themes select the Theme Group which contains the Theme you want to use and set the Selected Theme to the Theme you want to use.
![../../_images/color-theme-group-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-theme-group-in-library.png) ![../../_images/properties-startup-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-startup-theme.png)
    * In the Dictionaries window click Locales and Themes and for each Theme Group in your project select the Theme you want to use.
![../../_images/dictionaries-select-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dictionaries-select-theme.png)
  * To set a Theme using a trigger, in a trigger that you want to use to set the application theme, create a Theme: Activate Theme action and set the Theme that you want to use.
![../../_images/triggers-activate-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/triggers-activate-theme.png) ![../../_images/triggers-activate-theme-set-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/triggers-activate-theme-set-theme.png)


## Adding a resource to a Theme Group manually[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html#adding-a-resource-to-a-theme-group-manually "Link to this heading")
The fastest way to add a resource to a Theme Group is to use in the Node Tree the Add Resources to a Theme Group command. See [Adding resources used in a project to a Theme Group](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#adding-resources-used-in-project-to-theme-group).
![../../_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png)
To add a resource to a Theme Group manually:
  1. In the Library > Themes double-click the Theme Group which contains the Theme to which you want to manually add resources.
Kanzi Studio opens the Theme Group in the Theme Editor.
![../../_images/export-example-library-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-example-library-color.png)
  2. In the Theme Editor click + Add Resource and select:
     * Create and select the type of resource you want to create.
     * Add Existing and select a resource that already exists in your project.
![../../_images/add-resource.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-resource.png)
  3. Enter a name for the resource ID you want to use for that resource and click OK.
  4. In the Theme Editor in the column of each Theme set resource you want to use for the resource ID you created.
  5. In the Node Tree select the node where you want to use the resource ID you created, in the Properties set the property which points to a resource to < Resource ID >, and enter the resource ID you created in the Theme Editor.


## Deleting resource IDs from a Theme Group[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html#deleting-resource-ids-from-a-theme-group "Link to this heading")
To delete resource IDs from a Theme Group:
  * To delete resource IDs that are not used in the project, click Clean, select the resource IDs you want to delete, and click OK.
![../../_images/delete-unused-resource-ids.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/delete-unused-resource-ids.png)
  * To delete a resource ID, right-click the resource ID and select Delete Resource ID.
  * To delete multiple resource IDs press the `Ctrl` or `Shift` key and select resource IDs you want to delete, and press the `Delete` key.


## Localizing a Theme[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html#localizing-a-theme "Link to this heading")
Kanzi enables you to localize themed applications.
To localize themes:
  1. For each theme the content of which you want to localize, create a prefab from the content that includes the text nodes you want to localize. See [Creating and using a node prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#creating-and-using-a-node-prefab).
![../../_images/table-rpm-gasoline-hybrid-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/table-rpm-gasoline-hybrid-prefabs.png)
  2. Localize the text resources:
    1. In the Prefabs select the prefabs you created in the previous step and add their resources to a localization table.
See [Adding resources to a localization table](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/localization/localizing-applications.html#adding-resources-to-a-localization-table).
![../../_images/add-resources-to-localization-table.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-resources-to-localization-table.png) ![../../_images/localization-table-add.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/localization-table-add.png)
    2. In the Library > Localization double-click the localization table you created in the previous step to open it in the Localization Editor, add the locales to which you want to localize themes, and localize the text resources. See [Localizing text resources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/localization/localizing-applications.html#localizing-text-resources).
To add a locale click + Create Locale, enter the name for the locale, and click OK.
![../../_images/localization-editor-with-localized-text.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/localization-editor-with-localized-text.png)
  3. Use Prefab View nodes to show the localized content:
    1. In the Prefabs under the node where you want to show the localized content create a Prefab View node and in the Properties add and set the Prefab Template property to one of the prefabs you created in step 1.
You must use a Prefab View node so that you can dynamically change the prefab that the Prefab View instantiates. See [Prefab Placeholder and Prefab View nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#prefab-placeholder-and-prefab-view-nodes).
![../../_images/table-rpm-prefab-view-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/table-rpm-prefab-view-in-project.png) ![../../_images/displayed-prefab-in-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/displayed-prefab-in-properties.png)
    2. In the Prefabs right-click the Prefab View node you created in the previous step and select Add Resources to a Theme Group.
![../../_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png)
    3. In the Add Resources to a Theme Group window:
       * Set the Theme Group to the theme group to which you want to add the resources.
A theme group contains the information about which theme uses which resources.
       * Rename the Resource ID to something that is meaningful in the context of your project.
Click Add.
Kanzi Studio adds to the theme group the resource ID which points to the prefab shown in the Value column. In the Prefab View node from which you add the resources to a Theme Group, Kanzi Studio sets the value of the Prefab Template property to the resource ID.
![../../_images/add-displayed-prefab-to-theme-group.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-displayed-prefab-to-theme-group.png) ![../../_images/table-rpm-displayed-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/table-rpm-displayed-prefab.png)
    4. (Optional) In the Prefabs copy the Prefab View node you created in step 1 to the places where you want to show the same content.
![../../_images/table-rpm-prefab-views-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/table-rpm-prefab-views-in-project.png)
    5. In the Library > Themes double-click the theme group to which you added the resources, and in the Theme Editor for the resource ID you created in step 3 select the correct prefab for each theme.
![../../_images/table-rpm-in-theme-editor.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/table-rpm-in-theme-editor.png)
  4. In the Dictionaries window to view the resource dictionaries of localization tables and theme groups in the project, click Locales and Themes, and select different locales and themes to see the localized themes in the Preview.
![../../_images/dictionaries-set-locale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dictionaries-set-locale.png) ![../../_images/dictionaries-set-car-variant-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dictionaries-set-car-variant-theme.png)


## Using themes in multiple Kanzi Studio projects combined into a Kanzi application[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html#using-themes-in-multiple-ks-projects-combined-into-a-k-application "Link to this heading")
To use themes when you combine multiple Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application, you must make the theme groups accessible to the Screen node of the main project of your application in one of these ways:
  * Define the theme groups in the main project of your application.
  * Merge the theme groups from referenced projects to the main project which contains the Screen node. You can then use resource IDs to access the resources in the theme groups from the referenced projects. See [Merging projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html).
  * Contact the Rightware support team and request the Kanzi Engine plugin which enables you to use theming across multiple Kanzi Studio projects and kzb files. See [Submitting a support request](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/technical-support.html#submitting-a-support-request).

Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
Trajectories are paths in 3D space. See [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html) and [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html).
Kanzi Studio comes with these trajectory types:
  * Use an Angle Trajectory to create a path where two straight lines form an angle in 3D space.
See [Using angle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-angle-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/angle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/angle.png)
  * Use an Arc Trajectory to create a path in the shape of an arc in 3D space.
See [Using arc trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-arc-trajectories.html)
![../../_images/arc.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/arc.png)
  * Use a Circle Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a circle in 3D space.
See [Using circle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-circle-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/circle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/circle.png)
  * Use an Ellipse Trajectory to create a path in the shape of an ellipse in 3D space.
See [Using ellipse trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-ellipse-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/ellipse.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/ellipse.png)
  * Use a Line Trajectory to create a path with a single straight line in 3D space.
See [Using line trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-line-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/line.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/line.png)
  * Use a Rectangle Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a rectangle in 3D space.
See [Using rectangle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-rectangle-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/rectangle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rectangle.png)
  * Use a Spiral Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a spiral in 3D space.
See [Using spiral trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spiral-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/spiral.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/spiral.png)
  * Use a Spline Trajectory to import a trajectory defined by a set of points and control points in 3D space you created in a third-party tool.
See [Using spline trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html).
  * Use a Trapezoid Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a trapezoid in 3D space.
See [Using trapezoid trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trapezoid-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/trapezoid.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trapezoid.png)


## Using trajectories in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html#using-trajectories-in-the-api "Link to this heading")

![../../_images/angle-trajectory-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/angle-trajectory-in-preview.png)
## Creating an angle trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-angle-trajectories.html#creating-an-angle-trajectory "Link to this heading")
To create an angle trajectory:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Trajectories and select Angle Trajectory.
![../../_images/create-angle-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-angle-trajectory.png)
  2. In the Properties set these properties:
     * Normal to set the position of the trajectory in 3D space.
For example:
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the x axis, set X to 1, and Y and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the y axis, set Y to 1, and X and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into I and II, and VII and VIII octants, set X to 1, Y to -1, and the Z property field to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into II and III, and V and VIII octants, set Y and Z to 1, and the X property field to 0.
     * Length to set the length of the trajectory.
     * Angle to set the size of the angle in degrees.
![../../_images/angle-trajectory-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/angle-trajectory-properties.png)
  3. To take the trajectory into use, in the Node Tree select a Trajectory Layout or a Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties set the Trajectory property to the trajectory you want to use. See [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html) and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).


##  Angle Trajectory property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-angle-trajectories.html#angle-trajectory-property-types "Link to this heading")

Use an Ellipse Trajectory to create a path in the shape of an ellipse in 3D space.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
See [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html) and [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html).
![../../_images/ellipse-trajectory-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/ellipse-trajectory-in-preview.png)
## Creating an ellipse trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-ellipse-trajectories.html#creating-an-ellipse-trajectory "Link to this heading")
To create an ellipse trajectory:
  1. In the Library right-click Trajectories and select Create > Ellipse Trajectory.
![../../_images/create-ellipse-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-ellipse-trajectory.png)
  2. In the Properties set these properties:
     * Normal to set the position of the trajectory in 3D space.
For example:
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the x axis, set X to 1, and Y and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the y axis, set Y to 1, and X and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into I and II, and VII and VIII octants, set X to 1, Y to -1, and the Z property field to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into II and III, and V and VIII octants, set Y and Z to 1, and the X property field to 0.
     * Radius A to set the size of the ellipse trajectory on the X axis.
     * Radius B to set the size of the ellipse trajectory on the Y axis.
     * Angle to set the starting point of the ellipse trajectory.
![../../_images/ellipse-trajectory-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/ellipse-trajectory-properties.png)
  3. To take the trajectory into use, in the Node Tree select a Trajectory Layout or a Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties set the Trajectory property to the trajectory you want to use. See [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html) and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).

![../../_images/create-line-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-line-trajectory.png)
  2. In the Properties set these properties:
     * Length to set the length of the trajectory.
     * Direction to set the position of the trajectory in 3D space.

       * To set the trajectory diagonally into the I octant, set X, Y, and Z property fields to 1.

Use a Spline Trajectory to import a trajectory defined by a set of points and control points in 3D space you created in a third-party tool.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
You can import and convert curves, including NURBS curves, to Kanzi splines from .fbx files. Make sure that your third-party software exports splines as curves. See [Adjusting a spline created from a NURBS curve](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html#adjusting-a-spline-created-from-a-nurbs-curve).
## Creating a spline trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html#creating-a-spline-trajectory "Link to this heading")
To create a spline trajectory:
  1. Select File > Import > Import 3D Assets and select the .fbx file containing the spline you want to use for a trajectory.
![../../_images/import-3d-assets.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/import-3d-assets.png)
  2. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Trajectories and select Spline Trajectory.
![../../_images/create-spline-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-spline-trajectory.png)
  3. In the Properties set the Spline property to the spline you imported.
  4. To take the trajectory into use, in the Node Tree select a Trajectory Layout or a Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties set the Trajectory property to the trajectory you want to use. See [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html) and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).


## Adjusting a spline created from a NURBS curve[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html#adjusting-a-spline-created-from-a-nurbs-curve "Link to this heading")
When you use a NURBS curve for a spline trajectory you can adjust the number of subdivisions when importing the NURBS curve to Kanzi Studio. Kanzi uses the value you provide to tesselate the NURBS curve as a Kanzi spline. See [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html) and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).
To adjust a spline created from a NURBS curve:
  1. In the Library > Resource Files > 3D Assets select the .fbx file that contains the NURBS curve you are using for a spline trajectory.
  2. In the Properties set the Curve Tesselation Detail property to the number of subdivisions in the NURBS curve you want to use.
The default value is 16. Set the property to different values to find the result that suits you best.
  3. In the Library > Resource Files > 3D Assets right-click the .fbx file that contains the NURBS curve and select Clean Import 3D Asset File.
  4. In the Library > Trajectories select the spline trajectory that uses the NURBS curve you imported and in the Properties set the Spline property to the spline you imported.


##  Spline Trajectory property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html#spline-trajectory-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for spline trajectories, see [Spline Trajectory](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/spline-trajectory-reference.html).

Use a Trapezoid Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a trapezoid in 3D space.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
See [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html) and [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html).
![../../_images/trapezoid-trajectory-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trapezoid-trajectory-in-preview.png)
## Creating a trapezoid trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trapezoid-trajectories.html#creating-a-trapezoid-trajectory "Link to this heading")
To create a trapezoid trajectory:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Trajectories and select Trapezoid Trajectory.
![../../_images/create-trapezoid-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-trapezoid-trajectory.png)
  2. In the Properties set these properties:
     * Normal to set the position of the trajectory in 3D space.
For example:
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the x axis, set X to 1, and Y and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the y axis, set Y to 1, and X and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into I and II, and VII and VIII octants, set X to 1, Y to -1, and the Z property field to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into II and III, and V and VIII octants, set Y and Z to 1, and the X property field to 0.
     * Length to set the length of the base of the trajectory.
     * Back Length to set the length and angle of the non-parallel sides of the trajectory.
     * Depth to set the depth of the trajectory.
     * Smoothness to set the roundness of the angles in the trajectory.
  3. To take the trajectory into use, in the Node Tree select a Trajectory Layout or a Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties set the Trajectory property to the trajectory you want to use. See [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html) and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).


##  Trapezoid Trajectory property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trapezoid-trajectories.html#trapezoid-trajectory-property-types "Link to this heading")

# Using the Trajectory Layout nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#using-the-trajectory-layout-nodes "Link to this heading")

Use the Trajectory Layout nodes to arrange items along a trajectory path.
Kanzi Studio comes with several types of trajectories. When you need a different type of trajectory, create a spline trajectory in a third-party tool and import it to your Kanzi Studio project. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).
![../../_images/trajectory-layout.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout.gif)
## Creating a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#creating-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Trajectory Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Trajectory Layout node and select either Trajectory Layout 3D, or Trajectory Layout 2D.
![../../_images/node-tree-create-trejectory-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-create-trejectory-layout-2d.png)
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
Tip
To see the trajectory, in the Preview click ![image-analyze-off](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to enter the Analyze mode, right-click ![image-analyze-on](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png), and select Debug objects.
![../../_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, add child nodes to the layout that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you created a Trajectory Layout 3D node, add several Sphere nodes. If you created a Trajectory Layout 2D node, add several Image nodes.
![../../_images/node-tree-trajectory-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-trajectory-layout-2d.png)
As you add child nodes, the Trajectory Layout node positions them along the trajectory used by the Trajectory Layout node.
![../../_images/trajectory-layout-element-position.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-element-position.gif)
  3. (Optional)
Kanzi Studio creates and uses a circle trajectory by default. You can use an angle, arc, circle, ellipse, line, rectangle, spiral, spline, or a trapezoid trajectory. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).
![../../_images/trajectory-layout-types.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-types.gif)


## Stretching the trajectory to fill the layout[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#stretching-the-trajectory-to-fill-the-layout "Link to this heading")
By default, the size of the trajectory used by a Trajectory Layout node determines the amount of space that the trajectory occupies in the layout. For example, in a Circle Trajectory, the Radius property determines the size of the trajectory.
To stretch the trajectory to fill the layout:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and enable the Trajectory Layout > Stretch property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-stretch.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-stretch.gif)
## Adjusting the distance between items in a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#adjusting-the-distance-between-items-in-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
A Trajectory Layout node automatically calculates the distance between its child nodes.
To adjust the distance between the child nodes in a Trajectory Layout node:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Trajectory Layout > Override Distance property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-override-distance.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-override-distance.gif)
## Adjusting the position of items in a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#adjusting-the-position-of-items-in-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
By default, a Trajectory Layout node arranges its child nodes from the start of the trajectory spline.
To adjust the starting position of the Trajectory Layout node child nodes on the trajectory:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Trajectory Layout > Start Offset property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-start-offset.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-start-offset.gif)
## Setting the appearance of a Trajectory Layout 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#setting-the-appearance-of-a-trajectory-layout-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png)


## Using the Trajectory Layout node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#using-the-trajectory-layout-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create a Trajectory Layout 3D node:

```
// Create a Trajectory Layout 3D named Trajectory.
TrajectoryLayout3DSharedPtr trajectoryLayout = TrajectoryLayout3D::create(domain, "Trajectory");

```
Copy to clipboard
To create a trajectory and use it in the Trajectory Layout 3D node:

```
// Create a circle trajectory named Circle with radius of 4 device independent units.
// Set the trajectory layout to use it.
TrajectorySharedPtr trajectory = Trajectory::createCircle(Vector3(), Vector3::positiveY(), 0.0f, 4.0f, domain, "Circle");
trajectoryLayout->setTrajectory(trajectory);

```
Copy to clipboard
To add items to the Trajectory Layout 3D node:

```
// Create cube meshes and add them as items of the trajectory layout.
// Items on the trajectory appear in the order you add them to the trajectory layout.
Model3DSharedPtr item1 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item1", 1.0f, ThemeRed);
trajectoryLayout->addChild(item1);
Model3DSharedPtr item2 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item2", 1.0f, ThemeGreen);
trajectoryLayout->addChild(item2);
Model3DSharedPtr item3 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item3", 1.0f, ThemeBlue);
trajectoryLayout->addChild(item3);
Model3DSharedPtr item4 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item4", 1.0f, ThemeOrange);
trajectoryLayout->addChild(item4);
Model3DSharedPtr item5 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item5", 1.0f, ThemeGray);
trajectoryLayout->addChild(item5);

```
Copy to clipboard
To manually position items in the Trajectory Layout 3D node:

```
// Position an item in the middle of the trajectory.
TrajectoryLayout3D::setOverrideOffset(*item2, 0.5f);

// Set the distance between the items to one third of the length of the trajectory.
trajectoryLayout->setOverrideDistance(0.3f);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `TrajectoryLayout3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18894.html)` and `TrajectoryLayout2D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18890.html)` classes.
##  Trajectory Layout property types and messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#trajectory-layout-property-types-and-messages "Link to this heading")
For lists of the available property types and messages for the Trajectory Layout nodes, see [Trajectory Layout 2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/trajectory-layout-2d-reference.html) and [Trajectory Layout 3D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/trajectory-layout-3d-reference.html).

# Triggers[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/triggers.html#triggers "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use triggers and actions to create interactions. Use triggers to set off actions, such as setting a property to a certain value or setting the state of an application.
For example, Kanzi generates messages from user input and these messages are handled by nodes according to specified behavior.
Nodes define most of the message handling behavior, such as scrolling in a List Box node. However, to meet the requirements of your application, you can define additional behavior. For example, a Button node sends a click message when a user clicks that button, but you can define what happens after the sent click message. An example action is that a click triggers an animation that highlights the button that the user clicked.
All Kanzi nodes can send and receive messages and you can intercept these messages with triggers. Some nodes by default receive messages from specific user input events. For example, a Button node by default receives click messages and a Scroll View node by default receives scroll messages.
![../../_images/messages-and-triggers.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/messages-and-triggers.svg)
In Kanzi these concepts relate to defining event-driven logic:
  * **Input and hit testing.** Input is first recognized in a hit testing phase, where all nodes that have Hit Testable property enabled participate. If a pointer event (for example, mouse button down) is performed on top of nodes that participate in hit testing, only the topmost component receives the input. If a node has a manipulator that reacts to the received type of input, it can send messages (for example, a click message). See [Defining which node receives input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#defining-which-node-receives-input), [Using input manipulators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#using-input-manipulators) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
  * **Input manipulators.** An input manipulator reacts to a specific type of input gesture, such as pan, click, or long press. In Kanzi Studio you can use nodes that already contain specific types of manipulators, or you can add input manipulators using the Kanzi Engine API. For example, a Scroll View node contains a pan manipulator and a Button node includes a click manipulator. See [Using input manipulators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#using-input-manipulators).
  * **Messages.** Nodes use messages to communicate. The messages travel between nodes using a process called tunneling and bubbling. The message reaches its target node during tunneling and during bubbling messages travel to ancestor nodes, until a trigger intercepts the message and sets it as handled. This enables you to place triggers in nodes themselves, or their ancestors. For example, you can place a trigger called radioButtonHandler to the parent of multiple buttons. See [Using messages](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-messages.html).
  * **Triggers.** Triggers react to messages, a change in data, or events and apply logic. Kanzi includes the most common action types, such as Set Property or Go to State, but you can use the Kanzi Engine API to define to which messages triggers react. Each trigger includes settings, such as the Set Message Handled property, which prevents the message from bubbling up to other triggers, and conditions which you can use to define conditions under which the trigger sets off. You can add multiple triggers to a single message or event and each can have specific settings and conditions. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html) and [Triggers reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-triggers.html).
  * **Actions.** An action is an outcome of a trigger. Kanzi includes general actions like Set Property, Write Log, Activate Theme, and actions you can use to control a specific type of item such as, Go to State, Set Scroll Target, or Activate Activity. See [Actions and messages reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-actions.html).


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/triggers.html#sa "Link to this heading")
