Use a Write Log action to write a message to the Log window.
![../../_images/log-window.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/log-window.png)
To open the Log window, in the main menu select Window > Log.
Kanzi prints to the Log window messages, warnings, and errors.
## Writing to the Log window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html#writing-to-the-log-window "Link to this heading")
When you want to write a message to the Log window, use a Write Log action in any trigger.
To write to the Log window:
  1. In the Node Tree, create or select a node where you want to react to an event as a result of which you want to write a message to the Log window.
For example, in the Node Tree, create a Scroll View 2D node with content that you can scroll. See [Creating a Scroll View node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scroll-views/using-scroll-views.html#creating-scroll-view-node).
![../../_images/node-tree-scroll-view1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-scroll-view1.png)
  2. In the Node Components, press `Alt` and right-click Triggers and select a trigger that you want to use to write to the Log window when that trigger is set off. See [Triggers reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-triggers.html).
For example, create a Message Trigger > Scroll View > Scroll Ended trigger. Scroll Ended trigger is set off when the scroll position of a scroll view has finished changing.
![../../_images/node-components-create-scroll-ended.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-components-create-scroll-ended.png)
  3. In the Node Components > Triggers, press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you added in the previous step, and select Write Log action.
![../../_images/node-components-write-log-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-components-write-log-action.png)
  4. In the Write Log action, set the Log Text property to the message that you want to write to the Log window when the trigger is set off.
![../../_images/node-components-write-log-action-log-text.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-components-write-log-action-log-text.png)


In the Preview, when you scroll the Scroll View and the scrolling stops, Kanzi prints to the Log window the message that you set in the Log Text property.
![../../_images/log-window-scroll-ended.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/log-window-scroll-ended.png)
Tip
To open the Log window, in the main menu select Window > Log.
## Using Write Log action macros[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html#using-write-log-action-macros "Link to this heading")
Use a Write Log action macro to add to your log message content that Kanzi replaces with the value of that macro.
To use Write Log action macros:
  1. Create a Write Log action. See [Writing to the Log window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html#create-write-log-action).
  2. In the Write Log action, click Enter Operation and select a macro.
For example, instead of manually entering the name of a node, use the <Name> macro.
The <Name> macro inserts the name of the node that contains the Write Log action.
You can combine macros and text.  
| Macro  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| <Name>  | Inserts the name of the node that contains a Write Log action.  |  
| <EventName>  | Inserts the name of the trigger that executes a Write Log action.  |  
| {ValueSourceIndex}  | After you add a property value or a message argument, inserts the value of that item. See [Logging values from properties or message arguments](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html#logging-values-from-properties-or-message-arguments).  |  
![../../_images/node-components-write-log-action-name-macro.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-components-write-log-action-name-macro.png)


In the Preview, when you scroll the Scroll View and the scrolling stops, Kanzi prints to the Log window the message that you set in the Log Text property.
![../../_images/log-window-scroll-ended-macro.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/log-window-scroll-ended-macro.png)
## Logging values from properties or message arguments[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html#logging-values-from-properties-or-message-arguments "Link to this heading")
You can use a Write Log action to write to the Log window values from properties or message arguments.
To log values from properties or message arguments:
  1. Create a Write Log action. See [Writing to the Log window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html#create-write-log-action).
  2. In the Write Log action, click Add Value Source and set the source from which you want to print the value to the Log window.
For example, to print the position of the Scroll View on the x axis, set:
     * Value From to Message argument
     * Message Argument to Position X
![../../_images/write-log-action-formatting-add-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/write-log-action-formatting-add-property.png)
  3. In the Write Log action, click Enter Operation and select {ValueSourceIndex}.
This macro inserts the curly braces (`{}`) that Kanzi replaces with the value that you added in the previous step.
![../../_images/write-log-action-formatting-add-format-string.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/write-log-action-formatting-add-format-string.png)
  4. (Optional) When you refer to the values with empty curly braces (`{}`), Kanzi uses the order in which the values appear in the Write Log action. To set the order of values in a message:
    1. Add another value to the Write Log action.
For example, to print the position of the Scroll View on the y axis, click Add Value Source and set:
       * Value From to Message argument
       * Message Argument to Position Y
![../../_images/write-log-action-set-log-text-with-format-references.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/write-log-action-set-log-text-with-format-references.png)
    2. In the Log Text, add another pair of curly braces, and in the curly braces enter the index of the value that you want to use in that position.
For example, set the Log Text property to:

```
New position. Y axis: {1}, X axis: {0}.

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/node-components-write-log-action-custom-position.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-components-write-log-action-custom-position.png) ![../../_images/log-window-scroll-ended-macro-custom-position.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/log-window-scroll-ended-macro-custom-position.png)
Tip
To change the order of values in a Write Log action, use the arrows next to the value.
![../../_images/write-log-action-move-item-up-down-buttons.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/write-log-action-move-item-up-down-buttons.png)
  5. (Optional). You can apply formatting to the property values. To learn how to format log messages, see [Log message argument format specification](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/logging.html#log-message-argument-format-specification).
For example, set the Log Text property to:

```
New position. Y axis {1:+.2}, X axis {0:+.2}.

```
Copy to clipboard
This way you format the property values to:
     * Always show the sign of the value
     * Set the precision of the value to two digits
![../../_images/node-components-write-log-action-advanced-formatting.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-components-write-log-action-advanced-formatting.png) ![../../_images/log-window-advanced-formatting.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/log-window-advanced-formatting.png)


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Logging](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/logging.html)
[Triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/triggers.html)

# Using version control systems with Kanzi[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html#using-version-control-systems-with-k "Link to this heading")

When you add your Kanzi projects to a version control system, do not add these files and directories:
  * `.kzproj_N`
  * `.proj.kzm_N`
  * `.lock`
  * `.autosave`
  * `.user`
  * `assets`
  * `build_vs2022`
  * `compressed`
  * `cubemaps`
  * `gen`
  * `mipmaps`
  * `output`
  * `lib`
  * `thumbnails`


Note
The `cubemaps` and `mipmaps` directories excluded above hold the generated faces and roughness mipmaps of image-based lighting cubemap textures. Kanzi Studio regenerates them from the source image when they are missing, such as after a fresh clone. Therefore, also add to version control the source hdr or exr image from which you created each image-based lighting cubemap texture. See [Using image-based lighting cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html).
## Merging projects using version control tools[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html#merging-projects-using-version-control-tools "Link to this heading")
After configuring your version control tool you can use the Kanzi merge tool for Kanzi project updating and merging. For the integration Kanzi requires a version control tool that provides the necessary parameters to the Kanzi merge tool.  
| Example of parameter types  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| MINE  | The parameter for the source project.  |  
| THEIRS  | The parameter for the target project.  |  
| BASE  | The parameter for the base project.  |  
| MERGED  | The parameter for the merged project.  |  
## Integrating the Kanzi merge tool with a version control tool[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html#integrating-the-k-merge-tool-with-a-version-control-tool "Link to this heading")
To integrate the Kanzi merge tool with a version control tool:
  1. Configure your version control tool to use the Kanzi merge tool (`<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/KanziMergeTool.bat`) for .kzproj files.
  2. Pass to your version control tool the absolute path to the `KanziStudio.exe`. For example, `C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi\Studio\Bin\KanziStudio.exe`.
  3. Set the version control tool parameters for the Kanzi merge tool. For example, these parameters can be called MINE, THEIRS, BASE, MERGED.


## Integrating the Kanzi merge tool with SVN version control software[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html#integrating-the-k-merge-tool-with-svn-version-control-software "Link to this heading")
To integrate the Kanzi merge tool with SVN version control software, add Kanzi merge tool as an external program for merging files with the .kzproj extension.
For example, if you are using Tortoise SVN, in TortoiseSVN select SVN > Settings > External Programs > Merge Tool > Advanced and set:
  * Filename, extension or mime-type to .kzproj
  * External program to

```
<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/KanziMergeTool.bat "<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/KanziStudio.exe"  %mine %theirs %base %merged

```
Copy to clipboard
For example, if your installation of Kanzi is in `C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi`, use

```
C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi\Studio\Bin\KanziMergeTool.bat "C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi\Studio\Bin\KanziStudio.exe" %mine %theirs %base %merged

```
Copy to clipboard


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html#sa "Link to this heading")

# Using the Viewport 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-2d.html#using-the-viewport-2d-node "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Viewport 2D node can render both a Scene, which is a 3D node, and 2D nodes, such as Image or Button 2D.
When you create a Kanzi Studio project, that project contains a Viewport 2D node with a Scene that contains a Camera and a Directional Light. For Kanzi Engine, the Scene node is always the first child of a Viewport 2D node.
![../../_images/viewport-2d-banner.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/viewport-2d-banner.png)
## Creating a Viewport 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-2d.html#creating-a-viewport-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Viewport 2D node:
  1. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, press `Alt` and right-click a 2D node where you want to create a Viewport 2D node, and select Viewport 2D.
![../../_images/create-viewport-2d1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-viewport-2d1.png)
  2. Add content to the Viewport 2D node that you created.
For example:
    1. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, press `Alt` and right-click the Viewport 2D node and select Scene.
Kanzi Studio creates a Scene node that contains a Camera node and a Directional Light node.
![../../_images/scene-in-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/scene-in-prefabs.png)
    2. In the Scene node, create the 3D nodes that you want to show.
See [3D assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/3d-assets/3d-assets.html).


## Controlling how Kanzi renders a Viewport 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-2d.html#controlling-how-k-renders-a-viewport-2d-node "Link to this heading")
You can control how Kanzi renders a Viewport 2D node. Kanzi renders the background brush before the content of the Viewport 2D node by default.
To control how Kanzi renders a Viewport 2D node, set the Foreground Hint property to:
  * None to render the background brush after rendering the Viewport 2D node. Use it when the content of the Viewport 2D node is opaque.
  * Translucent to render the background brush before the content of the Viewport 2D node. This is the default value. Use it when the content in the Viewport 2D node is alpha-blended.
  * Occluding to not render the background brush. Use it when the entire Viewport 2D node is filled with 3D content.

![../../_images/foreground-hint.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/foreground-hint.png)
## Using the Viewport 2D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-2d.html#using-the-viewport-2d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create a Viewport 2D node:

```
// Create a Viewport 2D named Viewport 2D and add it to the RootPage.
Viewport2DSharedPtr viewport2d = Viewport2D::create(domain, "Viewport 2D");
rootNode->addChild(viewport2d);

// To render 3D nodes in a Viewport 2D you need to add a Scene to the Viewport 2D.
// Create a Scene named Scene for 3D nodes and add it to the Viewport 2D.
SceneSharedPtr sceneNode = Scene::create(domain, "Scene for 3D nodes");
viewport2d->setScene(sceneNode);

// Create a Camera named Camera and add it to the Scene.
CameraSharedPtr camera = Camera::create(domain, "Camera");
sceneNode->addChild(camera);

// Create a Point Light named Point light and add it to the Scene.
LightSharedPtr light = Light::createPoint(domain, "Point light");
sceneNode->addChild(light);

// Create a Box mesh named Box and add it to the Scene.
Model3DSharedPtr box = Model3D::createCube(domain, "Box", 1.0f, ThemeBlue);
sceneNode->addChild(box);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `Viewport2D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13906.html)` class.
##  Viewport 2D property types and messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-2d.html#viewport-2d-property-types-and-messages "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types and messages for the Viewport 2D node, see [Viewport 2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/viewport-2d-reference.html).

# Using the Viewport 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-3d.html#using-the-viewport-3d-node "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Viewport 3D node to add 2D nodes to a 3D scene.
![../../_images/viewport-3d-banner.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/viewport-3d-banner.png)
## Creating a Viewport 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-3d.html#creating-a-viewport-3d-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Viewport 3D node:
  1. In the Prefabs, create a 2D prefab whose content you want to add to a 3D scene.
![../../_images/prefabs-my-2d-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefabs-my-2d-prefab.png)
  2. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, press `Alt` and right-click a 3D node to which you want to add 2D nodes, and select Viewport 3D.
![../../_images/create-viewport-3d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-viewport-3d.png)
  3. Select the Viewport 3D node. In the Properties, add the Prefab Template property and set it to the 2D prefab that you created.
Kanzi first renders the content of the prefab to a texture, and then renders that texture on a 3D plane using an unlit alpha-blended textured material.
![../../_images/properties-viewport-3d-prefab-template.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-viewport-3d-prefab-template.png)
  4. (Optional) To set the material that you want to use to render the content of the 2D prefab, in the Properties:
    1. Add the Override Material property and set it to a textured material that you want to use to render the content of the 2D prefab. See [Using materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-materials.html) and [Creating textured materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/creating-textured-materials.html).
![../../_images/properties-viewport-3d-override-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-viewport-3d-override-material.png)
    2. Click + Add Binding and in Binding Editor, set:
       * Property to a texture property of the material that you set in the Override Material property.
       * Expression to

```
{@./Viewport3D.PrefabTexture}

```
Copy to clipboard
Click Save.
This way you set the override material to render the texture to which Kanzi renders the content of the 2D prefab.
![../../_images/viewport-3d-texture-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/viewport-3d-texture-binding.png)


## Adding a 2D UI control to a 3D scene[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-3d.html#adding-a-2d-ui-control-to-a-3d-scene "Link to this heading")
To add a 2D UI control to a 3D scene:
  1. In the Prefabs, create a 2D prefab that contains the 2D nodes that you want to add to a 3D scene.
For example, create a color picker with a slider. See [Creating a color picker with a slider](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/sliders/using-sliders.html#creating-a-color-picker-with-a-slider).
![../../_images/prefabs-color-picker.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefabs-color-picker.png) ![../../_images/preview-color-wheel-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-color-wheel-prefab.png)
  2. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, create a 3D scene to which you want to add 2D nodes.
For example, use the Car from the Factory Content.
See [Using the Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html).
![../../_images/preview-fc-car.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-fc-car.png)
  3. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, press `Alt` and right-click the 3D node to which you want to add 2D nodes and select Viewport 3D.
For example, create a Viewport 3D node in the Prefabs > CarScene > RootNode node.
![../../_images/prefabs-create-viewport-3d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefabs-create-viewport-3d.png) ![../../_images/prefabs-viewport-3d-color-picker.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefabs-viewport-3d-color-picker.png)
  4. Select the Viewport 3D node and in the Properties, add and set:
     * Prefab Template property to the 2D prefab whose content you want to add to the 3D scene.
For example, select the Color Picker prefab.
Kanzi first renders the content of the prefab to a texture, and then renders that texture on a 3D plane.
     * Render Transformation or Layout Transformation to position and orient the 2D prefab in the 3D scene.
For example, add the Render Transformation property and set:
       * Rotation X property field to -90
       * Rotation Y property field to 90
       * Translation Y property field to 0.1
This way you position the 2D prefab just above the floor under the car.
![../../_images/properties-prefab-template-and-transform.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-prefab-template-and-transform.png) ![../../_images/preview-color-picker-initial.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-color-picker-initial.png)
  5. To set the size of the 2D content in the 3D scene, in the Properties, add and set:
     * 2D to 3D Projection Scale to the scaling factor that you want to use to project the 2D content to the 3D space.
For example, if the width of your 2D prefab is 710 pixels and you set the 2D to 3D Projection Scale property to 0.08, the width of that prefab in 3D space is 56.8 units.
     * (Optional) Layout Width and Layout Height
For example, set these properties when you do not set the layout size of the prefab and it stretches to the size of its parent node.
![../../_images/properties-prefab-projection-scale-layout-size.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-prefab-projection-scale-layout-size.png) ![../../_images/preview-color-picker-scaled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-color-picker-scaled.png)
  6. Kanzi by default uses an unlit alpha-blended textured material to render the content in a Viewport 3D node.
To set the material that you want to use to render the content, in the Properties:
    1. Add the Override Material property and set it to any textured material.
For example, set it to the VertexPhongTexturedMaterial material. This material uses lights.
Tip
If your project does not contain the VertexPhongTextured material type, in the Library > Materials and Textures press `Alt` and right-click Material Types, and select VertexPhongTextured.
![../../_images/properties-override-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-override-material.png)
    2. Click + Add Binding and in Binding Editor, set:
       * Property to a texture property of the material that you set in the Override Material property.
       * Expression to

```
{@./Viewport3D.PrefabTexture}

```
Copy to clipboard
Click Save.
This way you set the override material to render the texture to which Kanzi renders the content of the 2D prefab.
![../../_images/binding-viewport-3d-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-viewport-3d-texture.png)
    3. Adjust the properties of the material that you set in the Override Material property.
For example, add and set:
       * Material > Diffuse Color property Lightness (L) property field to 255
       * Material > Blend Mode to Alpha: Premultiplied
![../../_images/properties-viewport-3d-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-viewport-3d-material.png)
When you turn off the lights in the scene, Kanzi renders the color picker with darker colors.
![../../_images/preview-toggle-lights.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-toggle-lights.gif)
  7. To access the properties of the 2D prefab that the Viewport 3D node renders, use bindings.
For example, if your color picker prefab has a property that holds the selected color, to paint the body of a car model with that color:
    1. Select the 3D node that renders the body of the car. In the Properties, add a binding and set:
       * Property to Diffuse Color
This property sets the color of a material when that material is lit.
       * Expression to point the property that contains the currently selected color in the color picker.
For example, set it to

```
{../../Color Picker Viewport/Color Picker/ColorPicker.Color}

```
Copy to clipboard
Click Save.
![../../_images/prefabs-car-body.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefabs-car-body.png) ![../../_images/binding-car-body-diffuse-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-car-body-diffuse-color.png)
    2. Repeat the previous step for the Ambient Color property, which sets the color of a material when no lights are present.
For example, set the binding expression to

```
{../../Color Picker Viewport/Color Picker/ColorPicker.Color} * Color4(0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 1)

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/binding-car-body-ambient-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-car-body-ambient-color.png)
In the Preview, when you use the color picker to select a color, the paint of the car changes to use that color.
![../../_images/preview-viewport-3d-complete.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-viewport-3d-complete.gif)


## Using the Viewport 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-3d.html#using-the-viewport-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To use a Viewport 3D node, create a 2D prefab and set the Viewport 3D node to render that prefab in a 3D scene:

```
// Create a Viewport 3D named Viewport 3D and add it to the Scene.
Viewport3DSharedPtr viewport3d = Viewport3D::create(domain, "Viewport 3D");
scene->addChild(viewport3d);

// Create an image that acts as a model for the prefab template.
// This can be any Node2D node or a tree of Node2D nodes.
Image2DSharedPtr image = Image2D::create(domain, "Image");

// Create a prefab template node based on the image.
PrefabTemplateNodeSharedPtr templateNode = PrefabTemplateNode::create(domain, Image2D::getStaticMetaclass(), "Prefab root node");

// Create a prefab template and set the prefab template node as its root.
PrefabTemplateSharedPtr prefabTemplate = PrefabTemplate::create(domain, templateNode, "PrefabForViewport3D");

// Use the prefab template in the Viewport3D node.
viewport3d->setPrefab(prefabTemplate);

```
Copy to clipboard
To bind from a node that is outside a Viewport 3D node, to a node that is in the 2D prefab used by the Viewport 3D node:

```
// Create a prefab template node from a 2D scene graph.
PrefabTemplateNodeSharedPtr templateNode = PrefabTemplateNode::create(domain, EmptyNode2D::getStaticMetaclass(), "Empty Node 2D");
templateNode->addProperty(Node::WidthProperty, Variant(320.0f));
templateNode->addProperty(Node::HeightProperty, Variant(240.0f));
templateNode->addProperty(Node::OpacityProperty, Variant(0.8f));

// Create a prefab template and set the prefab template node as its root.
PrefabTemplateSharedPtr viewport3DPrefab = PrefabTemplate::create(domain, templateNode, "Empty Node 2D");

// Create a Viewport3D node and add it to the Scene.
Viewport3DSharedPtr viewport3D = Viewport3D::create(domain, "Viewport 3D");
scene->addChild(viewport3D);

// Set the Viewport3D node to use the prefab template.
viewport3D->setPrefab(viewport3DPrefab);

// Create a node that is a sibling of the Viewport3D node.
EmptyNode3DSharedPtr sibling = EmptyNode3D::create(domain, "Sibling");
scene->addChild(sibling);

// In the sibling node, add a binding that binds a property in the sibling node to a property
// in a node in the 2D scene graph that the Viewport3D node shows. Use a relative path to refer
// to the scene graph that Kanzi instantiates in the Viewport 3D node.
sibling->setBinding(Binding::create("../Viewport 3D/Empty Node 2D", Node::OpacityProperty),
                    StandardMaterial::BlendIntensityProperty);

```
Copy to clipboard
To bind from a node that is in the 2D prefab used by a Viewport 3D node, to a node that is outside the Viewport 3D node:

```
// Create a Viewport3D node and add it to the Scene.
Viewport3DSharedPtr viewport3D = Viewport3D::create(domain, "Viewport 3D");
scene->addChild(viewport3D);

// Create a node that is a sibling of the Viewport3D node.
EmptyNode3DSharedPtr sibling = EmptyNode3D::create(domain, "Sibling");
sibling->setProperty(StandardMaterial::BlendIntensityProperty, 0.6f);
scene->addChild(sibling);

// Create a prefab template node from a 2D scene graph.
PrefabTemplateNodeSharedPtr templateNode = PrefabTemplateNode::create(domain, EmptyNode2D::getStaticMetaclass(), "Empty Node 2D");
templateNode->addProperty(Node::WidthProperty, Variant(320.0f));
templateNode->addProperty(Node::HeightProperty, Variant(240.0f));

// In the prefab template node, add a binding that binds a property in the prefab to a property
// in the sibling node of the Viewport3D node.
templateNode->addBinding(BindingLoadInfo(Binding::create("../../Sibling", StandardMaterial::BlendIntensityProperty),
                                         Node::OpacityProperty));

// Create a prefab template and set the prefab template node as its root.
PrefabTemplateSharedPtr viewport3DPrefab = PrefabTemplate::create(domain, templateNode, "Empty Node 2D");

// Set the Viewport3D node to use the prefab template.
viewport3D->setPrefab(viewport3DPrefab);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `Viewport3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13910.html)` class.
##  Viewport 3D property types and messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-3d.html#viewport-3d-property-types-and-messages "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types and messages for the Viewport 3D node, see [Viewport 3D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/viewport-3d-reference.html).
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-3d.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Viewport nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/using-viewports.html)
[Using the Viewport 2D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/viewport-2d.html)
[Using the Scene node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scenes/scenes.html)
[Using node prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html)
[Material types and materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/materials.html)
[Creating textured materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/creating-textured-materials.html)
[Using the Slider nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/sliders/using-sliders.html)
[Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html)

# Customizing the Kanzi Studio interface[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/workspaces/customizing-your-workspace.html#customizing-the-ks-interface "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
You can customize the Kanzi Studio interface. You can open new, rearrange, dock, and close windows to make the environment that best suits your needs.
To restore the workspace to the default state, in the main menu select Window > Reset Workspace.
![../../_images/reset-workspace.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reset-workspace.png)
This is how Kanzi Studio looks when you create a new project.
![../../_images/interface-overview.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/interface-overview.svg)
## Opening windows[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/workspaces/customizing-your-workspace.html#opening-windows "Link to this heading")
To open a new window select Window and select the window that you want to open:
  * Use the Activity Browser to create and inspect Activities and Activity Hosts, and to simulate the activation of Activities. The Activity Browser shows all possible UI states of Activities in your application.
See [Using the Activity Browser](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/activity-browser.html).
  * Animations shows animation data, animation clips, timeline sequences, and timeline entries in your project. See [Animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/animations.html).
  * Asset Packages shows collections of ready-made content that you can import to your Kanzi Studio project. See [Asset packages](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-packages/asset-packages.html).
  * Assets shows the 2D and 3D content, materials, and prefabs in your project.
  * Bookmarks shows the shortcuts in your project. See [Using bookmarks](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html).
  * Data Sources shows the data sources in your project. See [Data sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/data-sources.html).
  * Dictionaries shows the resource IDs of the resources that are local to the node that you select in the Node Tree.
See [Resources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/resources.html).
  * Library shows all the resources in your project. Here you can find, create, and edit all the materials, textures, animations, trajectories, composers, and other resources in your project. You can open a separate dockable window for each resource type. See [Resources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/resources.html).
  * Log shows the status of your project such as messages triggered in your project, but also warning and error messages.
  * Materials and Textures shows brushes, materials, material types, shader formats, and textures in your project. See [Using brushes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html), [Material types and materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/materials.html), [Using binary shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/shaders/using-binary-shaders.html), and [Textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html).
  * Meshes shows the mesh data in your project. See [Using meshes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/meshes.html).
  * Node Components shows the components, such as triggers, animation players, and input manipulators, for the node selected in the Node Tree. See [Node components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/node-components/node-components.html).
  * Node Tree shows all nodes in your project that Kanzi loads at application startup. This is where you create and organize the content of your project.
  * Pages shows the pages tool where you can create and manage the structure of your application. See [Using the Page and Page Host nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/pages/using-pages.html).
  * Prefabs shows the prefabs in your project. See [Using node prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html).
  * Preview shows your project the way it appears to your users. The Preview window has these modes:
    * In the Analyze mode you can analyze the performance and inner structure of your application. See [Analyzing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html).
    * In the Edit mode you can use the Preview window to edit the content in your project. Select any of the Preview window tools ![preview-node-tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png) ![grid-tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout-2d-tool.png) ![text-tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-tool.png) ![image3](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-2d-tool.png) ![image4](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-2d-tool.png) ![image5](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera-tool.png) to enter the Edit mode.
See [Editing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html).
    * In the Interact mode, you can interact with your application in the Preview window as you would on a device. When you are using a Preview tool, to switch to the Interact mode, in the Preview window click ![interact](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/interact.png).
  * Prism Editor shows the Prism Editor where you can create and edit Prism effects. See [Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html).
  * Properties shows the properties for the item selected in the Node Tree or Library. When you add, remove, or edit the properties, you edit the look and behavior of the selected item.
  * Property Types shows the custom property types in your project. See [Property types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/property-types.html).
  * Rendering shows the object sources, render passes, and filters in your project. See [Using object sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/object-sources/using-object-sources.html), [Rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html), and [Filters](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/filters.html).
  * Resource Files shows the resource files in your project grouped by file type. See [Using resource files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resource-files/resource-files.html).
  * State Managers shows the state managers in your project. See [State manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/state-managers.html).
  * State Tools shows the tools you can use to create, set, and manage states in your application. See [State manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/state-managers.html).
  * Textures shows the textures in your project. See [Textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html).
  * Trajectories shows the trajectories in your project. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).


Tip
To expand or collapse all elements under an item in any tree view, click the expander ![expander](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/expander.png) while holding down `Ctrl`.
## Rearranging windows in your workspace[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/workspaces/customizing-your-workspace.html#rearranging-windows-in-your-workspace "Link to this heading")
You can rearrange your workspace by docking, undocking, opening and closing windows.
To undock click the header of the window and drag it either to a new location in the guide diamond, or drop it to keep the window floating.
To close a window, click the X in the header of the window you want to close.
To dock a window:
  1. Click the header of the window you want to dock.
A guide diamond appears in the center of the area where the window is.
![../../_images/click-header-of-a-window.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-header-of-a-window.png)
  2. Drag the window over the area where you want to dock it, and move it over the corresponding portion of the guide diamond.
The area where the window docks becomes shaded.
![../../_images/shaded-area.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shaded-area.png)
  3. Release the mouse button to dock the window in the indicated position.
![../../_images/docked-window.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/docked-window.png)


## Adding any window as a tab to another window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/workspaces/customizing-your-workspace.html#adding-any-window-as-a-tab-to-another-window "Link to this heading")
You can add any window as a tab to any other window to see more than one type of content in the same window.
To add any window as a tab to another window:
  1. Click and drag the header of the window over the window where you want to add it as a tab, and move it over the central part of the guide diamond.
![../../_images/docking-as-tab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/docking-as-tab.png)
  2. Release the mouse button to add the window as a tab.
![../../_images/docked-tab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/docked-tab.png)


## Ordering property categories in the Properties window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/workspaces/customizing-your-workspace.html#ordering-property-categories-in-the-properties-window "Link to this heading")
To set the order of property categories in the Properties window, select Edit > User Preferences, in the Properties tab in the Property Category dropdown select a property category, and set the position of the property category.
For example, you can set the Transform 2D and your own My Property Category categories to be shown after the Description category.
Note
The General and Description property categories are always shown on the top.
![../../_images/user-preferences-property-category-order.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/user-preferences-property-category-order.png) ![../../_images/properties-property-category-order.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-property-category-order.png)

# Best practices[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/best-practices.html#best-practices "Link to this heading")

When creating applications for embedded and mobile devices, even seemingly small details can have significant impact on the performance of your Kanzi application on target devices. Kanzi graphics pipeline is optimized to allow 60 frames per second for 3D instrument clusters and human-machine interfaces. Use the best practices covered in this section of documentation to create optimal Kanzi applications for your target hardware.
Even though Kanzi provides many ways that enable you to create applications that consume less memory, CPU and GPU capacity, and device battery, how you create your application has a large impact on its efficiency.
## Thread safety[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/best-practices.html#thread-safety "Link to this heading")
Kanzi is thread-agnostic and does not guarantee thread safety. To make your Kanzi application code thread-safe:
  * Do not call Kanzi functions from custom threads unless the API documentation specifies that you can call the function from any thread.
  * Synchronize between threads all access to shared data.


## Pay attention to the log messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/best-practices.html#pay-attention-to-the-log-messages "Link to this heading")
Kanzi prints warnings and errors to the Kanzi Studio Log window and the Kanzi debug console to help you find the problems and bottlenecks in your Kanzi application. Pay careful attention to these messages. To ensure that your Kanzi application works correctly and performs optimally on your target platform, resolve all the issues shown in the warnings and errors. Even seemingly unimportant warnings can have a significant impact on the loading times and performance of your Kanzi application. For example, see [Adjusting the data size](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/adjusting-the-data-size.html).
## Use the Kanzi Command Prompt[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/best-practices.html#use-the-kanzi-command-prompt "Link to this heading")
The Kanzi Command Prompt opens the Windows Command Prompt with the Kanzi environment variables set for the version of Kanzi for which you open a Kanzi Command Prompt.
Use the Kanzi Command Prompt to access Kanzi utilities and build tools, such as Gradle and CMake, without using absolute paths or setting environment variables.
See [Using the Kanzi Command Prompt](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/using-kanzi-command-prompt.html).
## Kanzi best practices[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/best-practices.html#k-best-practices "Link to this heading")

# Adjusting the data size[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/adjusting-the-data-size.html#adjusting-the-data-size "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
When you use the correct data sizes for images, textures and shaders you reduce the memory requirements. Adjust the data size to reflect the requirements of your application:
  * If the screen resolution of the target devices is low, make sure the texels of the texture match the pixels of the target screen. For example, when you have a 50 by 40 pixels textured button on a screen 320 by 200 pixels, the optimal size of the texture that returns the best quality is a 50 by 40 pixels texture. You can combine image downscaling with image compression. Try to find a compromise between required visual quality and application performance. See [Compressing textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html).
  * You have to have a really good reason to use textures larger than 1024 pixels. If texture is 1024 pixels wide or high and contains a repeating pattern, extract the smallest repeating pattern and in the texture set the Wrap Mode to Repeat.
![../../_images/wrap-mode-repeat.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/wrap-mode-repeat.png)
  * The memory required by a texture corresponds directly to the texture format you use. For example, an 8-bit grayscale texture requires 8 bits for each pixel, whereas RGBA8 requires four 8-bit channels (32 bits for each pixel).
  * Make sure that all faces of a cubemap texture use images of the same size and format. When the size and format of the images in a cubemap texture do not match, Kanzi uses the default cubemap texture.
For example, for all faces of a cubemap texture use images that are 256 by 256 pixels large and are 8-bit grayscale.
When the size and format of the images in a cubemap texture do not match, Kanzi Studio uses red type to mark such textures.
![../../_images/cubemap-texture-faces-not-same-size.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cubemap-texture-faces-not-same-size.png)
  * Use mipmaps to create a set of downscaled sublevels from a large texture. Mipmaps increase the GPU memory use by one third, but improve the performance when the full texture does not have to be sampled. Use mipmaps to improve the performance whenever you scale a textured node.
See [Using mipmaps](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html).


Avoid creating textures from very large images. For example, do not create textures directly from digital camera pictures. Instead create textures from preprocessed and properly detailed graphics. - Make sure that the tools you use for creating and converting images create images of the smallest possible size. For example, if you are using PNG images, use tools like [pngcheck](http://www.libpng.org/pub/png/apps/pngcheck.html) and [Pngcrush](http://pmt.sourceforge.net/pngcrush/) to ensure that the images are of the correct type and do not contain any unnecessary data.

# Compressing textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html#compressing-textures "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
In Kanzi, you can use the ASTC and ETC algorithms for compressing textures, as well as precompressed DXT textures. Kanzi also supports Basis Universal, a supercompressed LDR/HDR GPU texture interchange system.
If your application tries to read more data from the memory than the memory can handle, reading the memory becomes a performance bottleneck for your application. If your target hardware supports any of these compression methods, use texture compression to reduce the memory bandwidth and improve the performance of your application. You can achieve the relatively smallest file size and the best image quality with the modern ASTC algorithm.
The best performing compression level depends on your target device. High compression levels use more CPU but less memory bandwidth, whereas low compression levels use less CPU but more memory bandwidth.
Kanzi applications send compressed textures directly to the GPU, reducing the amount of interchanged data and without requiring preprocessing on the CPU side at runtime (for example, loading libJPEG or libPNG).
For example, an unpacked 256 by 256 pixel RGB texture uses 196 kb (256 * 256 * 3 bytes). When compressed:
  * With ASTC that texture uses 16 kb (((256/8)^2)*16)/1024 with a block size of 8 by 8. With a block size of 12 by 12, the texture uses 8 kb.
  * With ETC that texture uses 32 kb (256 * 256 / 2).

![../../_images/compressing-textures.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/compressing-textures.svg)
If your target hardware does not support any of these compression algorithms, in some cases raw image format can be faster than any compression algorithm. This is particularly true when processing single small images.
If your target hardware does not support the selected texture compression algorithm, when you run your Kanzi application on your target device, Kanzi prints a warning message to the log. Kanzi paints black the surfaces where you use compressed texture formats that your target hardware does not support.
Because OpenGL expects DXT texture data to have the bottom row first, compress DXT files vertically flipped. Note that you can use the DXT files in your Kanzi application, but the DXT files are not supported in the windows emulation because of GPU limitations. See [Importing images](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-images.html).
Kanzi Studio compresses the images when you create the kzb file, but you can also compress them manually. See [Preprocessing images manually](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html#preproce).
Tip
When Kanzi Studio compresses images it by default uses all available CPU resources of your computer. To free up CPU resources for other applications while Kanzi Studio compresses multiple images, select Edit > User Preferences and in the Properties tab adjust the value of the Images to compress in parallel setting.
The Images to compress in parallel setting limits the number of logical cores Kanzi Studio uses when preprocessing multiple images. The number of logical cores in your computer determines the Maximum value.
![../../_images/images-to-compress-in-parallel.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/images-to-compress-in-parallel.png)
## Using the ASTC algorithm[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html#using-the-astc-algorithm "Link to this heading")
If your target hardware supports ASTC algorithm, use the ASTC algorithm for the best results. The ASTC algorithm creates smaller files and results in better image quality than the ETC algorithm.
To use the ASTC algorithm:
  1. In Kanzi Studio in the Library select Resource Files > Images, and select the image for which you want to apply compression.
  2. In the Properties set the Target Format property to ASTC.
![../../_images/target-format-astc-compression.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-format-astc-compression.png)
  3. In the Properties set:
     * ASTC Profile to select a compression color profile.
LDR linear, LDR sRGB, HDR + LDA A, and HDRA refer to the compression color profile:
       * LDR linear uses the linear LDR color profile.
       * LDR sRGB uses the sRGB LDR color profile.
       * HDR + LDR A uses the HDR color profile, tuned for HDR RGB with LDR alpha.
       * HDRA uses the HDR color profile, tuned for HDR RGBA.
![../../_images/astc-color-profile.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/astc-color-profile.png)
     * ASTC Block Size to the block size in pixels you want to use for compressing the image.
In ASTC the size of one compressed block is always 128 bits. Fewer pixels in a block result in better image quality of the compressed image, but create larger files. 4x4 pixels per block is the largest and best looking supported value, whereas 12x12 pixels per block creates the smallest file size output.
![../../_images/astc-block-size.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/astc-block-size.png)
     * ASTC Compression Speed to the amount of time it takes to compress an image.
Very fast, Fast, Medium, Thorough, and Exhaustive refer to the amount of time it takes to compress an image and image quality, not the file size of compressed image or decompression time:
       * Very fast takes the least amount of time to compress an image.
       * Exhaustive takes the most amount of time to compress an image and results in the best quality.
Use fast compressions for fast and good results and slower compressions for better quality.
For example, for the best final result use Exhaustive. During development Very fast is the most useful.
![../../_images/astc-compression-speed.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/astc-compression-speed.png)


## Using the ETC algorithm[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html#using-the-etc-algorithm "Link to this heading")
To use the ETC algorithm:
  1. In Kanzi Studio in the Library select Resource Files > Images, and select the image for which you want to apply compression.
  2. In the Properties set the Target Format property to the ETC compression you want to use:
     * ETC **fast** , **medium** , and **slow** refer to the speed of image compression and image quality, not the resulting size or decompression time. **Slow** returns the best image quality.
For the best final result with the ETC1 compression scheme use ETC **slow perceptual**.
     * ETC **Perceptual** refers to the emphasis of the green color channel over the red and blue color channels, based on the human visual system color affinity.
When using ETC1 compression scheme during development ETC **fast** is the most useful.
     * ETC2 to use the ETC2 compression scheme.
To set the quality of ETC2 compression use the Effort property.
The value of Effort corresponds to the compression time and image quality, not to the resulting size or decompression time. For the best image quality result set Effort to 100. During development 0 is the most useful because it gives the shortest compression time.
     * ETC2 with alpha to use the ETC2 compression scheme for images with alpha channel.
![../../_images/target-format-etc-compression.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-format-etc-compression.png) ![../../_images/etc2-compression-effort.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/etc2-compression-effort.png)


## Using the Basis Universal algorithm[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html#using-the-basis-universal-algorithm "Link to this heading")
To use the Basis Universal algorithm:
  1. In Kanzi Studio in the Library select Resource Files > Images, and select the image for which you want to apply compression.
  2. In the Properties set the Target Format property to Basis Universal.
  3. In the Properties set:
     * Basis Universal Texture Mode to select a texture mode.
UASTC LDR, UASTC HDR 4x4, UASTC HDR 6x6, and ETC1S refer to the texture mode:
       * UASTC LDR uses custom ASTC 4x4-like format designed for very fast transcoding to other LDR texture formats, high quality.
       * UASTC HDR 4x4 uses standard ASTC HDR 4x4 texture data, but constrained for very fast transcoding to BC6H.
       * UASTC HDR 6x6 uses standard ASTC HDR 6x6.
       * ETC1S uses a supercompressed subset of ETC1 designed for very fast transcoding to other LDR texture formats, low/medium quality but high compression.
     * UASTC Encoding Level to select UASTC 4x4 compression level.
![../../_images/uastc-encoding-level.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/uastc-encoding-level.png)
     * ETC1S Encoding Level to select ETC1S compression level.
![../../_images/etc1s-encoding-level.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/etc1s-encoding-level.png)


## Preprocessing images manually[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html#preprocessing-images-manually "Link to this heading")
Kanzi Studio compresses the images when you create the kzb file, but you can also compress them manually. To manually preprocess images, in the Library > Resource Files > Images right-click one or more images you want to preprocess, and select Preprocess images.
![../../_images/preprocess-images.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preprocess-images.png)
Tip
When Kanzi Studio compresses images it by default uses all available CPU resources of your computer. To free up CPU resources for other applications while Kanzi Studio compresses multiple images, select Edit > User Preferences and in the Properties tab adjust the value of the Images to compress in parallel setting.
The Images to compress in parallel setting limits the number of logical cores Kanzi Studio uses when preprocessing multiple images. The number of logical cores in your computer determines the Maximum value.
![../../_images/images-to-compress-in-parallel.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/images-to-compress-in-parallel.png)

# Using mipmaps[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html#using-mipmaps "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use mipmaps to create a set of downscaled sublevels from a large texture. Mipmaps increase the GPU memory use by one third, but improve the performance when the full texture does not have to be sampled. Use mipmaps to improve the performance whenever you scale a textured node.
For example, a 256 by 256 pixels texture has mipmap levels that reduce the texture to 128 by 128, 64 by 64, and so on until 1 by 1 pixel. The performance improves because smaller mipmap levels fit better in the fixed-size texture cache in the GPU.
When you create mipmaps in a third-party tool and include them in a .dds file, Kanzi Studio extracts the images for mipmap levels and uses them.
Avoid creating mipmaps from .jpeg textures, because the .jpeg image format causes the quality of the mipmaps to degrade.
## Generating mipmaps for a texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html#generating-mipmaps-for-a-texture "Link to this heading")
When you import an image that does not contain mipmaps, you can generate the mipmaps for the texture from that image in Kanzi Studio.
To generate mipmaps for a texture:
  1. In the Library > Resource Files > Images, select the image for which you want to create mipmaps.
Avoid creating mipmaps from .jpeg textures, because the .jpeg image format causes the quality of the mipmaps to degrade.
  2. In the Properties, enable the Generate Mipmaps property.
![../../_images/generate-mipmaps.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/generate-mipmaps.png)
  3. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Textures, select the texture that uses the image for which you want to generate mipmaps. In the Properties, set the Mipmap Mode property to Linear or Nearest to take the mipmaps into use. See [Filtering textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/filtering-textures.html).
![../../_images/mipmap-mode-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mipmap-mode-property.png)
  4. When you export the kzb file of your project and Kanzi Studio asks whether you want to preprocess the images, click Yes. If you do not preprocess images in Kanzi Studio, Kanzi Engine generates mipmaps when it loads your application on the target device. This increases the loading time of your application.
Note
Kanzi cannot generate mipmaps for images that use ASTC or ETC compression.
Tip
To manually generate mipmaps for images, in the Library right-click the image for which you want to generate mipmaps and select Preprocess images.
![../../_images/preprocess-images.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preprocess-images.png)


## Creating mipmaps for composition targets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html#creating-mipmaps-for-composition-targets "Link to this heading")
You can create mipmaps for composition targets when you render 3D content with a Composition Target render pass or Cubemap render pass. For example, use this to create a low-quality blur effect that is quick to render.
This procedure explains how to create mipmaps for the composition targets that Kanzi creates automatically. To create mipmaps for a Render Target Texture, see [Creating mipmaps for a Render Target Texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html#creating-mipmaps-for-render-target-texture).
To create mipmaps for composition targets:
  1. Create the render passes that you need to render your content to one or more composition targets.
For example, in the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs, create a Compose and Blit Pass. See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html).
![../../_images/compose-and-blit-pass-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/compose-and-blit-pass-library.png)
  2. In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs, select the Composition Target render pass or Cubemap render pass for whose composition targets you want to create mipmaps. In the Properties, add the Mipmap Mode property, and set it either to Linear or Nearest. See [Filtering textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/filtering-textures.html).
![../../_images/composition-target-mipmap-mode.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/composition-target-mipmap-mode.png)
  3. (Optional) To customize how Kanzi creates the mipmaps, you can set a mipmap filtering material for each composition target.
Kanzi Studio comes with a set of mipmap filtering materials that you can use.
To set the mipmap filtering materials:
    1. Set your render pass to use the mipmap filtering materials:
       * For a Cubemap render pass, add and set the Mipmap Generation > Cubemap Mipmap Material property to the material that you want to use.
For example, set it to the DefaultCubemapMipmapFilterMaterial. If your project does not contain this material, in the Library > Materials and Textures press `Alt` and right-click Material Types, and select DefaultCubemapMipmapFilter.
![../../_images/cubemap-mipmap-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cubemap-mipmap-material.png)
       * For a Composition Target render pass, add and set one or more of these Mipmap Generation properties:
         * Color Mipmap Material 0, Color Mipmap Material 1, Color Mipmap Material 2, and Color Mipmap Material 3 to set the mipmap filter materials for the color composition targets.
For example, to set the material for Composition Target 0, add and set the Color Mipmap Material 0 property to DefaultMipmapFilterMaterial. If your project does not contain this material, in the Library > Materials and Textures press `Alt` and right-click Material Types, and select DefaultMipmapFilter.
         * Depth Mipmap Material to the material that you want to use for the depth attachment of the first composition target.
For example, set it to the DefaultDepthMipmapFilterMaterial. If your project does not contain this material, in the Library > Materials and Textures press `Alt` and right-click Material Types, and select DefaultDepthMipmapFilter.
![../../_images/composition-target-mipmap-materials.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/composition-target-mipmap-materials.png)
The default mipmap filtering materials can use these properties as inputs to their shaders:
     * Current Mipmap Level reports the mipmap level that is being rendered.
     * Mipmap Source Texture reports the texture that contains the render target texture for which the mipmap is created. The shader must sample only from mipmap levels that are less than the Current Mipmap Level.
  4. (Optional) By default, Kanzi generates the mipmaps when the Composition Target render pass or Cubemap render pass creates the composition target. When you continue rendering to the same composition target in another render pass, creating the mipmaps immediately is likely to waste GPU time. To avoid this, in the render that creates the composition target, add and disable the Composition Target render pass > Resolve Immediately or Cubemap render pass > Resolve Immediately property.
![../../_images/resolve-immediately-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resolve-immediately-disabled.png)


## Creating mipmaps for a Render Target Texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html#creating-mipmaps-for-a-render-target-texture "Link to this heading")
You can create mipmaps for a Render Target Texture to which you render 3D content with a Composition Target render pass. For example, use this to create a low-quality blur effect that is quick to render.
To create mipmaps for a Render Target Texture:
  1. In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs create a Render to Texture Pass.
Render to Texture Pass creates the render passes and texture you need to render to a texture.
See [Rendering to texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html#rendering-to-texture).
![../../_images/render-to-texture-pass.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-to-texture-pass.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select the Viewport 2D node the content of which you want to render to a texture and in the Properties set the Render Pass Prefab property to the Render to Texture Pass you created in the previous step.
Kanzi now renders the Viewport 2D using the render passes you created.
![../../_images/scene-render-pass-set-to-render-to-texture-pass.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/scene-render-pass-set-to-render-to-texture-pass.png)
  3. In the Library select the Render to Texture Pass that you created, in the Properties click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/go-to-selected-item.png) next to the Composition Target 0 property to go to the Render Target Texture resource, and set the Mipmap Mode property to either Linear or Nearest. See [Filtering textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/filtering-textures.html).
![../../_images/render-to-texture-pass-go-to-render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-to-texture-pass-go-to-render-target-texture.png) ![../../_images/render-target-texture-mipmap-mode.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-target-texture-mipmap-mode.png)
  4. Use the Render Target Texture in a node where you want to show the 3D content. See [Using render target textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-render-target-textures.html).

# Filtering textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/filtering-textures.html#filtering-textures "Link to this heading")

By applying texture filtering you can improve the image quality in 3D scenes with slight decrease in performance. The baseline point sampling requires storing the whole texture data into memory, whereas when you use mipmapping (or any of the filtering options), when the texture area is small, you can use a smaller sized version of the texture. See [Using mipmaps](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html).
Select the texture filtering option that best reflects the requirements of your application.
## Using texture filtering[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/filtering-textures.html#using-texture-filtering "Link to this heading")
To use texture filtering:
  1. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Textures select the texture to which you want to apply filtering.
Avoid creating mipmaps from .jpeg textures, because the .jpeg image format causes the quality of the mipmaps to degrade.
  2. In the Properties set the Texture Settings properties.
Use the Texture Settings properties to control the texture filtering. Start by setting the Mipmap Mode property to the mipmap mode you want to use. Then set the Minification Filter and Magnification Filter properties to Linear. Note that using mipmaps increases the memory use.
Usually the best starting point for setting texture filtering is to set:
     * Minification Filter to Linear
     * Magnification Filter to Linear
     * Mipmap Mode to Nearest. If you are sure that the texture is not minified select Base, otherwise start with Nearest. For example, the default value for a Render Target Texture is Base. With this setting, the texture does not have mipmap levels and the base level is always sampled. See [Using mipmaps](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html).
![../../_images/texture-settings-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-settings-properties.png)
Note that some texture formats are available with OpenGL ES versions higher than 2.0. To set the OpenGL ES version, in the main menu select Project > Properties and in the Properties set the Target Graphics API property.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/target-graphics-api-opengl-es-30.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-graphics-api-opengl-es-30.png)
For example, set the Target Graphics API property to OpenGL ES 3.0, import HDR and floating point images in .dds format, and set the color format of textures. See [Using OpenGL ES 3.0+ in Kanzi](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-opengl-es-30.html).  
| Mipmap Mode  | Nearest sample  | Linear sample  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Base  |  Number of samples: 1 Uses the nearest pixel in the texture. This combination is equal to point sample. It returns the crudest result of all combinations and can cause aliasing when minified. Use this combination to get a very sharp result when magnifying the texture.  |  Number of samples: 4 Interpolates between four nearest pixels in the texture. Use this combination to magnify gradients. However, do not use it for minification.  |  
| Nearest  |  Number of samples: 1 Helps texture caching and helps reduce aliasing. However, it can produce a sharp transition when the texture is used on a flat surface. Use this combination when you want good performance and cannot afford better quality on your target platform. This combination is usually the fastest.  |  Number of samples: 4 Takes two samples from two mipmap levels and interpolates between these samples. Use this combination as the starting point. This combination is usually the best compromise between quality and performance. If you know there is no minification, you can set Mipmap Mode to Base.  |  
| Linear  |  Number of samples: 2 Takes one sample from two mipmap levels and interpolates between those samples. Use this combination for special effects. For example, to implement the rim light effect.  |  Number of samples: 8 Takes four samples from two mipmap levels and interpolates between these samples. Use this combination when you want the best quality and your platform is powerful enough to effortlessly render the result. This combination has the largest negative impact on performance.  |
